author: Pip Hinman
title: NSW Labor to introduce law overriding High Court coal mine ruling
content:
The NSW Labor government will introduce a law to allow MACH Energy to expand output at its contested Mount Pleasant coal mine in the Upper Hunter region of NSW, in response to a High Court ruling that invalidated the expansion approval.

The High Court ruled on October 7 that the NSW Independent Planning Commission (IPC) failed to consider how pollution from its coal would affect the region. It also emphasised that the IPC must consider Scope 3 — downstream emissions from coal burned elsewhere, including overseas — as part of its approval process.

Denman Aberdeen Muswellbrook Scone Healthy Environment Group (DAMSHEG) first challenged the IPC’s approval in 2023 in the NSW Land and Environment Court. Following a protracted legal battle, DAMSHEG had its case upheld in the High Court.

Premier Chris Minns told the ABC on October 19 that he was moving to protect jobs that would be “on the line”. He said the new law would “guarantee” 400 direct jobs until 2032 — the deadline for the temporary extension MACH Energy sought and was given, even though the High Court was considering MACH Energy’s case against DAMSHEG.

The mining corporation wants a licence to mine thermal coal until 2048 — something Minns and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese support.

However, the 22-year extension of the coal mine would include no guarantee of 400 jobs. DAMSHEG’s Tony Lonergan said the mine relies on contractors who can be laid off at any time.

Wendy Wales, also from DAMSHEG, said she wants fossil fuel workers to be able to transition to alternative employment. “We have never wanted anyone in the Hunter to lose their livelihood.”

“A law written for one company, days after the High Court ruled against that company, is an inappropriate use of the NSW legislative process,” she said. “The laws should reflect a balance where the overall welfare of citizens and environment is paramount and industry serves the needs of all citizens.”

The NSW Minerals Council welcomed Labor’s move. Chief executive Stephen Galilee said: “The Mount Pleasant mine has endured four years of activist legal challenges, creating uncertainty for hundreds of mine workers, their families and local supplier businesses.”

Greens MLC Sue Higginson said NSW Labor is being “fed lies about the job numbers at Mount Pleasant” and “selling the integrity of the NSW planning and legal systems down the river”.

She said MACH Energy had threatened to sack 400 workers at Mount Pleasant mine unless Labor introduced this law. It has been revealed that new job advertisements were posted by MACH Energy shortly after Minns announced the special law allowing expanded coal mining.

“MACH Energy’s own documents show that the increased coal mining that will be allowed by Minns’ special laws would only create around 100 jobs, completely undermining its threat to fire 400 workers if they didn’t get their way,” Higginson said.

“This is state capture — a form of modern day corruption ... where billion dollar corporations are writing laws that benefit them, in defiance of the law as laid down by the High Court of Australia.”

Retired Supreme Court judge Anthony Whealy has called for an independent review of the Minns government’s decision to draft laws to circumvent the High Court ruling.

Whealy told the ABC on October 20 that the government’s decision is “reprehensible” because it “obliterates” the legal process.

“The idea that a substantial mining venture can approach the government and say, ‘Look, let’s go behind the court processes and sort this out between ourselves’ is a very dangerous precedent, and that’s exactly what appears to have happened here,” Whealy said.

“They’ve effectively ignored what I would call respect for the rule of law by overriding it.”

The Greens are supporting his call for an independent review.

Higginson said Labor has “decided to step over the independent planning process ... the High Court of Australia and they are trashing the rule of law”.

The ABC also reported on October 20 that MACH Energy is being investigated over allegations it breached its coal production limits, as it scaled up construction during the High Court appeal process.

Denman Aberdeen Muswellbrook Scone Healthy Environment Group

author: Kerry Smith
title: Hunter Jobs Alliance says new law on coal transition gives hope
content:
The Future Jobs and Investment Authority (FJIA) Bill 2025 passed both NSW houses on October 20.

According to the Hunter Jobs Alliance (HJA), it is a major achievement and testimony to the many organisations and individuals that have campaigned over five years to secure a better future for workers, communities and the environment across NSW’s four coal regions.

HJA started with publishing Building for the Future: A ‘Hunter Valley Authority’ to secure our region’s prosperity in June 2021, which made the case for a “dedicated regional authority to support workers, diversify our economy and secure the Hunter’s future beyond coal”.

Since then, it has worked to get NSW Labor to commit to establishing a Transition Authority in its policy platform before the March election next year.

It is seeking 10 amendments to strengthen the law, particularly workforce transition planning obligations for coal companies.

HJA singled out the Australian Manufacturing Workers’ Union for “critical political and strategic support in advancing the proposal”, as well as Hunter Renewal, which championed this reform long before HJA’s involvement.

It said the new law establishes a dedicated public authority, and funds to support economic diversification, attract new industries and create jobs across NSW’s four coal regions.

“Importantly, it will also require coal mine owners to develop workforce transition plans to support workers affected by mine closures. This represents a significant shift from the current system, where coal companies have had limited enforceable responsibilities to prepare workers and communities for closure.”

HJA said its next job is to ensure the regulations are “developed and finalised before the caretaker period” in the lead-up to the March election next year.

“These must establish meaningful minimum standards for workforce transition plans, including paid retraining, paid training leave, career and financial advice, and assistance securing new employment.”

HJA is also seeking at least $150 million each year for the Future Jobs and Investment Fund, up from the current $22.5 million a year. “Securing this as a budget commitment ahead of the March 2027 election will be a key focus.”

HJA said its member organisations and everyone who has contributed to this campaign “demonstrates what can be accomplished when unions, environmental organisations, community groups, business and industry work together towards a shared vision for the future of the Hunter and NSW’s other coal regions”.

Future Jobs and Investment Fund

author: Sue Bolton
title: Sue Bolton: ‘Put working-class communities first’
content:
Sue Bolton, a fourth-term Socialist Alliance councillor at the Merri-bek City Council, is running for Broadmeadows in the Victorian elections.

This article is based on a speech she gave to the launch of SA’s campaign. The party is fielding candidates in Broadmeadows and Pascoe Vale in Naarm/Melbourne, and in four seats covering Djilang/Geelong. It is also standing in the Northern Metropolitan and Western Region for the Legislative Council.

Socialist Alliance’s campaign slogan “Fighting for people, not the billionaires” encapsulates our view that fundamental change won’t come from elected representatives.

Our approach is to work with communities getting organised so that they can become really strong. We need members of parliament who will champion a politics that defends working-class communities against the billionaires.

The only way to guarantee that working-class communities’ rights are safeguarded is by electing socialists who are also committed community activists.

The campaign to stop the redevelopment of the toxic site in Fawkner in 2017 is a case in point. When this development came through Merri-bek City Council, I objected and together with the community we fought hard against it. It would have sailed through because the Environmental Protection Authority had already approved it.

Right now the far right — and the mainstream right — are trying to take back social and political rights that took fights to win.

The Victorian Labor Party, following the One Nation (ON) playbook, is attacking migrants. It has stopped talking about renewable energy and the need to transition away from fossil fuels. Even if ON doesn’t get an MP, its policy announcements are pushing the major parties to the right — a core part of the billionaires’ divide-and-rule plan.

Billionaire mining magnate Gina Rinehart is writing Pauline Hanson’s policies. She has other billionaire supporters, but they prefer to remain in the shadows.

If migration was to be stopped tomorrow, there would still be a housing crisis. This is because state and federal policies allow developers and speculators to game the system. The destruction of public housing is another part of the housing problem.

What is the billionaire’s agenda? Pay zero or little tax and privatise, or cut, public services — not the fat cats but the people providing the services.

Even repairing potholes on roads and motorways has become political, after a man tragically died after hitting a pothole on his motorbike. VicRoads used to do those repairs. Since it has been handed to the private sector, the roads have deteriorated.

Labor’s privatisation agenda of critical public assets includes the Port of Melbourne, part of VicRoads and the Land Titles office. It includes demolishing 44 high-rise public housing towers, shafting people out of their communities and affordable homes.

The disintegration of the community health sector is part of this. The introduction of the national disability insurance scheme (NDIS) forced the community health centres to move to a user-pays model.

But communities have also shown that they will resist. Because of the community revolt, Labor’s plan to axe GPs and other services at various CoHealth sites, including Collingwood and Fitzroy, have been saved — for the moment.

While Premier Ben Carroll has sought to distance himself from Jacinta Allan and Dan Andrews, he supports the public housing demolition. Labor should be pledging to renovate and keep the public housing towers, and replace the dwellings that have been demolished.

The billionaire class wants to stop workers gaining pay rises which keep up with inflation. It wants to remove regulations so private businesses, like the mega data centre AI industry, or developers eyeing off the toxic site in Fawkner, can do whatever they like.

It is possible after the next election that the Treaty process in Victoria could be ripped up. The Coalition has promised to do that and ON would like to. Sections of Labor are nervous about the kind of rights First Nations people would have with a Treaty or treaties.

For First Nations people, the process is about more than symbolism; it is a way of improving their lives, including access to culture and practice to build stronger communities. This is important. We need to ensure that the rights of First Nations people are enhanced. Only then will we have improved rights for everybody.

The premier’s big announcement around the Upfield rail line duplication came down to $80 million for a new study. And this only happened after ON raised the issue.

We don’t need another study; we know the duplication is feasible and its cost. Still Labor only has plans for the duplication ending in Upfield, not extending to Craigieburn, even though the land has been allocated.

I restarted the campaign for the Upfield line duplication after finding out about the extraordinary number of cancellations on the line because of the single track at the end of it. As soon as a train is six minutes late, it terminates at Coburg; everything north on the line is cancelled.

The petition campaign on the northern end of the line meant that we started to meet people who had lost jobs, missed an exam, been fined for picking up their children late from childcare, all because of the train terminations. Those in Campbellfield, where there is no train station, have to walk half an hour to get to one.

Apart from a rent freeze, rents also need to be cut. Thirty per cent of those living in Broadmeadows are renters. A proportion will be on fixed incomes, or on pensions. There are no affordable private rentals for anyone those on JobSeeker or Youth Allowance.

We should also support for those with mortgages. There should not be any bank foreclosures or forced sales. Governments are pitting renters against people who don’t really yet own their homes, but are paying off the bank.

The billionaire class wants to shift all the costs associated with protecting the environment and communities on to working-class people.

None of the mainstream parties want to make it easier for people to have a real say in policies that shape their lives.

Communities need to have that, not only because they have solutions, but they can often see that most of the parties standing for office are there to represent the big end of town, and thereby want to prevent people from planning society and the economy around what the community needs.

[Get in touch with Sue Bolton if you’d like to help Socialist Alliance out.]

author: Luca Tavan
title: Europe’s youth and workers in revolt
content:
The metaphor of a tinderbox is one of the most overused in politics. But how else could you describe the situation in Europe today, where every small spark of resistance seems to be catching and turning into a powerful blaze? 

Things kicked off in France in late September, when students in the working-class suburb of Créteil in the South-east of Paris blockaded their school in protest against poor conditions. This has since grown into the deepest challenge French President Emmanuel Macron has faced in his ten years in power. On October 17, students were joined by workers in a national mobilisation of 800,000. Strikes, demonstrations, blockades and riots have all played a role in this movement. It’s not just the radical left comparing this situation to the legendary student and worker uprising of May 1968.

In Spain, anger at the eviction of María del Carmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman whose rent was raised 230 percent when her apartment was acquired by an investment firm, has generated a massive movement for housing justice. The streets have forced the centre-left Sanchez government to call early elections, and typically hesitant union leaders to schedule a general strike for November 11. 

Protests have rocked Albania since May, in response to an environmentally catastrophic luxury resort development tied to the Trump family. On October 13, youth inspired by the French protests brought their own demands over education and wages into the mix, turning the movement into a national uprising. Government buildings have been invaded and burnt, and the call for the downfall of Edi Rama’s government is widespread. It is the country’s largest revolt since the fall of Stalinist regime in the early 1990s.  

In Italy, mass protests pledging to “fare come in Francia” (to do as in France) last weekend turned into standoffs against the police. In Milan, 250 people were detained, more than 80 percent of whom were minors. Belgium, Portugal, and Ireland have seen mass protests and strikes taking aim at austerity and intolerable working conditions. 

This marks the biggest wave of protests on the continent in at least a generation. Anyone who wants to see capitalism one day toppled and replaced with a system really fit for human beings should take great hope from these events. 

There’s no telling how long these struggles will continue, whether they will lose momentum, or if massive state repression will succeed in intimidating many off the streets. But this convergence of different struggles provides a glimpse of the possibility of rebuilding class-based politics after a decade characterised by despair and far right ascendancy. 

The roots of the revolt 

While these different movements are profoundly shaped by their specific national contexts, they have common roots in decades of battered living standards and attacks on workers. An entire generation suffered the consequences of the 2008 economic crisis - wages were slashed, young people were left without the prospect of ever finding a job, and social services were gutted to bail out the banks. 

Italy provides perhaps the sharpest example of the consequences of this class war waged by the rich: according to data from Italy's Parliamentary Budget Office, private sector workers have seen their real wages fall by 6.6 percent between 1990 and 2026. 

In countries experiencing economic recovery, young people are learning that they bear the costs of boom as well as bust. New jobs created are insecure, and wage increases are offset by soaring housing costs. 

This long, bitter experience has brought questions of social class back to the fore and changed the character of struggle. A comparison of the current occupation of Madrid’s Puerta del Sol with the last one is instructive. 2011’s 

Indignados

movement shared many characteristics with the protests of today, fuelled by anger at low wages, evictions and the callousness of the political class. It was an inspiring and important moment for the left. But the politics of the movement were organically populist, seeking to build a cross-class alliance of Spanish ‘citizens’ against the political caste they blamed for the country’s ruin. The most popular slogans reflected this - like “real democracy now!” and “they don’t represent us”. 

This sentiment was also expressed in a hostility to the organised left and workers’ movement within the occupation - seen by many participants as just another facet of the “politics” they felt alienated from. Unions and left parties were even banned by the movement from participating in its marches. This tragically misguided decision put real limits on the extent to which the struggle could deepen and spread from the square to the workplaces. 

Today, the movement is consciously associated with the traditions of the left and working-class struggle. One of the most popular slogans is “Long live the struggle of the working class,”, and visitors to the occupation in Puerta del Sol are greeted with the banners of the radical left, from the anarchist CNT to the Coordinadora Juvenil Socialista (Socialist Youth). They can even take a walk down a thoroughfare protesters have named the “Paseo de Rosa Luxemburg.” 

It’s also not surprising that youth in general, and students in particular, have been the leavening agent and the detonator of so many of these struggles. Young people have been the motor behind every great movement of historical change over the history of capitalism.

Today, the lives of a new generation are being shaped by an alarming new political context - characterised not just by class attacks, but also by the reorganisation of world capitalism around rising war and authoritarianism. 

That militarism and austerity are just two sides of the same coin is clear to student protesters in France: the government is attempting to pass €54 billion in social spending cuts, while boasting that they are ahead of schedule with plans to double military spending. German students resisting the potential reintroduction of conscription have made the same connection, with chants like “The rich want war, the youth want a future” and “Our only war is the class war”. 

Ruling-class hypocrites sermonise about violence 

Much of the domestic response to these movements and international commentary has focused on rioting and alleged “violence” of some demonstrators. In a televised address over the weekend, Emmanuel Macron criticised what he called ‘unbridled violence’, asking “how could French people do this to France?”

But much of this ‘violence’ is a response to brutal state repression, a fact which warrants little attention in mainstream media coverage. In France, riots were provoked by outrageous police tactics. One 

eyewitness

 account describes: “officers patrolled in groups of four or five mopeds, each carrying a pair of armed officers. One officer stands ready to jump off, beat protesters indiscriminately and speed away before anyone can retaliate.”

The denunciation of violence is particularly ironic from the French president. Macron currently enjoys a narrower social base than many dictatorships (a recent Ipsos BVA-Cesi survey found that 82 percent disapproved of his performance) and has only been able to hold on to power through the routine and systematic use of violence. In the current wave of protests, one student has lost a hand, one an arm, another an eye. 

There has also been much establishment consternation about property damage, particularly after the burning of the historic town hall in the French town of Limonge. Karl

 

Marx wrote on this theme 150 years ago, as troops moved in to crush the Paris Commune, murdering thousands of workers: “The bourgeoisie of the whole world, which looks complacently upon the wholesale massacre after the battle, is convulsed by horror at the desecration of brick and mortar!” 

Those who rule over a system based on such brutal violence are in no position to remonstrate about the rights of buildings. 

If many of the participants in these movements are willing to defend a variety of forms of resistance, from the strike to the blockade to the riot, it’s because of an inevitable impatience that comes from learning how far you get when you go through the “proper channels.”  Anjeza Marku, an Albanian student, told the Austrian newspaper 

Der Standard

: L

“We protested peacefully for 135 days, but those in power merely insulted the participants. The public sees the youth as Albania’s last hope—we have often even been compared to the youth in France. But the government couldn’t care less whether we protest peacefully. It won’t listen to our voices anyway”.

Repression and racism 

The establishment's focus on the supposed violence of these movements has two aims. First, to criminalise resistance, and second, for a wing of the ruling class, to racialise it in public consciousness. 

The response of Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s far-right government is typical. It has sent 500 additional troops to Milan and rushed through a new “security decree” further penalising protests and allowing for 

preventive detention of minors

. 

At the same time, the government and their right-wing backers in the media have made a concerted attempt to blame the unrest on “maranza, a racist slur for groups of North African youth in working class suburbs. Deputy Premier Matteo Salvini complained the squares were filled with “maranza and rotten left-wing riff-raff.” and has threatened to strip Italian-born migrants who riot of their citizenship rights. Businessman and current Defence Minister Guido Crosetto has accused youth of waging a ‘hybrid war’ against Italian society. 

The reason migrant youth have had a prominent place in the demonstrations is obvious. Working-class migrants have to suffer the double blow of economic exploitation and racist humiliation. Moroccan youth who faced down heavily armed police in Bologna last weekend weren’t doing so for the first time. In July, the city saw its own “George Floyd'” moment, when protests erupted after police killed Abderrahim Fakir, a Moroccan migrant suffering a psychiatric episode. Migrants living in Fakir’s neighbourhood of Pilastro are used to being targeted. During 2020 regional elections, Matteo Salvini performed a stunt in the area where he rang the bell of a Tunisian family’s home to ask them over the intercom if they were drug dealers. No wonder that when resistance breaks out, people who are so beaten and repressed rush to the front lines. 

This racialised authoritarian response is being carried by the far right from Europe across the world. Trump addressed a Kansas rally on Tuesday to denounce the movement and describe France as a country “conquered, looted, and burned to the ground by migrants, jihadists and communists.” Here in Australia, Pauline Hanson has warned: “Unless Australia stops importing people who reject our democracy, our way of life … these riots will eventually be coming to Australian cities”. Sky News has attempted to draw the link between the European revolt and sinister forces at home, with segments like: “Pro-Palestine rioters ‘energised’ by anti-West sentiments.” The right-wing press has hysterically denounced an upcoming student strike against Hanson on November 11, accusing the high-schoolers of planning a “France-style riot.” 

The sharp divergence of responses to this wave of revolt, described either as the great hope for a more just world or a terrifying plot to Islamicise the west, reflects the depth of the political polarisation that has been produced. But it also reflects the asymmetry of that polarisation, one in which the far right is several orders of magnitude stronger than the left and has had its conspiratorial and fascistic worldview embraced as a permanent and legitimate wing of capitalist politics. The radicalisation on the right continues to build. In Italy where Meloni’s far-right coalition is losing its lustre, it now faces a challenge in the form of the hardline fascist Futuro Nazionale, led by retired army general Roberto Vanacci.

Challenges for the left 

These hopeful struggles in Europe have emerged in a pretty bleak period. The ascendancy of the far right and multiplying horrors of capitalism are felt especially by people on the left who are aware of the long-term challenges for our side. Decades of defeat, demoralisation and working-class disorganisation have had a profound impact on the politics of the left. One reflection of this has been the tendency for socialists to lower their horizons and adapt to the politics of the centre-left, accepting Spain’s Pedro Sanchez or Brazil’s Lula da Silva as the height of their ambition. 

Another expression of this demoralisation is the retreat in some left-wing circles into doomerism and crisis-mongering, emphasising the potentially apocalyptic direction of world capitalism without an argument about how the forces to resist it could be built.

These struggles show another possibility. They are a vindication of Marxism’s central claim: that the functioning of capitalism contains within it potentially explosive contradictions, which can rapidly burst onto the scene. The capitalist system can never come good on its promises of a good life for the majority. And the potential power of the masses of people that have no real stake in this rotten order can be obscured and repressed, but it can never be eradicated. 

People are driven to act again and again. This is the only thing that can open up the possibility not just winning immediate gains but also creating ideological fissures which can lead to a break with the dominant order. Lenin reflected on this basic point after the failed revolution of 1905:

“Only struggle educates the exploited class. Only struggle discloses to it the magnitude of its own power, widens its horizon, enhances its abilities, clarifies its mind, forges its will.”

But it’s not enough to champion resistance. The challenge for socialists is not only to act as participants, but to try to give shape and direction to it and argue for a way forward. There will be many obstacles on the road to deepening these struggles, including opportunistic capitalist politicians who want to ride these movements into power, as in Albania, and conservative union leaders who only want strikes according to a neatly planned timetable, as in Spain and France.  

The last great wave of European revolt in 2011 generated exciting new possibilities. But ultimately the political forces it generated led things to disaster. In Spain, the populist party Podemos channelled resistance in a parliamentary direction and ultimately ended up in coalition with the centre-left they pledged to replace. In Greece, a party that emerged as a coalition of the radical left ended up forming a government, only to rapidly capitulate to the financial pressure of the ruling class and become as bad as the centre parties they had denounced.  

But despite the weight of so many crushing defeats, a new generation is standing up and grasping toward radical solutions to the radical problems posed by capitalism. The challenge for socialists is to grab hold of this opportunity and begin building the forces for revolution in the 21st century.

author: Unknown
title: Martin H. - Barry Pateman: An Appreciation
content:
Author

: Martin H.

Title

: Barry Pateman: An Appreciation

Date

: 2026-10-21

Notes

: [First posted on the Kate Sharpley Library website]

Source

: https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/c2ft1b




 It’s important to appreciate those who have come before us. I first met Barry through Albert Meltzer, probably at a bookfair. I’d learned to trust that if Albert thought well of someone, he was probably right. Barry was an impressive man, physically and mentally, with the sort of self-deprecating humour instantly recognisable to anyone brought up in a British working class environment. And he was able to talk to people, without the sort of academic language that can be so off-putting. 




 The times I saw him were few and far between but they were always memorable. Barry was brimming with ideas, whether about anarchist history, theory and practice, sport or wider culture. Like Albert he had a high regard for the autodidacts – especially those miner militants whose self-education far outstripped those who had had a university education. He was good company. 




 It was perhaps telling that I learned of Barry’s death a few days after returning from Ron Marsden’s funeral. Both had been intimately involved in the tension between organising as anarchists and remaining accessible to ordinary people. It’s a tension that runs through most of the anarchist organising and groups that I have been part of in my life, and one I kept promising Barry I would write something about – the organisations that can never get above Dunbar’s number

[1]

 in membership without splitting, the affinity groups claiming to be membership organisations, the strategies designed for different times, the insights from Stuart Christie’s autobiography about affinity groups. Sorry, mate, life always seemed to get in the way, I am way too easily distracted…. 




 He was generous with his time and his thoughts. He had many strings to his bow – as you would expect from someone who admired those self-educated working class militants – as was so warmly described by the guy who knew him from the New Zealand Cricket Museum at the memorial service. 




 Barry would regularly talk about how militant young miners from South Yorkshire were interested in the Direct Action Movement, during the height of the 1984–5 strike. But as they weren’t fully formed anarchists, DAM couldn’t accept them, despite their hard won experience of class struggle. It was this discussion that led DAM to become the Solidarity Federation (alongside other struggles like the Ardbride dispute 1986–87). Unfortunately, with a fabulous sense of timing, SF’s orientation towards labour movement militants happened at exactly the time the pool of labour movement militants shrank, following the catastrophic defeats of the 80s and early 90s. Barry saw the effects of these defeats first hand, as the mutual aid of the strike gave way to desperation and the destruction of former mining areas by a vengeful government. There were successes, most notably the Workmates group on the privatised part of the Tube, but that also swerved the same organisational question by staying independent – it wasn’t part of SF and as far as I know no one outside the originators ever joined SF. The arguments around SF’s industrial strategy, of building trust and organisation in a workplace and then tackling issues from that base are not new

[2]

 – but the obstacles to winning over new people to an anarcho-syndicalist project through this activity remain substantial. 




 One of the commitments of the KSL has always been to uncover the motivations and actions of the unknown militants, who didn’t leave piles of writings for posterity. Barry was assertive that we hear the true voices of our forebears, not mediated by what we think now and what we want to bolster our own current views. We are much richer for that approach. The histories published by KSL are accessible to the general reader. The context is there. The achievements are many: Recognising the importance of Guillamon’s work on the Spanish revolution and ending the myth of the spontaneous uprising in 1936, achieved without any groundwork. And his work on the early 20

th

 century movement and Emma Goldman stands out. 




 He kept looking for ways to spread the ideas of anarchism, and always in an outward-facing way. Whether through solidarity with strikers and others in struggle, through engaging with younger anarchists, or through the achievements of the Kate Sharpley Library he was always ready to share his experiences and knowledge and improve our understanding. To be an anarchist is hard, there’s a lot to live up to, and it’s important to understand the ways in which we all contribute. Barry was a standard bearer for a rigorous approach to anarchist history and we owe him a lot for that. 




 I remember parroting one of the myths about Emma Goldman, that somehow her militancy declined as she grew older – Barry soon corrected me – “she was militant to the end”. 




 And so was he. 




Footnotes




[1]

 Dunbar’s number comes from anthropologist and evolutionary biologist Robin Dunbar and is a suggested cognitive limit to the number of people with whom one can maintain stable social relationships. It’s normally taken to be about 150. 




...

author: Dougal McNeill
title: Striking for Palestine in Aotearoa
content:
Thousands of workers at universities and polytechnics (TAFEs) across Aotearoa (New Zealand) went on strike Wednesday 21 October, rallying against poor pay offers and the increasing precarity of employment in tertiary education. This was exciting enough on its own terms. The last time we went on strike, in 2022, it was the first in decades, and felt like something new. Now tertiary workers join teachers, public servants, health workers and others who have taken action over the last two years.

Our right-wing coalition government has attacked many of our rights but, in the fightback against their assault on everything from Te Tiriti o Waitangi (the country’s founding treaty with Indigenous groups) to pay equity, we’ve seen that the long drought around industrial action in these islands has been broken by welcome and nourishing rain.

Each bargaining campaign has different priorities and, at Te Herenga Waka in Wellington, my university, one part of our campaign stands out. We went on strike for Palestine. University Workers for Palestine, a campaign group bringing together staff across the country, emerged from the anti-genocide protests since 2023 to make concrete demands of institutions here. One focus is university superannuation schemes and their investments, including in weapons companies and others connected to Israel’s ongoing war against the Palestinians. A core part of our demands, then, is for the superannuation scheme to divest from the genocide.

We are striking for the “Three Ps”: pay, precarity and Palestine. The last of those got the loudest cheers at the strike rally yesterday, and there were signs from “Librarians for Palestine” to staff committing “from the river to the sea” that Palestine will be free. Unionised workers here have shown that our action for everyday pay and conditions can be linked to a wider vision of justice and liberation.

It’s a small start, but an exciting one, and another sign that the protest moment of 2023 has, over the years, become a long-term movement for Palestinian freedom.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Sara’s impunity killed her case
content:
Can Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio still refuse to testify in her defense as the deluge of evidence requires her to take the witness and debunk what she insists are fabricated documents that prove her amassing enormous wealth even before she got married? Press releases do not win impeachment cases and not even the pompous statements of Malou Tiquia or the strained legal *legerdemain of Michael Wesley Poa could dent the facticity of the evidence laid down in open court.




The brutal truth is that her 16-member defense panel cannot act as her surrogate since not one of them is competent to answer the questions posed by the prosecution. They are lawyers but not one of them can claim that signatures were forged, or that bank accounts were opened in her name but without her knowledge. Only Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio can answer the prosecution’s queries. Legal doppelgangers are prohibited.




If Sara were the only competent witness to disprove or affirm the validity of bank accounts, manager’s checks, credit memos and other records, why can’t she be woman enough to take the cudgels for her own self and declare before the whole world that she is being persecuted and slapped with manufactured charges? The fact is, Sara always enjoyed Duterte’s impunity and practiced it, and no matter how many times the Commission on Audit (COA) questioned her disbursements as Davao City mayor, she made mincemeat of all of them.




Her playbook is copycat from Donald Trump, who learned it from Roy Cohn: Deny everything, do not pay, deflect and project all the crimes to the accusers and refuse to apologize. For all his mentoring of Trump, what Cohn got was a pair of “diamond” cuff links that turned out to be worthless **yags, or imitation diamond. Cohn died a lonely death, disbarred and forgotten, from the scourge of humanity called AIDS. Are we hearing that the 16 defense lawyers are not getting paid? Not yet, but with the impeachment case now down to Article II on ill-gotten wealth, maybe a discount is in order.




Sara is a businesswoman who even tried to do some catering for her own people in the course of the trial, charged to the Senate. A deadbeat VP? Not an impossibility. She can do a Trump, a confirmed grifter who never paid 3,500 contractors and forced them to file cases and get swamped with legal fees. She is indolent, which explains why she delegated the disbursements of her confidential funds to non-bonded military officers in violation of COA regulations. By doing so, she betrayed public trust and punished with double impeachment cases.




DepEd officials also confirmed that Sara was known better for being absent from the job and her rudderless leadership at the DepEd. And in the few times she ever visited schools, she had a dispute with walls decorated with educational materials, promoting the doctrine of high tech education. Sweden just threw away gadgets from classroom, and pupils will now have to work with paper and pencils, not tablets and laptops. That’s the culture of learning giving the prophets of high tech a whack on the chin.




Sara will not testify. Not because she is ***faineant, or work-shy, or indolent, or even a ham of an actress. Being asked questions by people she regards as her inferiors is beneath her dignity. During the congressional investigation, she even wanted former Rep. Stella Quimbo to be sacked as panel member, accused former ACT Teachers Rep. France Castro of being a convicted criminal and slammed others for persecuting her to thwart her march to Malacanang accompanied by the Richard Wagner’s “Ride of the Valkyries.”




By not testifying, she, in ham-fisted fashion, will simply rely on a forensic analyst to “destroy” the contention of Atty. Alex Cabrera about Sara’s conservatively estimated P818-million ill-gotten wealth from 2022 to 2025. Some of those approached to do the job purportedly rejected the overtures. Her hubris, her firm belief that she is above the law and destined to be president of this country through her corruption, sloth and ignorance should eventually convict her. To be honest, 

binitbit lang siya ng tatay niya ngunit naniwalang kaya niyang maging pangulo. Mahirap mangarap nang gising kahit practitioner ka ng

 impunity. #




= = = = =




WORDS OF THE DAY




Legerdemain

 (French) – sleight of hand, manual dexterity, or clever trickery used to deceive people.




Yag

 (yttrium aluminum garnet) – a synthetic crystal used in solid-state lasers and medical devices, or an acronym in tech and gaming slang. 




Fainéant

 (French/English) – idle, indolent, or ineffectual.

Sara’s impunity killed her case

Kodao Productions

author: Marcelo Oliveira
title: Ministério Público encurrala Meta para barrar bloqueios e restrições nas eleições
content:
Em dois movimentos distintos, um judicial e outro extrajudicial, 

o Ministério Público Federal (MPF) quer barrar bloqueios, suspensões de contas e restrições de alcance promovidos pela Meta no Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp e Threads.




Na Justiça Federal do Rio Grande do Sul, o MPF ajuizou nesta quarta-feira, 21 de outubro, uma ação civil pública, com pedido de urgência. Em outra frente, a Procuradoria Federal dos Direitos do Cidadão (PFDC) enviou recomendação à Meta, cobrando providências imediatas.




A ação lida especificamente com as denúncias que fazem parte da representação feita pelas organizações Ctrl+Z, Artigo 19, Conectas e Sleeping Giants Brasil, que mostram que a Meta bloqueou conteúdos políticos pró-Lula e contra Flávio. A 

Agência Pública

 

mostrou

 que além dos bloqueios, 

a plataforma derrubou perfis com acusação de terrorismo e nudez, mesmo não havendo conteúdos nesse sentido.

 A Procuradoria pede o restabelecimento imediato de contas, páginas e conteúdos afetados pelas restrições apontadas na representação.




A ação pede ainda que a Justiça Federal proíba o uso exclusivo de algoritmos para decisões de bloqueio de conteúdo e que as futuras reavaliações e análises de recursos sejam conduzidas obrigatoriamente por equipes humanas especializadas

, com a fixação de multa diária de R$ 500 mil por conta afetada, em caso de descumprimento.




O MPF apurou que as restrições arbitrárias impostas pela companhia foram operadas por meio de algoritmos automatizados, sem notificação clara sobre as supostas violações ou oportunidade de contestação por canal efetivo com revisão humana. Essa prática provocou o enfraquecimento do engajamento de conteúdos cívicos e o cerceamento do debate democrático.




Ao público, no dia 16, a Meta 

reconheceu

 que “a conta de anúncios da campanha de Lula foi desativada por engano por pouco mais de 1 hora”, mas afirmou que não se tratou de “razões políticas”.




Após pedir para ‘Flávio abrir o sigilo’, dona de comunidade é bloqueada pela Meta




Uma das vítimas das restrições foi a arquiteta Carolina Martins, 43, de Brasília. Ela criou um grupo e uma comunidade visando angariar apoio para a candidatura de Lula no segundo turno. O grupo chegou a ser derrubado, acusado de “terrorismo” sem fundamentação pela empresa. Ela teve a conta de WhatsApp derrubada e ainda está sofrendo outras restrições da Meta.




Ao divulgar esta semana a proposta do presidente Lula para que ambos os candidatos abram seu sigilo bancário, feita após o 

debate

 da rede Bandeirantes, 

Martins postou uma imagem que dizia “Flavio Abra o Sigilo”. Na segunda-feira, dia 19, ela foi suspensa pela Meta de postar links em suas publicações no Instagram até 16 de novembro sob a acusação de “práticas comerciais proibidas”.













Recomendação quer resposta da Meta em 48 horas




Já a recomendação, que é uma medida extrajudicial para uma empresa ou ente público realizar medidas para corrigir uma ilegalidade, foi expedida pela Procuradoria Federal dos Direitos do Cidadão, em Brasília, e direcionada diretamente à Meta para que a companhia adote medidas urgentes de transparência e proteção à liberdade de expressão nas redes Facebook, Instagram, Threads e WhatsApp durante o período eleitoral.




À empresa foi dado prazo de 48 horas para responder se acatará as recomendações do MPF e para detalhar as providências que serão adotadas durante o segundo turno das eleições, além de 30 dias para apresentar um relatório conclusivo.




A medida da PFDC vem depois da instauração de investigação no último dia 13 na qual o MPF pediu à Meta uma série de informações. A companhia enviou uma resposta ao MPF no dia 19 de outubro, complementada ontem, 20. 




Nas respostas, segundo a PFDC, a Meta teria alegado, em síntese, que a sua moderação se basearia nos Padrões da Comunidade e na legislação local, que não levaria em conta a orientação política ou ideológica dos usuários.




As respostas foram consideradas genéricas pelo MPF e não abordaram as moderações indevidas e não esclareceram caso a caso no que se baseou cada restrição, conforme demandado no ofício da semana passada.




A manifestação da Meta não mencionou as suspensões fundadas em enquadramentos graves (como terrorismo e abuso sexual), nem das remoções que teriam ocorrido após denúncias em massa. A recomendação à Meta é assinada pelo Procurador Federal dos Direitos do Cidadão, Paulo Thadeu Gomes da Silva, e mais cinco procuradores do MPF que atuam na área de direitos humanos.

title: Bet Blaze funcionou em endereço de empresas ligadas a Willer Tomaz, investigado pela PF
content:
Um relatório de análise da nuvem associada ao celular do advogado Willer Tomaz de Souza, produzido pela Polícia Federal (PF), revela que a Foggo Entertainment Ltda, empresa responsável pelas operações da plataforma de apostas Blaze no Brasil, utilizou o mesmo endereço comercial que já havia sido registrado anteriormente por empresas ligadas a Willer Tomaz e a seus ex-sócios. Tomaz ganhou manchetes de todo o país em agosto devido a seu processo contra a própria Blaze, tentando reaver R$ 163 milhões que teria apostado na plataforma, o que chamou a atenção da PF e do Ministério da Fazenda por suspeita de lavagem de dinheiro.




O imóvel localizado na Alameda Prudente de Moraes, nº 86, no bairro Mercês em Curitiba, consta nos registros cadastrais da Foggo Entertainment — CNPJ que recebeu transferências milionárias enviadas por Willer — e já havia sido sede da RioPag S/A, processadora de pagamentos de apostas da Loterj, além de outras sociedades vinculadas a um ex-sócio de Willer.




A análise do iCloud do aparelho celular e Willer Tomaz foi possível a partir de quebra de sigilo autorizada pela Justiça após operação de busca e apreensão contra o advogado e empresário no âmbito da 

operação Sem Desconto, que investiga as fraudes no INSS

. A apuração da PF aponta que o advogado realizou diversas transferências bancárias fracionadas e sistemáticas de R$ 100 mil para a conta da Foggo Entertainment. Ao rastrear a estrutura societária e operacional da empresa de apostas, os investigadores identificaram a sobreposição de endereços entre a operadora da Blaze e a Riopag S.A.




Para os investigadores, a coincidência de endereços “reduz a força de uma leitura puramente casual e justifica aprofundar a investigação sobre eventuais vínculos societários, comerciais ou operacionais entre o investigado, antigos parceiros e a estrutura responsável pela atividade de apostas”.




Uma das suspeitas da PF é que a plataforma de apostas não fosse utilizada apenas para apostas recreativas, mas como meio de circulação intensiva, pulverização do dinheiro e eventual retorno de capital. A análise dos extratos de Willer Tomaz revelou movimentações diárias na plataforma que chegaram a superar R$ 35 milhões em dias específicos, acumulando registros contábeis de perdas na ordem de R$ 40,83 milhões entre junho e outubro de 2025.




Com o cruzamento do endereço em Curitiba e a identificação de saques em cassinos no exterior, as autoridades buscam determinar se as perdas registradas na conta de apostas eram efetivas ou se retornavam ao patrimônio do grupo por meio de estruturas empresariais interpostas.



















Dinheiro que circula em várias etapas/empresas




Até o momento, o “

amigo advogado

” de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) tem negado ser sócio ou acionista de várias empresas, inclusive as ligadas à operação de bets que funcionavam legalmente no estado do Rio de Janeiro até a primeira semana de outubro. No entanto, um email extraído do iCloud do aparelho celular do empresário, enviado pelo próprio Willer Tomaz para a instituição Magnum Bank, indicam, segundo a PF, “o controle ou vínculo de fato” de Tomaz sobre uma longa lista de empreendimentos, incluindo a RioPag S/A, que opera o meio de pagamento de prêmios da Loterj desde 2023.




Na mensagem em questão, Willer “declara ser sócio ou acionista” de uma lista de companhias, incluindo Rio Pag S/A e Embrasis. “Inclusive daquelas em que seu nome não consta formalmente do quadro societário”, escreve a PF.




Materiais obtidos pela 

Agência Pública

 e o relatório da PF ajudam a desenhar a estrutura entre as companhias ligadas à RioPag até chegar a Tomaz, um arranjo que envolve empresas atualmente registradas no Distrito Federal e no Rio de Janeiro.








































Certidões emitidas pelas Juntas Comerciais do Distrito Federal e do Rio de Janeiro mostram que a RioPag tem uma única acionista, uma empresa atualmente chamada Capital Pretium S/A (antes chamada de Pixs Holding SA). Por sua vez, a Capital Pretium também possui apenas uma sócia, a Empresa Brasileira de Sistemas de Computação (Embrasis S/A). Até 6 de outubro de 2026, quando houve alteração de diretoria e do estatuto social da empresa, os dois únicos acionistas da Embrasis S/A eram Willer Tomaz (82,5%) e sua irmã, Christine Tomaz de Souza (17,5%).




Oficialmente, o advogado amigo de Flávio Bolsonaro não exerceu papel de gestão ou direção em nenhuma delas. A PF conseguiu estimar o fluxo financeiro entre a teia de empresas até que o dinheiro chegasse a Willer Tomaz. Segundo a investigação, a RioPag repassava aproximadamente 15% de seus recursos à atual Capital Pretium. A Pretium passava à Embrasis cerca de 90%, enquanto a Embrasis, dos irmãos Christine e Willer Tomaz, fazia o repasse “quase integral”, segundo a PF, de seus volumes financeiros.




Segundo relatórios mensais apresentados pela RioPag ao governo do Rio de Janeiro obtidos pela 

Pública

, entre março de 2024 (quando assumiu o controle da operação) e agosto de 2026, a RioPag registrou mais de R$ 185 milhões em receitas. O valor dizia respeito a serviços como o pagamento de prêmios de produtos lotéricos, de bilhetes de ‘raspadinha’ a apostas esportivas (

bets

). A PF identificou ainda que Willer teria recebido ao menos R$ 67,7 milhões da Embrasis ao longo de 2024, conforme declaração de Imposto de Renda Pessoa Física reproduzida no relatório da operação.




Para SPA, Blaze não cumpriu requisitos para o combate à lavagem de dinheiro




Willer Tomaz de Souza foi a pessoa com o “maior volume total de depósitos” em bets no país em 2025, segundo uma nota técnica assinada em 1º de outubro de 2026 pelo subsecretário de Monitoramento e Fiscalização da Secretaria de Prêmios e Apostas (SPA) do Ministério da Fazenda. Ainda assim, WTS, como é citado no documento, teria sido enquadrado pela Blaze como um cliente de risco “médio” ao invés de risco “crítico”. O exemplo é utilizado para ilustrar uma série de “indícios de infrações administrativas” por parte da bet – entre as quais constam “ausência de seleção e análise de operações suspeitas” de lavagem de dinheiro.




“Uma rápida pesquisa em fontes abertas na internet mostra que o cliente já esteve detido sob suspeita de corrupção”, aponta a pasta, que alega que Willer Tomaz deveria ter sido avaliado como um cliente de risco “crítico” para que fossem tomadas “medidas especiais importantes” como “comunicações ao Coaf” em relação às movimentações do advogado.




Segundo a nota técnica, o amigo de Flávio Bolsonaro “girou cerca de R$ 5 bilhões em apostas no período, e somou quase R$ 200 milhões acumulados em saques” na Blaze somente naquele ano. Para a SPA, tais valores “deveriam ao menos haver passado por seleção e análise, ainda que a análise concluísse pela ausência de indícios” de lavagem de dinheiro.




Para a Fazenda, “operações do mesmo cliente [Willer] também chamam a atenção” pelo volume de dinheiro movimentado, pela frequência da movimentação e também pela multiplicidade de operações simultâneas. De acordo com a nota técnica assinada pelo subsecretário Carlos Renato Xavier de Resende, as operações poderiam ser enquadradas em práticas proibidas pela legislação que regulamentou a atividade das bets no país – tais como “possível uso de ferramenta automatizada” e “depósitos ou saques em curto espaço de tempo, sugerindo fracionamento ou dissimulação”.










 




Houve diversas situações em que múltiplos depósitos ou saques ocorreram num curtíssimo espaço de tempo, como, por exemplo, um mesmo dia (30/10/2025) em que foram realizados cinco depósitos de R$ 500 mil em uma mesma hora da manhã, outros cinco do mesmo valor em uma mesma hora da tarde, e outros quatro do mesmo valor em uma mesma hora da noite, totalizando R$ 7 milhões em depósitos em um único dia”, segundo a SPA. A pasta aponta ainda que, no dia seguinte, houve “doze saques de R$ 500 mil realizados em um espaço de 18 minutos”




somando R$ 6 milhões.

 










A nota técnica destaca ainda que a Blaze “falhou em evidenciar uma devida avaliação do perfil econômico desse cliente [Willer Tomaz]” e que “a observação do extrato de operações dele (em especial os vários depósitos e saques em períodos curtíssimos descritos anteriormente) levantam a possibilidade – sujeita a análise, naturalmente – de operações estruturadas (aquelas em que as movimentações financeiras são divididas em várias partes menores, visando-se a não disparar gatilhos de alerta e/ou chamar a atenção dos responsáveis pelo monitoramento, fiscalização ou persecução criminal)”.




Para basear seus argumentos, a SPA afirma que a Blaze comunicou ao Coaf a existência de apenas sete operações suspeitas na plataforma em 2025 e outras nove em 2026, e nenhuma delas envolvia valores acima de R$ 15 mil.




“Chama a atenção o fato de uma empresa identificar, selecionar, analisar e comunicar ao Coaf atividade atípica em operações de valores comparativamente irrisórios, enquanto a atividade de um cliente que fez 629 apostas individuais de valor igual ou superior a R$ 500 mil (cada uma) ao longo de um ano (sendo quatro delas de R$ 1 milhão, e 394 delas de exatos R$ 500 mil) – o cliente sobre cuja atividade se discorreu anteriormente – sequer tenha sido objeto de análise pela mesma empresa”, segundo a nota técnica da Fazenda.




Procurado pela 

Pública

, a assessoria de imprensa de Willer Tomaz informa que “todos os pontos levantados repetem informações já divulgadas e reiteradamente esclarecidas nas últimas semanas”: “Requentá-los às vésperas do segundo turno, a partir de dados sigilosos vazados, tem o evidente propósito de interferir no processo eleitoral. O advogado Willer Tomaz não cometeu nenhuma irregularidade. Nunca dividiu conta bancária com o senador Flávio Bolsonaro, tema que já motivou queixa-crime por difamação; as viagens foram convites entre famílias, sem contrapartida; e as questões de natureza pessoal estão sob análise dos tribunais.”




Procurada, a operadora da Blaze no Brasil, a Foggo Entertinment, ainda não respondeu aos questionamentos da 

Pública.

 Anteriormente neste mês, ao 

UOL

, a empresa informou que nunca manteve relação societária com Willer Tomaz, Edson Antônio Lenzi Filho ou empresas a eles vinculadas e que nenhum deles teria participação, direta ou indireta, no capital ou controle da companhia. Assim que houver manifestação oficial sobre o assunto à reportagem, este espaço será atualizado.







Flávio Bolsonaro e a conta de holding




Ainda no âmbito da operação Sem Desconto, a PF mapeou uma rede de relações operacionais, financeiras e pessoais entre o presidenciável Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o advogado Willer Tomaz. Os apontamentos  apresentados no relatório mostram desde a inclusão do senador como usuário com plenos poderes em conta bancária empresarial até o custeio de viagens familiares em aeronaves privadas por uma offshore vinculada a negócios de apostas esportivas.




De acordo com o relatório, Flávio Bolsonaro esteve cadastrado com perfil de usuário master na conta bancária da Alcazar Holding mantida junto ao Banco Santander. A condição permitia o gerenciamento da conta até 22 de maio de 2025, quando uma secretária do escritório de Willer Tomaz encaminhou e-mail à instituição financeira solicitando expressamente a remoção do acesso do parlamentar e do próprio advogado.



















A Alcazar Holding detinha, inclusive, 33,33% do capital social da Fraction 024 Administração de Bem Próprio S.A., sociedade proprietária de um jato executivo Legacy 650. A Fraction ganhou projeção pública por ter sido utilizada como pagadora em operações de cessão de ativos vinculadas a investigações sobre o Banco Master e o grupo Viking Participações, ambos de Daniel Vorcaro.




Os arquivos examinados pela PF expõem, ainda, um histórico de deslocamentos internacionais realizados em conjunto por integrantes das famílias de Willer Tomaz e de Flávio Bolsonaro. Os relatórios de voos em jatos executivos para destinos como Cascais (Portugal) e Nice (França), apontam que a aquisição de passagens e a logística de transporte foram intermediadas pela Cathedral Holding.




Segundo a PF, a Cathedral Holding não atuava apenas na esfera patrimonial ou no custeio de despesas pessoais do grupo. A empresa figura no organograma do grupo de Willer Tomaz como sócia da Rede Loto Ltda – primeira operadora a obter credenciamento junto à Loteria do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (Loterj) para explorar apostas esportivas no estado por meio do domínio BestBet.




Conversas secretas e limpeza na Googlesfera




O relatório da PF com base no iCloud do aparelho celular do advogado Willer Tomaz registra ainda que Flávio Bolsonaro era um dos contatos favoritados pelo advogado no aplicativo Confide. A plataforma é um aplicativo que oferece troca de mensagens privadas de vida curta, que desaparecem após pouco tempo, sem histórico aparente no aparelho.



















Os peritos identificaram ainda planilhas e comprovantes de pagamentos efetuados por Willer Tomaz a prestadores de serviços encarregados de remover reportagens e desindexar links do buscador Google. A ideia era tentar controlar o que a plataforma apresentava entre os resultados ao público que buscasse os nomes de Willer Tomaz ou do amigo Flávio Bolsonaro, evitando conteúdos negativos ou indesejados pelo empresário.




Entre os conteúdos que deveriam ser excluídos estava uma reportagem que abordava a atuação política de Flávio Bolsonaro em relação ao projeto de lei dos jogos de azar e sua presença em reuniões com operadoras de cassinos em Las Vegas.




A 

Pública

 buscou a equipe de Flávio Bolsonaro, que não respondeu aos questionamentos até o momento. Em caso de resposta, este espaço será atualizado.

author: Thorin Klosowski
title: Introducing Our New Surveillance Self-Defense Guide: Online Privacy for Parents and Youth
content:
The internet is a vast and confusing place no matter your age. Trying to help youth engage with it safely and privately is a complicated topic that touches on many different skillsets and ideas. But just because it’s complicated doesn’t mean it’s impossible. We’ve launched our 

Online Privacy for Parents and Youth

 Surveillance Self-Defense guide in hopes to provide a framework for finding solutions that work for you. 




EFF rolls out this crucial resource as state and local governments consider 

ill-advised laws

 that cut young people off from essential information and experiences. This particularly harms vulnerable youth and marginalized groups who often find safety in supportive online communities they can't access offline. Such laws also entail age gating, which compromises the privacy of all internet users and stifles young users’ ability to 

learn, grow

, and 

express themselves

.




Young people have unique needs and those needs change over time. Trying to protect from everything all the time is an exhausting process, but the security community has long had a solution for this: 

security planning

 (also called threat modeling). The idea is to provide a series of questions designed to help you focus on what’s truly important. When it comes to online privacy, this is as applicable for youth and parents as it is for anyone else. 




We used a security plan as our foundation for this guide because deciding what is and isn’t important is the first step we should all take when assessing our privacy risks. But this isn’t a place for quick fixes, and every young person has their unique needs and considerations. There is no single tool or technology fix that can substitute for spending time learning, and then teaching a young person, how the internet works, how to use it, what sorts of harms exist, and how to navigate those harms.




Solutions are rarely about the tools or software you use. It’s about understanding the threats and concerns you have, and then determining what steps you can take to mitigate those risks. We hope our 

Online Privacy for Parents and Youth

 guide can help provide the outline to get the conversation started.

author: thecollective
title: Getting Involved
content:
Getting Involved 




In this time of reduced anarchist projects, we’re seeing if there’s energy for us to expand a little. So this is us officially opening up to folks who want to be involved. Here are some of the projects that would be fun and simple to engage in. A list of more-involved options follows.




1. Writing one, or some, opinion pieces for the podcast. You can read it yourself or have one of our regular voices read it for you.

2. Writing a, or some, 

Topic of the Week prompts

.

3. Re-starting the ANews weekly digest (ATUBES) for printing out, leaving about, starting conversations with new people.

4. Recording readings from The Anarchist Library for possible airing on the ANews podcast.

5. Signing up to be one of the weekly conversants for the Topic of the Week prompt featured on the ANews Podcast.

If any of these appeal to you, get in touch via emai at: thecollective at anarchistnews dot org




For the future, maybe. (If there is one!)




We’d like to have a radio project. Imagine 24/7 radio stream that is at times live on air and at other times recorded. This would take probably at least a couple people who are consistent and dedicated. Is that you and a friend? You and an interesting enemy? You and a friend and an interesting enemy? Let us know!

 




We'd like to have more regular feedback and report backs from the various events that anarchists attend and/or organize. Finding and encouraging these report backs would be a potentially easy starting project that could get more involved as it goes along, or just remains checking in with folks you know to give us their (un)biased opinions on what went down, or didn't.

author: Rory Mir
title: Interoperability vs. Security: Why not both?
content:
An open internet where people can freely build, share, and remix each other's work is a powerful engine of grassroots innovation we’ve all benefited from. In recent decades, however, corporations have taken control of an increasing share of this work, giving them a greater ability to stifle challengers and limit our choices. When regulators address this by mandating that  tech giants play fair by requiring interoperability, the gatekeepers respond with a tired refrain: Playing fair puts users’ security at risk.




Unfortunately for these trillion-dollar companies, this 

gotcha

 isn’t the end of the conversation. Regulators can ensure that meaningful choice 

and

 security thrive.




Lawmakers have been catching up, recognizing that the best way to rein in big tech is to require these 

oligopolies

 to open up their platforms to independent developers. As we 

explained six years ago

, mandating interoperability helps prevent the misuse of people’s data and enables more privacy-respecting alternatives. Tech giants, in contrast, have been arguing that our data is safer when they have exclusive control.




Tech Giants Claim Interoperability Means Insecurity




The European Union’s 

Digital Markets Act

 (DMA) put interoperability into law under Article 6(7): “gatekeeper shall allow providers of services and providers of hardware, free of charge, effective interoperability with” a designated 

Core Platform Service

 they operate. The language describes an unambiguous requirement to remediate vendor lockouts and anti-competitive behavior of the major service operators—it is not optional.




Apple 

claimed

 that enforcing this obligation in mobile app stores would put their customers at risk and do irreparable harm to trust in their brand. It’s an argument reminiscent of Apple’s fight against the 

right to repair

, and in both instances the company is fighting to maintain its restrictive ecosystem to stop people from finding better deals elsewhere. Apple has long cultivated a more corporate-controlled experience with the iPhone, but this argument is now also being used for the relatively-more-open Android devices from Google.




In the same year Apple argued against the DMA, Epic Games 

sued Google

 for its restrictive terms of service and extractive policies for revenue generated in apps. Google predictably 

alleged

 that opening up its platform to other app stores it couldn’t vet would allow harmful apps to be installed. The case was ultimately decided this year in the U.S. federal appeals court for the Ninth Circuit, with the court rejecting this argument, dealing a blow to  Google’s 

feudal security

 arrangement, and paving the way for 

third-party app stores to be delivered as apps via the Google Play Store

.




Interoperating Secure Systems Can (and Should) Exist




Policymakers cannot take tech giants’ claims at face value. Companies have every incentive to resist interoperability requirements, because interoperability lowers practical barriers and reduces 

switching costs

 for consumers adopting competing services. 




Even where companies offer credible claims from internal technical and security experts, independent experts rarely have the access and information they need to test those claims. Companies have 

selectively made arguments

 that security is harmed by interoperability, often in contexts which are to their advantage. These companies are happy to let a general misconception flourish which frames security as 

inherently opposed

 to interoperability.




This narrative is wrong. We’ve seen that when interoperability and information security are both set as essential and non-negotiable criteria, secure interoperable systems result—systems that don’t sacrifice the rich features we’ve come to expect of the services we rely on. 




The cross-platform rollout of 

Rich Communication Services

 (RCS), and now 

Message Layer Security

 (MLS) on top of it is a perfect example of this, creating end-to-end secure messaging by default between Android and iOS. For RCS and MLS, Google was conveniently on the other side of the interoperability argument, 

campaigning Apple to adopt the standard

 to overcome the diminished “green bubble” experience iPhone users had when texting non-iPhone users. Once 

Apple finally agreed

 to interoperate by implementing common standards, all users benefited from improved messaging security. In cases where legitimate security concerns are raised, these can be assessed and remedied on a case-by-case basis, without sacrificing user agency.




Striking the Right Balance




Retrofitting interoperability into already secure closed systems shouldn’t be done carelessly: it requires regulators strike the right balance of pressure and leniency to allow the time and precision necessary to make these renovations. Any components developed with the assumption of privileged access by trusted parties (e.g. your 

browser engine

) are particularly vulnerable to serious security risks when opened up to unaccountable third parties.




By adapting interoperability and information security as essential design principles, we can expect more safety, but also more freedom.




With regard to the DMA, when security concerns are legitimate, we urge the European Commission to work with companies and outside experts to offer guidance in technical implementation and provide clarity on regulatory compliance. This approach paves a path forward that balances the interest of legal oversight and the needs of the companies alike. 




Policymakers wishing to uproot these unfair platforms of control must do so with care and limit the impact this disruption can have. But security concerns must not act as a lever to indefinitely delay compliance. Closed systems should be impartially evaluated, and if concerns are valid, regulators can allow more time and guidance to be given to companies implementing these changes. One possibility is a tiered approach: offering leniency during an initial period where systems need to be retrofitted to abide by new requirements, followed by a subsequent and ongoing stricter observance of fair play.




Once interoperability and information security are adopted as essential design principles, further development with these rights-enhancing principles in mind will more easily follow. The result will be an internet the world deserves—where we can expect more safety, but also more freedom.

author: Veridiana Alimonti
title: EFF to Brazil’s ANPD: Data Privacy and Free Expression Must Underpin Platform Regulations
content:
The Brazilian National Data Protection Agency (ANPD) plays a pivotal role in the regulation of digital platforms according to new legislation approved in Brazil. Throughout this year, EFF has presented comments, filed submissions, and met with the agency to emphasize crucial guardrails that the enforcement of new regulations should ensure.

 




ANPD is responsible for detailing and applying obligations set in Law n. 15.211/2025, which established rules for the protection of children and adolescents in the digital space. While some provisions establish important privacy safeguards, like prohibiting advertising based on profiling of underage users, the law created mandatory age assurance mechanisms for accessing digital products and services.

 




We have 

raised alarms

 on the privacy and free expression issues around age-gating the internet. 

Age verification technology is often 

inaccurate

 and 

privacy-invasive

. 

Examples also show

 how it’s prone to enforcement overreach, resulting in sites blocked beyond legal requirements. In the UK, providers disproportionately restricted 

several

 counseling, support and mental health sites under the Online Safety Act. Current age assurance methods risk wrongly walling off adults with 

no valid IDs

, 

facial differences

, 

physical disabilities

, among others.

 




We highlighted these concerns in our 

comments

 and 

submissions

 

underscoring that ANPD should avoid a blanket approach to age assurance obligations. Following the legislation, restrictions should apply only to products and services that are inadequate or prohibited to children and adolescents according to categories already set in regulation, with robust protections against subjective and overbroad interpretations. Guarantees such as access to information, freedom to participate in society and meaningful access to technologies also compound what constitutes the best interests of the child. 

 




Moreover, we stressed that 

zero knowledge proofs

 alone fail to ensure strong user privacy, including safeguards that the law itself sought to secure. Our submission explains why other requirements, such as 

unlinkability, selective disclosure, batch issuance

 and processing on device, are crucial for achieving greater levels of protection and mitigating privacy harms. Minimum information being shared to the verifier and 

no “phoning home”

 to the issuer of a user’s accepted credentials are conditions that prevent actions like collusion and data sharing about the user.

 




We also shared 

inputs

 about the scope of the law, asking more clarity on which providers are covered by its obligations and the importance of treating differently non-dominant players like federated networks and free software applications. Without that clarity, this could negatively impact beyond gaming and major platforms that are the main target of these regulations. We elaborated on the agency’s regulation of prevention duties, the relevance of modulating them according to the type and structure of providers, and alerted them that their interpretation should not result in general monitoring obligations.

 




On another but related front, we sent 

comments

 regarding Brazil’s 

new internet intermediary rules

. Here too, ANPD has a critical regulatory role after a 

Supreme Court’s decision

 and presidential decrees changed the liability regime initially set in the law known as “Marco Civil.” 

 




With the turn to notice and takedown mechanisms and duty of care obligations, we emphasized measures to prevent censorship of protected content. These involve ensuring solid means for appeals of restricted posts, avoiding overreliance on 

AI-based content moderation

, strictly tailoring the application of concepts like duty of care and systemic failure, and not normalizing the blocking of platforms and websites. 

 




We raised concerns about a trend reflected in the new regulation requiring platforms to proactively report user to authorities with unclear guarantees. Finally, we urged the agency to advance essential transparency and accountability measures for enabling greater public oversight over the application of the new regime.

 




As we 

said

 before, platform accountability under the new rules ultimately hinges on how accountable its enforcement will be by platforms and state institutions. Rigorous commitment to fundamental rights, including freedom of expression, privacy and data protection, is required so that intended protections don’t instead lead to harms. ANPD must uphold this commitment and make sure that new regulations don’t backfire.

title: Siber Güvenlik Başkanlığı'ndan kritik güvenlik uyarısı
content:
Siber Güvenlik Başkanlığı, dünya genelinde yaygın olarak kullanılan PHP yazılım altyapısında kritik güvenlik açıkları tespit edildiğini belirterek şu açıklamayı yaptı “Dünya genelinde yaygın olarak kullanılan PHP yazılım altyapısında kritik güvenlik açıkları tespit edilmiştir.

Başkanlığımız, söz konusu zafiyetlerin oluşturabileceği risklerin erken tespiti ve olası etkilerinin sınırlandırılması amacıyla ulusal ölçekte güvenlik taramalarını başlatmış, ilgili kurum ve kuruluşlara acil güvenlik bildirimlerini iletmiştir.

Kamu kurumlarımızın, kritik altyapı işletmecilerimizin ve özel sektör kuruluşlarımızın sistemlerini gözden geçirerek gerekli güvenlik güncellemelerini ivedilikle uygulamaları önem taşımaktadır.

Dijital altyapılarımızın güvenliği ve kritik hizmetlerin sürekliliği için ulusal düzeyde koordinasyon ve önleyici güvenlik çalışmalarımız sürmektedir.”
