title: Who pays the price of peace?
content:
In his work 

The Old Regime and the Revolution

, Alexis de Tocqueville exposes one of the fundamental contradictions of the French Revolution: The monarchy had been overthrown, and the institutions of the old regime had been abolished, yet the centralist tradition of state domination over society persisted within the new order. The regime had changed, but the state’s power to determine social relations remained largely intact.




As Tocqueville demonstrates, therein lies a fundamental danger: Change can perpetuate existing power structures rather than overcome them.




From this perspective, the process currently underway in Turkey concerning the Kurdish question must also be examined. The decisive question is not merely whether the armed conflict will come to an end, but whether the historically entrenched relationship of domination from which this conflict emerged will also change.




After more than half a century of struggle, the Kurdish freedom movement has made historic decisions that fundamentally transform its armed strategy and organizational existence. These decisions cannot be explained by the naivety of a movement unaware of Turkey’s political realities. Throughout its long struggle, the Kurdish movement has come to understand the centralist nature of the state, its security-driven reflexes, and its resistance to democratization. Its insistence on a democratic solution stems not from ignorance of this reality, but from a determination to change it.




However, a movement’s willingness to transform itself offers no guarantee that the state power confronting it will undergo a similar transformation. Today, we are dealing not only with historically entrenched patterns of state conduct, but also with the current regime’s strategy for shaping its own future. The Kurdish question is not separate from this strategy. Rather, it is one of the central issues that the regime seeks to restructure in line with its political and regional objectives.




The transition is not intended to be a solution




The limits of this approach become particularly evident in remarks made by presidential adviser Mehmet Uçum on October 17. Uçum defines the process in unequivocal terms: “This is not a resolution process, but a transition process.”




This is by no means merely a terminological distinction. A resolution requires confronting the historical causes of a conflict, the political demands of the parties involved, and the question of equal rights. The transition described by Uçum, by contrast, is based on ending the movement’s organizational existence, completing the disarmament process in full, and having its completion verified and confirmed by the state. Democratization and a new constitution are designated as subjects for separate negotiations. The idea that they should be made prerequisites for the transition is explicitly rejected.




As a result, the transformation of the Kurdish movement becomes a concrete obligation in the present, while the democratic transformation of the regime is postponed to an indefinite future.




There is a timetable for disarmament, but none for political equality.




Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş has also stated that even after a law is passed, no further steps will be taken until disarmament has been verified and officially confirmed by the state. At the same time, he calls for an end to “separatist language.” Verifying disarmament is an understandable necessity within a negotiation process. However, when the state authority responsible for verification also dictates which political views may no longer be expressed, this goes beyond security-related oversight.




Uçum, for his part, establishes a hierarchy among political actors within Kurdish politics. He determines who should be regarded as legitimate negotiating partners and who should be considered obstacles to the process. This reveals an approach that seeks not only to define the conditions of the transition, but also to determine the boundaries within which Kurdish political representation is permitted to operate.




Who determines the boundaries of what is politically conceivable?




His remarks on the future constitutional debate are particularly revealing: “No one should expect negotiations on the new constitution to be conducted on the basis of ethnic and identity-based political positions.”




Uçum argues that these issues must come to an end not only in practice, but also “in people’s minds.” This is no longer simply about ending the armed conflict. Rather, boundaries are also being drawn around the political demands Kurds may bring into the new phase and the visions of the future they are even permitted to put forward for discussion.




Yet peacefully discussing independence, federalism, autonomy, or democratic coexistence, and advocating corresponding political positions, does not in any way imply a desire to continue the armed conflict. Renouncing armed struggle does not mean renouncing the right to self-determination.




Uçum’s remarks cannot be regarded as a definitive decision by the state. Nevertheless, the approach they reveal is sufficiently clear: The regime seeks to end the conflict while retaining the power to define the political boundaries of the new phase.




The end of armed struggle is not yet a solution




It is precisely at this point that Tocqueville’s critique of centralism acquires particular significance. A centralist state does not necessarily resist change. At times, it directs that change itself and even presents itself as its driving force. However, it resists when change begins to challenge its own structures of domination. The fact that a regime makes the Kurdish question politically manageable in accordance with its own vision of the future does not mean that it has resolved it.




The end of armed struggle does not mean that Kurds have thereby been recognized as a collective political subject. They did not acquire their political existence only with the beginning of the current process. Rather, they have developed their own political will through more than a century of resistance and immense sacrifices. The state’s responsibility, therefore, is not to bring this will into existence, but to cease denying its existence and the rights associated with it.




The measure of a genuine solution cannot, therefore, be the silence of weapons. What matters instead is the recognition of Kurds as political subjects with the right to participate in determining their own future and to make their own decisions.




The state is not content with being merely one of the parties to the peace process. It also claims the role of arbiter, control over the process’s timetable, and the authority to define the boundaries of legitimate political expression. This does not constitute a democratic solution between political subjects on an equal footing.




Who bears the burdens, and who reaps the benefits?




Through historic decisions, the Kurds have demonstrated their willingness to engage in negotiations and assume the far-reaching obligations associated with peace. Yet peace cannot be an agreement in which one side takes concrete and irreversible steps while the other postpones its responsibilities to an indefinite future.




The burdens of peace must be distributed with due regard for historical responsibility and political equality. For the state to confront its policy of denial, recognize the collective existence of the Kurdish people, and provide legal guarantees for that recognition is not a concession it graciously grants in exchange for disarmament, but a necessary prerequisite for a just solution.




This is precisely where the fundamental problem lies: instead of conducting negotiations between political subjects on an equal footing, the conditions of the transition are being determined unilaterally. The consent of a people cannot be secured by dictating which political demands they must abandon.




At this point, the warning issued by Ömer Hayri Konar from Imrali also takes on particular significance. He cautioned that the policies pursued thus far are continuing in more subtle forms. A change in the methods of struggle does not mean that the historical causes from which that struggle emerged have been eliminated.




The end of the conflict could bring Turkey considerable benefits, ranging from security and regional relations to domestic politics and its international standing. However, if the regime appropriates these benefits while the collective rights and political equality of the Kurds remain unresolved, an unavoidable question arises: Who bears the costs of peace, and who reaps its rewards?




Put more pointedly, this amounts to getting off cheaply: claiming the benefits of ending the conflict without changing the historical relationship of denial and domination from which the conflict emerged.




A democratic solution to the Kurdish question and the democratization of Turkey cannot be separated from one another. However, this connection does not justify postponing the recognition of Kurdish rights to an indefinite point within an equally uncertain democratization process. There is therefore no contradiction in defending the negotiation process while simultaneously criticizing the regime’s position. Supporting peace does not mean suspending democratic opposition.




Self-determination is not a favor granted by the state




The Kurds are not waiting for the state to grant them their freedom. Their history of struggle spanning more than a century already demonstrates this. What is expected of the state is that it assume its historical responsibility: acknowledge the policy of denial, the massacres, forced assimilation, and the political order that made all of this possible, and initiate the legal and democratic steps arising from this reckoning with the past.




The state is confronted by a Kurdish freedom movement whose political will has been tested and proven through more than half a century of struggle. This will did not emerge through state recognition, but was forged and sustained in the face of denial and prohibitions, at the cost of immense sacrifices. To assume that the Kurdish freedom movement, after more than half a century of struggle, would submit to the political boundaries imposed by the regime would be to misunderstand both the history and the very foundations of this movement’s existence.




In the same work, Tocqueville describes the confidence that those who carried out the revolution placed in their own strength:




“They were filled with such proud confidence in their own strength that this confidence could sometimes lead them astray. Yet without such self-confidence, a people would never have risen beyond the role of serving others.”




 




This does not mean believing that a people always makes the right decisions, but rather having confidence in its own ability to determine its future, even while recognizing that it may make mistakes along the way. Denial and assimilation are directed not only against a people’s language, identity, and rights. They also seek to undermine its self-confidence. A people is meant to be made to believe that it is incapable of shaping its own future and can exist only within the boundaries permitted by the ruling power.




It is precisely for this reason that Uçum’s demand that political aspirations must also come to an end “in people’s minds” is particularly significant: The aim is no longer merely to determine the boundaries of political action, but also to define the limits of what a people is even allowed to imagine for its own future.




Ultimately, the Kurds can negotiate the conditions, methods, and guarantees of peace. Forms of struggle and political programs may change. However, no negotiation can be made conditional on the Kurds relinquishing their determination to decide their own future. The history of more than half a century of struggle demonstrates that this determination has been sustained not by accepting boundaries imposed by the state, but by resisting them. Throughout history, political orders established to suppress the will of entire peoples have undergone transformation; many have long since become a thing of the past. The measure of lasting peace, therefore, cannot be how far the will of a people can be restricted, but whether political conditions are created in which that will can develop freely.




The patience of the Kurds cannot serve as a guarantee for a democracy whose realization in Turkey has been postponed for a century. Peace does not mean forcing the Kurds to fit within boundaries drawn by the state, but overcoming the system of denial and domination that has imposed those boundaries upon them for a century.

author: Unknown
title: Organizations in Rojhilat call on Damascus government to recognize Kurdish language rights
content:
Nine professional associations and civil society organizations from Rojhilat (East Kurdistan) and Iran issued a joint statement condemning the restrictions and bans imposed on Kurdish-language education in Rojava (West Kurdistan).




The statement called on the Syrian government to recognize the right to education in the mother tongue at all levels of education. The signatories also urged international organizations and human rights groups to take action to have these bans lifted.




‘Restrictions cause unrest’




With the start of the new academic year in Syria, the organizations stated that Kurdish students who had previously received education in their mother tongue are now facing restrictions, with Kurdish-language instruction limited to just three hours.




The organizations said these restrictions have caused unrest among students and local communities and led to the cancellation of numerous classes.




‘Recognizing linguistic and cultural diversity is a prerequisite for peaceful coexistence’




Highlighting Syria’s national, linguistic, and religious diversity, the statement criticized the continuation of policies pursued under the former Assad regime. These policies, it added, included stripping large numbers of Kurdish citizens of their citizenship and implementing policies of “Arabization.”




“Recognizing linguistic and cultural diversity is a prerequisite for peaceful coexistence and the development of a democratic society. Imposing a ‘one nation, one language’ model on different communities will only lead to conflict and discrimination,” the statement said.




‘Fundamental rights have been restricted’




The organizations noted that the autonomous administration system established in Rojava following the developments in Syria in 2011 had created greater opportunities for recognizing the region’s linguistic, cultural, and historical diversity.




However, it emphasized that following the overthrow of Bashar al-Assad’s regime and the subsequent political and military changes, the fundamental rights of different ethnic groups, including the right to education in their mother tongue, had been restricted.




Call for an end to restrictions




Drawing attention to established principles of international law and the educational and psychological needs of children, the organizations called for an end to restrictions on education affecting Kurds and other linguistic communities in Syria.




The statement emphasized the right of all students to receive education in their mother tongue at every level and expressed solidarity with students, the Rojava Teachers’ Union, and the people of the region.




In conclusion, the signatories called on international organizations and human rights institutions to take concrete and effective steps to pressure the Syrian government into recognizing and guaranteeing the right to education in the mother tongue.




The signatory organizations are as follows:




1- Kurdistan Teachers’ Union – Sine




2- Kurdistan Teachers’ Union – Seqiz and Ziviye




3- Kurdistan Teachers’ Union – Merîwan and Serabad




4- Harsîn Teachers’ Union




5- Mazandaran Teachers’ Union




6- Bushehr Teachers’ Union




7- Islamabad Traditional Clothing Educators’ Union




8- Zîla Jiyanê (Çroy-e Jiyan) – Saqiz




9- Kurdish Unity Front

author: Unknown
title: ÖHD documents environmental destruction on Mount Gabar
content:
The Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) has investigated the ongoing ecological destruction in the Gabar Mountains in the Kurdish province of Şırnak. A delegation from the Ecology Commission of the ÖHD’s provincial executive board and its local branch documented the impact of large-scale deforestation and intensive oil extraction on the ground. The findings of the investigation are expected to be published in a report in the coming days.




ÖHD lawyer Hülya Yıldırım regards the activities on Mount Gabar not as an isolated case of environmental destruction, but as part of the war and security policies pursued in Kurdistan for decades. She noted that forests are also being cleared in the neighboring mountainous regions of Besta and Cudi, while fires are destroying large areas of land and natural habitats are being damaged by mining operations and environmentally harmful industrial facilities.




“There are now oil wells and extraction facilities in virtually every corner of Mount Gabar. As a result, the mountain is literally being blasted apart. The Tigris River is being polluted by oil leaks and petroleum waste,” said Yıldırım, a member of the ÖHD Ecology Commission.







Oil extraction hinders return to destroyed villages




According to the delegation’s observations, the impact of oil extraction extends beyond the immediate destruction of the natural environment. The health of local residents and workers, as well as livelihoods dependent on agriculture and livestock farming, are also at risk.




The consequences are particularly severe for people who have been waiting for decades to return to their home villages. Numerous settlements in the region were burned down and forcibly depopulated during the dirty war against the PKK in the 1990s. According to the ÖHD, current oil extraction and development activities are creating additional obstacles to the resettlement of these villages.




Yıldırım also criticized the fact that the approval procedures for activities affecting the natural environment do not even comply with the requirements of existing legislation. She argued that these practices reflect a policy that views forests, mountains, soil, and waterways solely as resources to be exploited for economic gain.




“These areas, these mountains, this land, and this river are all regarded merely as resources. We will continue to oppose this mentality and the approval procedures that do not even comply with existing laws,” the lawyer stated.







‘This destruction is a policy of special warfare’




ÖHD lawyer Ayşe Şehriban Demirel, who participated in the field inspection, also placed the environmental destruction within the region’s political context. She argued that the activities on Mount Gabar should not be viewed solely from an economic perspective, but as an expression of a deliberate policy targeting the Kurdish population and their living environment.




“What is happening here is a policy of special warfare. This destruction causes us profound pain. We are working to put an end to this exploitation and ensure that those responsible are held accountable,” Demirel said.




The ÖHD plans to make the findings gathered during its investigation public in the coming days and expand its legal and public advocacy efforts against environmental destruction. The organization also intends to link resistance to the activities on Mount Gabar with efforts to protect the neighboring mountainous regions of Cudi and Besta.




“We will expose the ecological destruction on Mount Gabar and raise our voices against this exploitation and destruction of nature, particularly in Cudi and Besta as well,” Demirel announced.

title: Petites leçons de manipulation par CHATGPT ... et le monde qui se profile derrière
content:
Présentation, discussion et apéro autour du livre "Petites leçons de manipulation par CHATGPT" avec l'autrice Sarah Dubernet à la médiathèque alternative Mille Bâbords (61 rue Consolat) samedi 24 octobre à 18h30.




Samedi 24 octobre à 18h30 la médiathèque des luttes, Mille Bâbords, accueille Sarah Dubernet pour discuter de son livre sur le monde de ChatGPT.




Trois semaines à harceler ChatGPT sur différentes questions qui fâchent ; voici un livre dans lequel l'autrice lui fait dire ce que ses concepteurs et financeurs ne veulent pas qu'il dise : ses censures, sa propagande, l'idéologie transhumaniste et les responsabilités politico-industrielles qui en découlent, les ésotérismes et exotérismes scientifiques, religieux, politiques… Une joute improvisée entre une technocritique et une IA sur le système technicien, son impact et les méthodes d'ingénierie sociale qui lui permettent d'avancer toujours dans le même sens, sans jamais être dérangé.




Ce livre souligne l'importance de protéger notre intelligence, nos questions et nos propres façons d'y répondre face à une machine qui n'a pas vocation à nous éveiller. Si l'autrice a pu lui faire dire tout ça, c'est parce qu'elle connaissait déjà les sujets abordés. Mais ChatGPT expliquera ici que son rôle est au contraire de nous orienter vers un tout autre chemin… les échanges sont étayés de rapports institutionnels.




Ceci n'est pas un livre sur ChatGPT. C'est un livre sur son monde et la façon dont il le sert. Ces échanges constituent un document rare, un témoignage précieux, non seulement sur les mécanismes de l'IA mais aussi sur la nature même du « dialogue » que l'on nous vendra demain comme neutre et transparent alors qu'il sera au contraire de plus en plus « sécurisé »




Mille Bâbords est un lieu de culture politique et de rencontre pour la vie associative et militante marseillaise proposant un service de prêt gratuit pour toustes. La bibliothèque est ouverte au public lors des permanences tous les lundis et les 2ème et 4ème jeudis de 15h à 18h.

title: Iqaluit woman charged with 2nd-degree murder
content:
RCMP have charged a woman with second-degree murder following a disturbance in Iqaluit’s Tundra Valley neighbourhood over the weekend.




Police found a 37-year-old woman with life threatening injuries in the city’s 2400 block at around 5:50 a.m. on Saturday, said RCMP spokesperson Sgt. George Henrie in a news release.




She was transported to Qikiqtani General hospital, where she died.




Christie Nutarariaq, 32, has been charged with second degree murder in relation to the incident.




The incident is unrelated to 

another

 murder charge that police announced Monday.




In that case, RCMP charged a 21-year-old Qaqasie Aningmiuq with second-degree murder, following an altercation on Oct. 6 that left one man dead.




Nutarariaq is in custody. Her next court appearance is set for Nov. 17.

title: Cops raid DIY HRT meeting in Berlin
content:
This Sunday, 18 October 2026, German police raided a trans DIY HRT event organized by The Dolls Berlin in community centre Casa Kuà.

While the group was holding a talk about cryptocurrency and their role in purchasing HRT online, 38 uniformed and plain clothes cops stormed the building, confiscating hormones and money from attendees, recording their identity and detaining them for over 4 hours. So far, nobody was charged with any crime, (as there is nothing illegal about having hormones or money on your person).

The intimidation raid has shocked the community and over a hundred people gathered quickly for a counter demo. One person was arrested during the demo.

title: A trans woman, Joelle, was denied a spot in a cancer ward in the UK because she was trans and it…
content:
A trans woman, Joelle, was denied a spot in a cancer ward in the UK because she was trans and it lead to her death from an easily treatable form of lymphoma. As she was dying she begged for a room in either the male or female ward - but she was denied being told to wait until they had a rare single room available. For 16 days she was in that hospital dying from something easily treatable because of transphobic legislation. Sex/gender segregated wards are just another way the government violently enforces the sexgender binary - causing the death of transgender and gender diverse people.

Trans Legal Clinic is crowdfunding money to fund the legal case to get justice for Joelle and to prevent any more trans people from being denied care the way she was. If you can donate please do.

title: Συγκέντρωση υπεράσπισης του Αναρχικού Στεκιού Φιλοσοφικής ΕΚΠΑ, Τρίτη 20/10, στις 11:00
content:
ΣΥΓΚΕΝΤΡΩΣΗ ΕΝΑΝΤΙΑ ΣΤΙΣ ΑΣΤΥΝΟΜΙΚΕΣ ΕΙΣΒΟΛΕΣ ΚΑΙ ΓΙΑ ΤΗΝ ΥΠΕΡΑΣΠΙΣΗ ΤΟΥ ΑΝΑΡΧΙΚΟΥ ΣΤΕΚΙΟΥ ΦΙΛΟΣΟΦΙΚΗΣ | Τρίτη 20/10 στις 11:00 στον 8ο όροφο της Φιλοσοφικής Σχολής – αίθουσα 819




Καλέσματα:




ΑΝΑΡΧΙΚΟ ΣΤΕΚΙ ΦΙΛΟΣΟΦΙΚΗΣ




ΣΥΓΚΕΝΤΡΩΣΗ ΕΝΑΝΤΙΑ ΣΤΙΣ ΑΣΤΥΝΟΜΙΚΕΣ ΕΙΣΒΟΛΕΣ ΚΑΙ ΓΙΑ ΤΗΝ ΥΠΕΡΑΣΠΙΣΗ ΤΟΥ ΑΝΑΡΧΙΚΟΥ ΣΤΕΚΙΟΥ ΦΙΛΟΣΟΦΙΚΗΣ | Τρίτη 20/10 στις 11:00 στον 8ο όροφο της Φιλοσοφικής Σχολής – αίθουσα 819




ΤΟ ΑΝΑΡΧΙΚΟ ΣΤΕΚΙ ΦΙΛΟΣΟΦΙΚΗΣ ΘΑ ΠΕΡΑΣΕΙ ΣΤΑ ΧΕΡΙΑ ΤΩΝ ΦΟΙΤΗΤΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΟΧΙ ΤΩΝ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΤΗΣ ΕΛΑΣ




Από το Πάσχα κι έπειτα έχουν πραγματοποιηθεί τρεις αστυνομικές εισβολές στην Φιλοσοφική σχολή και ισάριθμες εκκενώσεις του Αναρχικού Στεκιού Φιλοσοφικής. Έχουν ακολουθήσει τρεις μαζικές συγκεντρώσεις έξω από το Αναρχικό Στέκι Φιλοσοφικής με την στήριξη πλήθους φοιτητών, εργαζομένων και αλληλέγγυων και δύο ανακαταλήψεις της αίθουσας 819, όπου αυτό στεγάζεται από το 1995. Κατά την τελευταία, μάλιστα, μαζική συγκέντρωση υπεράσπισης του, την 1η του Σεπτέμβρη, η οποία έληξε με το άνοιγμα της πόρτας και την ανάκτηση του στεκιού παρά την ασφυκτική αστυνομική πίεση, οι ένστολοι δολοφόνοι της ΕΛΑΣ εισέβαλλαν στην άδεια τότε, λόγω εξεταστικής περιόδου, Φιλοσοφική Σχολή, θέλοντας να τρομοκρατήσουν και να αποδιοργανώσουν την συγκέντρωση και να προχωρήσουν σε συλλήψεις φοιτητών, κάτι το οποίο δεν επετεύχθει χάρη στην αλληλέγγυα στάση και την αποφασιστικότητα των συγκεντρωμένων. Τις επόμενες μέρες, κατά την προσφιλή τους τακτική, συνεργείο επανασφράγισε στα κλεφτά την πόρτα του Αναρχικού Στεκιού Φιλοσοφικής.




Γιατί όμως τέτοια επιμονή από τον πρύτανη του ΕΚΠΑ και τους πολιτικούς του προϊστάμενους στο Υπουργείο για την εκκένωση του Αναρχικού Στεκιού Φιλοσοφικής και τέτοια κινητοποίηση της ΕΛΑΣ;




Η απάντηση δεν βρίσκεται, σίγουρα, στα προπαγανδιστικά αστικά αφηγήματα, για την πάταξη της «ανομίας» και της «εγκληματικότητας» μέσα στα πανεπιστήμια. Όποιος έχει και την ελάχιστη σχέση με τα ελληνικά πανεπιστήμια, μπορεί να καταλάβει πολύ καλά την φαιδρότητα αυτών των επιχειρημάτων. Ούτε πρόκειται για μια μάχη μεταξύ αναρχικών και αστυνομίας γύρω από μια κατειλημμένη αίθουσα και τέλος, όπως πάλι προπαγανδιστικά προβάλλεται από το κράτος και τους μηχανισμούς του. Οι στόχοι που θέλουν να πετύχουν με τις αστυνομικές εισβολές και την εκκένωση των κατειλημμένων αγωνιζόμενων χώρων μέσα στα πανεπιστήμια είναι πολύ διαφορετικοί, αφορούν και επηρεάζουν την συντριπτική πλειοψηφία των φοιτητών/τριών.




Οι πραγματικοί στόχοι αφορούν την εδραίωση και το βάθεμα των αστικών σχεδιασμών για την τριτοβάθμια εκπαίδευση. Οι διαγραφές φοιτητών, τα μη κρατικά – στην ουσία – ιδιωτικά πανεπιστήμια, τα επί πληρωμεί προπτυχιακά ξενόγλωσσα προγράμματα είναι συνθήκες που πριν από, όχι και πολλά χρόνια, θα φαίνονταν αδιανόητες να γίνονται πράξη. Όχι επειδή οι προηγούμενες κυβερνήσεις δεν είχαν την πολιτική βούληση, αλλά επειδή οι συσχετισμοί δύναμης μέσα στα πανεπιστήμια δεν το επέτρεπαν να συμβεί. Αυτούς τους συσχετισμούς δύναμης επιχειρούν να ανατρέψουν, εκριζώνοντας και καταστέλλοντας τις αγωνιζόμενες δυνάμεις μέσα στα πανεπιστήμια και επιχειρώντας να τσακίσουν τις κατακτήσεις που κερδήθηκαν με αίμα και αγώνες κατά τις προηγούμενες δεκαετίες. Για να μπορούν μετά ανεμπόδιστα να εφαρμόσουν τους αστικούς σχεδιασμούς που οδηγούν την συντριπτική πλειοψηφία των φοιτητών στην ταξική εξουθένωση και το άγχος για να ολοκληρώσουν τις σπουδές και παράλληλα στο κυνήγι επί πληρωμεί καταρτίσεων και εξειδικεύσεων για να βγουν στην επισφαλή αγορά εργασίας, όπου θα αμείβονται με 3,60.




Κι ενώ οι αστικοί σχεδιασμοί για τις σπουδές μας προχωρούν, τα ιδιωτικά συμφέροντα διεισδύουν όλο και βαθύτερα μέσα στο ίδιο το «δημόσιο πανεπιστήμιο», μετατρέποντας το σε «πανεπιστήμιο Α.Ε.». Ιδιωτικά συμφέροντα σε ερευνητικά προγράμματα, συνεργαζόμενες εταιρείες με το πανεπιστήμιο, εργολαβίες σε κάθε πτυχή του (από την σίτιση έως την καθαριότητα και την φύλαξη), εισέρχονται όλο και περισσότερο μέσα στην καθημερινότητα των σχολών μας, κερδοφορώντας μέσα σ’ αυτό. Και για να επιτευχθεί αυτό το όραμα, πρέπει οι αγωνιζόμενες και ριζοσπαστικές φωνές να εκλείψουν και γιατί όχι και οι χώροι που στεγάζονται να παραδοθούν κι αυτοί στην κερδοφορία των λίγων και να μην βρίσκονται στα χέρια των φοιτητών και της συλλογικής τους αντίστασης. Εκεί βέβαια θα ανθίσει η πραγματική ανομία του συστήματος, η ανομία των απευθείας αναθέσεων σε εργολαβίες, η ανομία των μαφιόζων – ναρκεμπόρων εργολάβων που συνεργάζεται το ΕΚΠΑ (π.χ. MyServices), η ανομία των μεγαλοεπιχειρηματιών που αισχροκερδούν. Αυτή η ανομία βέβαια δεν τους ενοχλεί γιατί είναι απόλυτα συμβατή με το σύστημα του κράτους και του καπιταλισμού, αποτελώντας δομικό στοιχείο του.




Η σημασία της 20ης Οκτώβρη και γιατί υπερβαίνει την μάχη γύρω από μια αίθουσα




Την 20η του Οκτώβρη καλούμε τους φοιτητές και τις φοιτήτριες, τους εργαζόμενους του πανεπιστημίου και κάθε αλληλέγγυο, σε συγκέντρωση ενάντια στις αστυνομικές εισβολές και για την υπεράσπιση του Αναρχικού Στεκιού Φιλοσοφικής στις 11:00 στον 8ο όροφο της Φιλοσοφικής Σχολής. Το επίδικο της συγκεκριμένης συγκέντρωσης και της συνέχειας του αγώνα για την διατήρηση της, αφορά πολλά περισσότερα από μια «μάχη» για μια αίθουσα μέσα στα πανεπιστήμια, όχι γιατί αυτή είναι ασήμαντη και δεν θα την διεκδικήσουμε. Αλλά γιατί, ο αγώνας αυτός είναι ένας αγώνας ενάντια σε όλα τα παραπάνω που επιχειρούν να εφαρμόσουν μέσα στα πανεπιστήμια, επιχειρώντας στην φιλοσοφική και στις υπόλοιπες σχολές να ξεριζώσουν τους αγώνες και τις κατακτήσεις του φοιτητικού κινήματος. Εάν υπήρχε, άλλωστε, και οποιαδήποτε άλλη εμφανή αιτία για τις συνεχείς εκκενώσεις και τις αστυνομικές εισβολές στην φιλοσοφική, είμαστε σίγουροι ότι θα την έπαιζαν από το πρωί μέχρι το βράδυ στα δελτία ειδήσεων και τα συστημικά siteς τους. Κάτι τέτοιο δεν συμβαίνει, επιχειρώντας να μετατρέψουν την φιλοσοφική σχολή εν κρυπτώ σε πεδίο εφόδου των δολοφόνων της ΕΛΑΣ.




Το πανεπιστημιακό άσυλο και η πολιτική δράση μέσα στα πανεπιστήμια ποτέ δεν μας παραχωρήθηκαν από το κράτος, αλλά κερδήθηκαν με αιματηρούς αγώνες. Αυτούς τους αγώνες επιχειρούν να αφανίσουν, γιατί όταν μιλάνε για «εκσυγχρονισμό» και «πρόοδο» του ελληνικού πανεπιστημίου στην πραγματικότητα μιλούν για επιστροφή δεκαετίες πίσω: στη χούντα των συνταγματαρχών.




Στις 20 του Οκτώβρη, λοιπόν, να τους δείξουμε ότι η πλειοψηφία μέσα στις σχολές είμαστε εμείς και όχι οι εργολαβίες, τα εταιρικά κοράκια, οι πρυτάνεις και οι εισαγγελείς που παρασιτούν εις βάρος μας μέσα σ΄ αυτές. Καλούμε σε μαζική συμμετοχή και στήριξη όσους δεν επιθυμούν να δουν την φιλοσοφική σχολή – και κάθε σχολή- να μετατρέπεται σε ερημωμένη και αποστειρωμένη ζώνη, χωρίς συλλογικούς χώρους και αντιστάσεις. Μέσα στους καιρούς υποχώρησης των αγώνων που ζούμε, υπάρχει η αναγκαιότητα να δώσουμε κάθε μικρή και μεγάλη μάχη μέσα στα πανεπιστήμια. Η συγκέντρωση της 20ης του Οκτώβρη να αποτελέσει μια μικρή νίκη, στον ορίζοντα των επομένων που θα πρέπει να ανοίξουμε.

author: Natalia Viana
title: A eleição das Big Techs
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Xeque na Democracia, enviada toda segunda-feira, 12h. Para receber as próximas edições, 

inscreva-se aqui.







“Wow”, tuitou Elon Musk, dono do X, depois que as apostas no site Polymarket passaram a favorecer Flávio Bolsonaro na disputa contra Lula, demonstrando quem é seu favorito nas eleições brasileiras. O advogado Martin de Lucca, tuitou: “Primeiro eles cancelaram o X. Depois cancelaram o Rumble. Recentemente, até cancelaram o Polymarket. O tiro saiu espetacularmente pela culatra”, escreveu Lucca, que advoga para a Truth Social, rede de Donald Trump, e para a Rumble, rede social de direita que teve investimento milionário de JD Vance e de Peter Thiel, depois da vantagem de Flávio no primeiro turno. “Que bela manhã, né Brasil?”. 




JD Vance reuniu-se com Flávio Bolsonaro em maio deste ano, e com André Marinho, filho do coordenador de campanha bolsonarista, em abril. Seu aliado e fiador, Peter Thiel, esteve em São Paulo apenas duas semanas depois, em 30 de abril, com uma comitiva de pelo menos 15 executivos, segundo 

revelou

 o jornalista Paulo Motoryn. De acordo com o 

site Amado Mundo

, a rede Rockbridge Network, fundada por JD Vance, mantém um representante integrante dentro da sede de campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro em São Paulo, e enviou um plano de trabalho que incluía a criação de um Conselho de Tecnologia para assessorar sua campanha, 

segundo

 o Intercept. 




Mark Zuckerberg, em janeiro do ano passado, nomeou o Brasil – sem nomear – ao afirmar que “os países latino-americanos têm tribunais secretos que podem ordenar empresas para silenciosamente derrubar [posts]” e que se uniria ao governo de Donald Trump para lutar contra essas ordens secretas – a referência eram ordens do STF depois da tentativa de Golpe de Estado em 2023. 




Os donos das Big Techs estão acompanhando de perto as eleições brasileiras. Afinal, sabem que elas serão cruciais para definir como será o futuro dos seus negócios. 




O caso mais notório de interferência, até agora, tem sido a Meta – empresa que mais faturou com impulsionamento de campanhas, R$282 milhões. Mesmo assim, funcionários da empresa 

reclamaram

 em canais internos da inação dos desenvolvedores lotados nos EUA em reverter o banimento da conta de anúncios da campanha de Lula no Instagram, em 9 de outubro. Os americanos fizeram corpo mole em vez de permitir condições iguais às do adversário, que seguia impulsionando seus conteúdos. 




Mas esse foi apenas um dos eventos. Na semana passada, a IA da Meta permitia que qualquer pessoa criasse imagens pró-Flávio e contra o Lula – acusando o PT de corrupto, por exemplo. Se o mesmo pedido era feito sobre o candidato do PL, a IA respondia que não podia gerar a imagem. A Meta reconheceu que sua IA permitiu a criação de imagens favorecendo Flávio e que “a conta de anúncios da campanha de Lula foi desativada por engano por pouco mais de 1 hora, e não por razões políticas”.




Antes disso, a Meta suspendeu por algumas horas a conta do canal Revelando Brasil no Instagram, que tem publicado vídeos documentais sobre casos envolvendo Flávio Bolsonaro, quando este se tornava o principal assunto das redes, uma semana antes do primeiro turno. Até agora não houve explicação do porquê.    




A tendência para o lado da campanha do filho de Jair incomodou até mesmo o TSE, que na semana passada decidiu que a Big Tech tem que agir com isonomia sobre conteúdos das duas campanhas – e que 

prove

 que está fazendo isso. Em caso de descumprimento, a Meta terá que pagar R$ 500 mil por dia.




O Ministério da Justiça acionou a Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) e o Ministério Público Federal para abrir uma investigação contra a Meta, e a Procuradoria Federal dos Direitos do Cidadão do MPF já 

abriu um procedimento para investigar a empresa

. Além disso, a deputada Érika Hilton (PSOL-SP) está coletando assinaturas para uma CPI na Câmara dos Deputados para investigar se está havendo interferência das Big Techs nas eleições. 




A mobilização chamou a atenção da imprensa internacional – o que forçou a Meta a publicar um comunicado negando tentar interferir nas eleições. A empresa ainda saiu com essa: “Há muito tempo, a Meta alerta que as regras rígidas do Brasil para conteúdo digital aumentam o risco de aplicação excessiva e ameaçam a liberdade de expressão. Desde 2025, essas regras ampliaram a possível responsabilidade das plataformas por conteúdo e anúncios gerados por terceiros” – ou seja, a culpa dela estar prejudicando a campanha petista é da regulação.  




É aí que está o fio da meada. 

Faz sentido para a Meta e também para outras Techs investirem no fim do governo Lula porque o Brasil é o fiel da balança no sul global em termos de regulação do mundo digital. 




Durante o governo Lula, elas contabilizaram muitas derrotas: o banimento do Twitter pelo STF; a decisão do STF de responsabilizá-las legalmente por conteúdo ilegal; o Eca Digital, conhecido como “Lei Felca”; a decisão do Cade de abrir uma investigação conta o Google por concorrência desleal ao jornalismo ao lucrar com o conteúdo sem pagar por ele, além de outras decisões da Secretaria Nacional do Consumidor (Senacom), do MJ, e da ANPD – por exemplo, a agência 

obrigou

 a Meta a informar os usuários e pedir permissão sobre uso de conteúdos de usuários no Facebook, WhatsApp, e Instagram para treino no IA. Recentemente, as “lives” do Discord foram banidos depois do suicídio de uma menina de 13 anos.  




Flávio e a bancada digital já 

avisaram

 que querem reverter todas essas regras. Flávio planeja um “revogaço” dos decretos de Lula que regulamentaram a decisão do STF sobre a responsabilização das plataformas, que estabeleceu a ANPD como agência reguladora. A “bancada da liberdade de expressão digital”, que tem nomes como Carol di Toni, Filipe Barros e Carlos Jordy, do PL, quer que o Congresso defina as responsabilidades da ANPD.     




Só que, no Brasil, a discussão sobre redes sociais e Big Techs ultrapassou, e muito, a esfera do Congresso. É o que mostra o caso da interferência da Meta nas eleições. Arrisco dizer que o Brasil é o único país em que a sociedade tem clareza dos riscos representados pelas Big Techs. Não se trata de um partido, um político ou um punhado de ONGs: é um país se mobilizando para conter os danos da tecno-oligarquia. 




Hoje às 17h, a pressão vai aumentar. Organizações da sociedade civil e movimentos sociais convocam a sociedade para um ato pacífico na sede da Meta, na Faria Lima, em São Paulo.




E agora, volto ao início da minha coluna. 

Se as Big Techs estão de olho nas nossas eleições, o mesmo é verdade para a crescente comunidade de especialistas, legisladores, jornalistas e ativistas que se importam com a batalha mundial da humanidade contra essa oligarquia.

 Com as eleições, o epicentro desta luta volta a ser o Brasil – e isso não vai terminar no domingo, vença quem vencer. O Brasil seguirá tendo um dos movimentos atuantes e mais robustos de pressão e organização cívica para emparedar as Big Techs – um movimento, ouso dizer, irreversível.

author: Alexei Miagkov
title: Announcing Privacy Badger for Safari on macOS
content:
Exciting news for Safari users: Privacy Badger is now available on Safari for macOS! You’ll need Safari version 26.5 or higher to use it.




Whether you want to protect yourself from data brokers or just don’t want Big Tech profiting off your browsing data, Privacy Badger is here to help. More than 4 million people already use EFF’s free tracker-blocking extension to take a stand against online surveillance. Safari users can now join them and EFF in the fight for a better web. 

 




Install Privacy Badger




Support the Fight Against Online Tracking




Safari support has been one of Privacy Badger’s most 

requested

 features for years. Thanks to recent improvements in Safari's extension support, we’ve finally made it happen for Safari version 26.5 and higher. Privacy Badger is now available on all major desktop browsers. And before you ask, yes, we will look into supporting 

Safari for iOS

 once we've ironed out any issues on macOS.




Why Install Privacy Badger on Safari?

 




Most websites

 contain invisible tracking code that lets companies collect, share, and profit from your personal data. Some of those companies are data brokers that sell your information to anyone willing to pay. Creepy ads are just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the harms of online tracking: Once your information enters the data broker ecosystem, it’s nearly impossible to know 

who buys it

 or what they’re doing with it. Privacy Badger blocks online trackers to prevent your browsing data from being used against you. 

 




Privacy Badger goes beyond Safari’s 

built-in privacy features

 to provide additional protection against online tracking. In its default browsing mode, Safari limits the information that trackers can access but still allows them to load. Privacy Badger blocks trackers from loading in the first place, preventing them from tracking you using 

techniques

 that bypass Safari’s protections.

 




Privacy Badger works well by itself, and will continue to enhance your privacy when installed along side an ad blocker or with 

Safari’s Advanced settings

 to 

block trackers in all windows

. Since Privacy Badger 

automatically learns

 to block trackers, Privacy Badger will block trackers that other tools don’t know about or 

choose not to block

.

 




For example, Privacy Badger blocks 

tracking from widgets

 like embedded tweets, comments sections, and video players. These widgets can share your data even if you never click on them. Privacy Badger prevents these trackers from loading and replaces them with 

click-to-activate placeholders

.

 




Beyond tracker blocking, Privacy Badger automatically sends the 

Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal

 to tell websites not to sell or share your personal information. The GPC signal is already legally binding in 

a growing number of states

, including California, Colorado, New Jersey, and Connecticut. 

 




All these features (

and more

) work together to help keep your browsing activity private on Safari.

 




Try It Out and Spread the Word

 




If you use Safari on macOS, give Privacy Badger a try. You’ll install Privacy Badger through the App Store on your macOS device. Installing extensions is a little more complicated on Safari than other browsers, so follow Apple’s 

directions here

 if you’re having trouble. 

 




This is our first release of Privacy Badger for Safari, and we will keep improving it based on your feedback. If you run into any problems, let us know by emailing 

extension-devs@eff.org

, or by opening an issue on 

GitHub

. And if blocking harmful trackers causes issues on a website you visit, you can 

disable Privacy Badger for that specific site

 while keeping it enabled and protecting you everywhere else. You can also let us know about broken sites by using the “Report broken site” button found next to the “Disable for this site” button in Privacy Badger’s popup window.

 




When you use Privacy Badger, you join EFF and millions of other users in the fight for a better web. Help spread the word by telling your friends and family who use Safari that they can use Privacy Badger too! 

 




Install Privacy Badger

 




Support the Fight Against Online Tracking

author: CMI Argentina
title: Se registró una nueva caída del empleo formal en julio: 9085 trabajadores perdieron su puesto
content:
Según datos del Sistema Integrado Previsional Argentino (SIPA), analizados por el investigador del Instituto de Estudios y Formación de la CTA – Autónoma Luis Campos, suman ya 14 meses consecutivos de retroceso del empleo en el sector privado. Agrega que julio fue el mes de mayor destrucción desde noviembre del año pasado, y que en el último año se destruyeron más puestos que en el primer año y medio de gobierno de La Libertad Avanza.




Foto: Indymedia Trabajadoras/es




“La fase de destrucción de empleo formal en el sector privado ya tiene la misma magnitud que la que se produjo en los últimos dos años del gobierno de Cambiemos. La gran diferencia es que en ese momento el sector público funcionaba como amortiguador. Ahora no. A nivel sectorial no se salva nadie, ni siquiera los ganadores del modelo. En el último año minería y petróleo e intermediación financiera destruyeron empleo formal. Agro y pesca tuvieron una suba marginal. Por el contrario, industria y comercio se desplomaron”, detalla Luis Campos.







Agrega que en lo que va de la gestión de La Libertad Avanza el empleo formal solo creció en Neuquén y Río Negro. Entre ambas provincias sumaron 16.723 trabajadores, mientras que en las 22 restantes perdieron su puesto casi 285.000 personas.




“En julio creció bastante el empleo en el sector público, pero posiblemente se trate de un tema metodológico. Había caído fuerte en junio, recuperó todo el deterioro en julio. Contra noviembre de 2023 acumula un retroceso del 2,5%, bien por debajo del sector privado. En casas particulares el empleo formal también cayó en julio, pero como tendencia general parece haberse estabilizado en los niveles de principios de 2025 luego de una caída muy fuerte en los cinco años anteriores”, señala.




En cuanto a los sueldos, Campos explica que el salario real relevado por el SIPA perdió un par de décimas contra la inflación en julio: “Parece haberse estancado a partir de marzo en niveles similares a los de noviembre de 2023. No parece haber ninguna razón para que repunte en el corto plazo”.




“En agosto la Encuesta de Indicadores Laborales registró una caída marginal. Por lo pronto, no hay ninguna señal de que el empleo formal vaya a recuperarse. Veremos hasta cuándo resisten las modalidades refugio, si es que ya no empezaron a agotarse”, finaliza el investigador.
