title: Martyr Welat wanted to be the voice of truth
content:
The early days of the Rojava Revolution saw many people living in Rojava seeking to become the voice of their society and expose the attacks, violations and suffering endured by their people. However, this was no easy task. Journalists who decided to document the realities faced by the people encountered numerous difficulties and dangers. Many lost their lives in pursuit of this mission. Many journalists seeking to document the atrocities committed during the Turkish state's occupation attacks on North and East Syria were targeted, particularly during the attacks on Serêkaniyê and Girê Spî in October 2019. One of them was martyr Vedat (Welat) Erdemci, who remained determined to be the voice of his people and bring the truth about the region to public attention until his final moments.




Journalist Zinar Cafer spoke to ANF about the life and work of journalist Vedat Erdemci, who was martyred during the attacks on Serêkaniyê on 11 October 2019.







Cafer said that a few words could never adequately convey the stories of the martyrs of the free press and added: “Writing books about the martyrs of the press or speaking about them in programmes is not enough on its own. At the beginning of the Rojava Revolution, many people in Kurdistan wanted to become the voice of their society because we witnessed numerous violations and attacks. The Rojava region of Kurdistan was experiencing attacks unlike anything seen elsewhere. Many people wanted to become the voice of this society. Of course, this was not work that everyone could easily undertake. Those capable of revealing the truth were mostly involved in journalism. However, whatever work a person undertakes, there is a price to pay. We take this opportunity to commemorate all the martyrs of the free press with respect. There were journalists in Rojava who succeeded in becoming the voice of truth and society through their pens and cameras until their final moments. When we speak of the martyrs of the press, we must particularly remember those martyred in October. The attacks on Serêkaniyê and Girê Spî took place in 2019. Welat Erdemcî was also martyred during those attacks.”




‘Martyr Welat wanted the world to hear the suffering of the Yazidi people’




Journalist Zinar Cafer said he had the opportunity to meet martyr Welat Ekinci in 2018 and continued: “I consider myself fortunate to have had the opportunity to meet martyr Welat in 2018. I first met him in the Deir ez-Zor region, during the operations to drive ISIS gangs out of the area. I was working in journalism at the time, particularly for Çira TV. The channel operated with the aim of becoming the voice of the Yazidi community. We were producing reports and covering developments, particularly the rescue of Yazidi women, children and other members of the Yazidi community. When I met martyr Welat, everyone was engaged in a race to deliver information as quickly and accurately as possible. Welat and I were almost competing with each other. We were both present when two Yazidi girls were rescued by fighters of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF). The girls said, ‘We are Yazidis.’ Martyr Welat wanted to film the girls for a documentary he was planning to make. We also wanted to prepare a news report about what had happened. 




There was a competition over who could send their footage first and who could finish editing more quickly. We got to know each other through our work. Once we had filmed our footage, our relationship as comrades began to develop. Our comradeship with Colî and Suad also began during that period. Later, after filming together, we went to the Internal Security Forces headquarters. We sat together and talked. Martyr Welat wanted to make a documentary. His aim was to become the voice of the Yazidi community. He wanted to bring the suffering and hardships endured by the Yazidi people, particularly Yazidi women, and the 73rd Ferman (Shengal genocide) to public attention. Through his documentary, he wanted to show how ISIS had committed atrocities against the Yazidi community, what those atrocities involved and the immense suffering people had endured. His aim was to reveal all of this. We worked together on the documentary and completed part of it. Once the two Yazidi girls had been rescued, we travelled to Hasakah (Hesekê). Yazidis were living in the village of Gumer, south of Hasakah. We stayed there together for several days. Once we got to know each other, we began sharing the footage we had filmed and working together. I realised that we both had the same goals and aspirations. That was how we began exchanging footage and information and working together in the area.”




Turkish state attacked a convoy carrying civilians




Zinar Cafer continued by drawing attention to the attacks on civilians, the role of journalists in bringing the truth to public attention and martyr Welat's determination to reach Serêkaniyê. Zinar Cafer said: “The occupying state's brutal attacks on the region began. As is known, the attacks on the cities of Serêkaniyê and Girê Spî were launched on 9 October 2019. Martyr Welat wanted to be the voice of truth. That is why he never lost touch with the people or distanced himself from the people of Serêkaniyê. As we have said before, when a journalist wants to go somewhere and document an event, they can begin directly with the suffering of the people. As we were trying to expose the suffering endured by the people, we saw a civilian convoy heading towards Serêkaniyê. The convoy had set out to support the fighters in Serêkaniyê and to act as human shields. On 12 October, Hevrîn Xelef, co-chair of the Future Syria Party, had also been brutally murdered. Martyr Welat had been trying to reach the place where she was before he was martyred.




However, he was unable to get there because of security conditions, which deeply upset him. We were waiting at the time. As the attacks on the people of Serêkaniyê began, I spoke with martyr Welat before he travelled to the city, and we exchanged the information we had gathered. I asked him to join Çira TV, and he wanted to do so. However, he was unable to join because of the lack of an internet connection and technical difficulties. The convoy that set out from Qamishlo was made up of people from cities across Rojava Kurdistan who wanted to act as human shields in Serêkaniyê. As is known, civilian convoys came under attack on 13 October. Convoys carrying civilians and our comrades working in the press were brutally targeted. Dozens of civilians, including martyr Mihemed and martyr Seed, were martyred in these brutal attacks in Serêkaniyê. Martyr Welat also wanted to document these attacks.”




Free press workers are targeted for documenting the truth




The comrades of Welat Ekinci decided to complete his documentary after he was martyred, determined to fulfil his dreams and aspirations. With the support of director Ararat Sûveyda, they completed the documentary Hêvî (Hope), using footage that had already been filmed. Zinar Cafer said that although some footage was missing, they had managed to continue martyr Welat's work and bring the documentary to completion. Cafer explained that completing the documentary meant more to them than simply continuing a journalistic project. It also meant fulfilling a goal that martyr Welat had worked towards. Cafer said they wanted to fulfil the dreams and aspirations of the martyrs of the free press and bring to public attention the truths they had sought to document. He stressed that journalists who use their cameras and pens to document violations and reveal the realities faced by the people frequently become targets of attacks.




Cafer said journalists sought to inform the public about the conditions faced by the people, the suffering endured by civilians and the crimes committed against them. However, he emphasised that this important responsibility also brought numerous dangers. Journalist Zinar Cafer once again commemorated the martyrs of the free press, including Welat Erdemcî, Dilovan Gever, Nazım Daştan and Cihan Bilgin. He said free press workers continued their efforts to document the truth and become the voice of the people despite all threats and attacks. Numerous civilians and journalists lost their lives in the attacks on civilian convoys on 13 October 2019. Welat Ekinci had also wanted to document these attacks and bring the truth about the conditions faced by the people to public attention. However, he too was martyred during the same period.

author: Unknown
title: Two Iraqi soldiers killed in mine explosion in Kirkuk
content:
An officer and a soldier from the Iraqi army were killed in a mine explosion in Kirkuk on Wednesday. Two other soldiers were injured. The explosion occurred in Wadi Zixêtûn (Zghaitoun), near Reşad (Rashad), when a military vehicle belonging to the 11th Division triggered a previously planted mine.




Among those killed was Ahat Yasir, the division’s communications officer. The unit had been deployed to the area to investigate suspected positions and activities of remaining militants from the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS).




The previous day, the Iraqi Air Force had carried out airstrikes on ISIS positions in the valley south of Kirkuk. The soldiers involved had subsequently been dispatched on a reconnaissance mission.

author: Unknown
title: YPJ: Attack on the images of our martyrs is an assault on the honour and values of our society
content:
The General Command of the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) released a statement condemning the attacks against the images of fallen female fighters in Hesekê.




The YPJ statement on Wednesday said: “Recently, despicable attempts and attacks have targeted images of our martyrs and the sanctity they represent, which are among the most sacred values of our people and our revolution. These attacks, which directly target the dignity of our martyrs, violate the fundamental principles of humanity, moral awareness, and the inviolable red lines of society’s conscience.”




The statement stressed that: “Our martyrs are our identity, our honour, and the most sacred values underpinning our existence. Those who were defeated by the will and resistance of free women are now attacking our martyrs through inhumane methods that go beyond all standards of human morality. These immoral scenes and despicable acts are in no way befitting our people or our homeland. Such attacks constitute a direct assault on the honour and values of our entire society.”




The YPJ General Command called on the Damascus government to assume its responsibility, take immediate action against these inhumane acts, and hold those responsible fully accountable to the fullest extent possible. YPJ vowed that: “We will not remain silent in the face of these attacks, and no violation of the sanctity of our martyrs will go unanswered or unaccounted for.”




The statement concluded: “We call on all members of our nation, particularly women and young people, to remain vigilant against this psychological warfare, take a firm stand against these immoral scenes, safeguard our dignity, and stand united in solidarity with our martyrs. We will remain steadfast in defending the honour, dignity, and identity of our martyrs until the very end.”

author: Unknown
title: Families condemn the attack on the images of martyrs: We will continue on the path of our martyrs
content:
Rojin Mohammad, a founding member of the Martyrs’ Families Foundation in Kobanê, expressed her dismay at the attacks targeting images of martyrs in Hesekê, stating, “We will not accept such immoral acts.”




Rojin Mohammad explained that, for several days, certain groups have been systematically spreading chaos in the al-Khuwairan neighbourhood of Hesekê and attacking images of the martyrs.




“This is an attack on all peoples”




Speaking about the attacks, Rojin Mohammad said: “These martyrs sacrificed their lives for the freedom of Syrian soil and to protect all peoples from massacres. Attacking their images is not an attack on their families alone; it is an attack on all our values. This is a clear violation of the law.”




“The aim is to derail the integration process”




Mohammad pointed out that the aim of these attacks is to undermine the integration process in Syria. She continued: “This chaos and recklessness will not allow Syria to achieve integration or reach a positive outcome. On the contrary, these acts are an attempt to obstruct the integration process. The Syrian state must take notice of these attacks, put an end to these acts of sabotage, and hold those responsible accountable.”




“We will continue on their path”




Rojin Mohammad concluded her message by saying: “A democratic and free Syria must be built through the joint efforts of all its components. As mothers, we say that we will remain committed to the path of our martyrs until the very end. Martyrs never die.”

author: Unknown
title: There’s probably some weird corner of the internet where “marginalized people need to have…
content:
I really, really don’t think “My turbo-principled position is that because marginalized groups are sometimes maligned as sexual predators, marginalized people need to have solidarity with confessed actual sexual predators!” is a good hill to die on for anybody.

Guys who use their privilege to actually do this stuff don’t need any more people standing up for them. They’ve already got mainstream society making excuses and ensuring that their rights are protected in ways that, say, for example, a trans woman accused of having a bit of a bad vibe could never even dream of.

As a person who’s considered guilty even when proven innocent, you aren’t going to reap any benefits from defending someone who’s already treated like he’s innocent despite being proven guilty.

There’s probably some weird corner of the internet where “marginalized people need to have solidarity with confessed actual sexual predators” is an actual opinion that some people have, but I’ve never really encountered that opinion ever.

What I have encountered far far more is

Because this marginalized group is so often maligned as sexual predators, they will sometimes be convicted as sexual predators, therefore our solidarity should include convicted sexual predators, as some are innocent and we can’t tell which ones they are.

Because this marginalized group is so often a victim of abuse and abuse is often cyclical, some will complete the cycle of abuse and will become abusers. Therefor our compassion should include people who have committed abuse because only with support can we break the cycle of abuse.

We should stand in solidarity with all incarcerated people, no matter how terrible their wrongdoings, because prison abolition and transformative justice for all is the only path to a truly free and just society.

And other variations of that, which then get twisted as “so you think we should have solidarity with confessed actual sexual predators?”, when like, that was not the point.

title: Carcere di Torino: cimici dei letti e condizioni degradanti. Il diario di un detenuto racconta la realtà del carcere
content:
Ieri è stato sollevato in Consiglio Regionale il problema delle cimici dei letti all’interno della sezione maschile del carcere di Torino. La questione è uscita grazie a dei fogli di diario, alcuni passaggi sono stati letti anche in seduta di Consiglio. 




Noi li abbiamo ricevuti da alcuni detenuti e di seguito li ripubblichiamo integralmente.




diario cimici

Download




Ne avevamo già parlato 

qui

 quando, a seguito di racconti di detenuti, abbiamo avuto la possibilità di fare uscire il tema. Erano coinvolti sicuramente il Blocco B e la decima sezione in particolare. Ma, stando alle ricostruzioni, sembra molto probabile un’infestazione del magazzino dei materassi del carcere, oltre che delle celle.




Da allora non è stata fatta alcuna azione per migliorare le condizioni. 




In questa intervista su 

Radio Blackout

 Giorgio, da poco uscito dal carcere per termine di sconto della pena, racconta in maniera dettagliata la situazione. 




Giorgio Rossetto

, militante di lunga data dell’Autonomia torinese e della resistenza No Tav, è recentemente uscito dall’ennesimo periodo di detenzione, scattato il 22 agosto 2026 con la revoca degli arresti domiciliari.




Grazie al suo contributo cerchiamo di osservare la situazione attuale all’interno del carcere delle Vallette a Torino, tra processi di deumanizzazione, autolesionismo e suicidi, disperazione dilagante e sofferenza sociale:







Qui il video in cui la consigliera regionale Alice Ravinale solleva la questione

 







Anche al Tg Regionale di martedì 13 ottobre è passato un servizio sulle condizioni del carcere di Torino.







Ciò che già scrivevamo qualche settimana fa “Chissà se il Sindaco Lo Russo, il Presidente della Regione Cirio o il ministro della Giustizia Nordio se ne fregheranno altamente anche questa volta. Certo è che i detenuti e le detenute devono aver riconosciuta la loro dignità e molte volte trovano anche da soli il modo per farla rispettare, come successo nei giorni scorsi nel carcere Don Bosco di Pisa” possiamo riproporlo senza modifiche a riprova dell’inerzia e totale disinteresse delle istituzioni a fronte di una situazione gravissima.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Propaganda Show": IDF Raids Palestinian NGOs in the West Bank Ahead of Israeli Elections
content:
Israeli forces have raided what they say are the offices of several Palestinian NGOs in the occupied West Bank. Palestinian officials say a child was injured from Israeli gunfire, while others suffered from tear gas inhalation. At least one journalist was reportedly detained in the raids, which come four years after the forced closure of multiple NGOs that the Israeli government designated as “terrorist” organizations.




“This is part of the whole propaganda show that this government is actually implementing just before the Israeli election,” says human rights lawyer Sahar Francis. “They just wanted to cause harassment, and this is the main message: the persecution and the collective punishment for the whole Palestinian community.” Francis was formerly the general director at Addameer Prisoner Support and Human Rights Association, one of the organizations that Israel claims to have raided this week despite the fact that it was already forced to close its West Bank offices in 2022.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Bogus": Minnesota State Senator Zaynab Mohamed on DHS Raid on Rep. Ilhan Omar's D.C. Home
content:
On Monday, federal agents from the Department of Homeland Security raided the Washington, D.C., home of Congressmember Ilhan Omar. Omar has faced years of racist targeting from President Trump over her ethnicity and immigrant background. She immigrated to the United States as a refugee from Somalia when she was a child. Omar is the first Somali American elected to federal office, the first woman of color to represent Minnesota and, along with Michigan’s Rashida Tlaib, one of the first Muslim women to serve in Congress.




“Congresswoman Omar has been under attack by this administration for the last decade. … She’s a symbol of everything that this administration hates: an immigrant who stands up for her community, who fought to be here in this country, and now is doing her job and her duty to serve her constituents,” says our guest Zaynab Mohamed, a fellow Somali immigrant who represents Minneapolis in Minnesota’s state Senate. As Trump spews racist invective against the Somali American community in Minnesota, Mohamed says, “We will continue to do everything we can to reject this type of hate and rhetoric from this administration.”

author: David S. D'Amato
title: Jalan Libertarian Menuju Egalitarianisme
content:
Oleh: 

David S. D’Amato

. Teks aslinya berjudul “

The Libertarian Road to Egalitarianism

”. Diterjemahkan ke Bahasa Indonesia oleh Taratsa.




Sebuah studi terbaru dari 

National Bureau of Economic Research

 yang dilakukan Emmanuel Saez dan Gabriel Zucman

 menemukan bahwa “

0,1% keluarga [di Amerika Serikat] yang berada di puncak distribusi kekayaan kini memiliki bagian kekayaan yang kira-kira sama dengan 90% keluarga yang berada di bagian terbawah.

” Lebih jauh, studi tersebut menunjukkan bahwa “pemulihan” ekonomi yang terus kita dengar ternyata belum sampai kepada kelas menengah. Hanya mereka yang berada di puncak piramida ekonomi yang benar-benar menikmati manfaatnya.




Ketika sebagian kecil penduduk menimbun begitu banyak kekayaan negara, para pakar kebijakan dan akademisi sibuk mencari pihak yang harus disalahkan sekaligus menawarkan berbagai solusi. Seperti yang bisa diduga, pasar bebas kemudian menjadi sasaran kritik sebagai sumber semakin lebarnya ketimpangan kekayaan dan pendapatan. Sebagai pendukung deregulasi dan pasar bebas, kaum libertarian sering dituduh hidup dalam dunia fantasi dan menutup mata terhadap persoalan ketimpangan.




Kami, kaum libertarian, sebenarnya ikut memperburuk keadaan. Ketika persoalan ini tak terhindarkan muncul, terlalu banyak dari kami justru terlihat gelisah dan bersikap defensif dengan bersikeras bahwa ketimpangan 

sama sekali bukan

 masalah, bahwa yang seharusnya kita lihat adalah standar hidup atau ukuran lainnya. “Kapitalisme sangat baik bagi orang miskin—sumpah!” Kaum libertarian harus menerima kenyataan yang pahit bahwa ketimpangan memang merupakan persoalan yang sangat besar.




Namun, kita tidak perlu memandang ketimpangan sebagai titik lemah dalam argumen kita mengenai kebebasan ekonomi, atau sebagai persoalan yang tidak mungkin kita menangkan. Hubungan ekonomi yang ada saat ini bukanlah hasil dari kebebasan pertukaran maupun kepemilikan pribadi yang sah. Justru kaum libertarian berada pada posisi yang kuat dalam persoalan ketimpangan. Kebebasan dan kesetaraan pada kenyataannya saling melengkapi dan memperkuat satu sama lain; yang pertama secara alamiah menghasilkan yang kedua.




Kaum anarkis individualis seperti Lysander Spooner berpendapat bahwa “ekstrem dalam kekayaan maupun kemiskinan” merupakan hasil dari “legislasi positif”, yakni ketika hukum-hukum arbitrer menggantikan hukum alam dan “menciptakan monopoli serta privilese”. Dalam kapitalisme, menurut Spooner, pemilik modal memperoleh kekuasaan khusus dalam perekonomian—kekuasaan yang tidak ada hubungannya dengan kebebasan sederhana untuk memproduksi, bertukar, dan berkompetisi. Jika dilihat secara menyeluruh, intervensi negara pada akhirnya menguntungkan orang-orang kaya dan mereka yang memiliki koneksi politik, yakni elite ekonomi yang mempunyai akses khusus kepada mereka yang membuat dan menjalankan aturan yang harus kita semua patuhi.




Intervensi-intervensi tersebut memang tidak selalu sempurna, dan sistem kapitalisme monopoli di negara ini tentu dilapisi dengan berbagai kebijakan yang secara formal dimaksudkan untuk melindungi pekerja, konsumen, dan masyarakat miskin. Namun, tidak satu pun kebijakan tersebut mengubah tujuan mendasar intervensi negara: merampas hak para pemilik yang sah dan menempatkan massa masyarakat dalam posisi bergantung pada para pemberi kerja. Singkatnya, tujuan historis negara adalah perang kelas yang permanen, yakni penggunaan kekuasaan negara untuk melindungi sebuah kelas bangsawan sosial-ekonomi.




Karena itu, kaum kiri sebenarnya cukup tepat dalam persoalan ketimpangan, meskipun mereka cenderung keliru dalam memahami kebebasan, hak-hak individual, dan pasar. Kaum anarkis pasar menghendaki 

keduanya

, kebebasan dan kesetaraan, dengan memperjuangkan masyarakat tanpa negara yang menjadikan kesetaraan dalam kebebasan dan otoritas sebagai hukum tertingginya.




Persaingan yang benar-benar terbuka merupakan kekuatan yang membubarkan sekaligus menyebarkan konsentrasi kekuasaan. Kaum libertarian seharusnya berhenti mencari-cari alasan untuk membenarkan ketimpangan yang luar biasa besar saat ini, seolah-olah kita sampai pada kondisi ini melalui 

laissez-faire

 dan kedaulatan individu.




Seluruh hasil publikasi didanai sepenuhnya oleh donasi. Jika kalian menyukai karya-karya kami, kalian dapat berkontribusi dengan berdonasi. Temukan petunjuk tentang cara melakukannya di halaman Dukung C4SS: 

https://c4ss.org/dukung-c4ss.

author: Unknown
title: Hatimoğulları'ndan Halk TV'ye dayanışma ziyareti: "Basını sansürlemekten vazgeçin"
content:
DEM Parti Eş Genel Başkanı Tülay Hatimoğulları, Parti Sözcüsü Ayşegül Doğan ve beraberindeki heyet, kayyum atanan Halk TV’nin Ankara temsilciliğine destek ziyaretinde bulundu.

Ziyaret sonrası açıklama yapan Hatimoğulları, kayyum atamasını kınadığını vurgulayarak şöyle konuştu:

"Heyetimizle birlikte sabahleyin aldığımız haber üzerine hızla buraya geldik. İstanbul'daki gelişmeleri takip ediyoruz. Halk TV'ye bir şafak operasyonuyla yüzlerce polisin baskın yapması asla kabul edilebilir bir şey değil. Kayyum rejimi bu ülkede parça parça tesis edildi. Belediyeler üzerinden başladı ve artık Türkiye'de kayyum atanmayan hiçbir şey kalmadı. Ticari kurumlardan tutalım da üniversitelere kadar ve bundan şu anda en çok muzdarip olan, gerçekten Türkiye'deki basın yayın kuruluşlarıdır, organlarıdır. Bunu kabul etmek mümkün değil. Halk TV'ye yapılan bu saldırıyı bir kez daha burada sizlerin huzurunda kınıyoruz.

Bir televizyonu yüzlerce polisle basmak demek, Türkiye'yi çok karanlık bir dehlize doğru hızla sürüklemek demektir ve biz buna defaatle tanıklık ettik. Bundan önce TELE1'de oldu ve son zamanlarda birçok kanalda gerçekleşti. Bugün şayet televizyonun sahibiyle ilgili başlatılmak istenen bir soruşturma varsa bu soruşturma televizyon kanalı kapatılarak yapılmaz. Burada televizyon kanalının kendi yayın akışına devam etmesine hiçbir şekilde müdahale etmeksizin bir soruşturma açılacaksa o soruşturma açılır. Ortada bir suç varsa onun gereklilikleri yerine getirilir. Ama ne yazık ki Türkiye'de artık bir şeye bahane üretmek için, basını sansürlemek, ekranları karartmak, kalemleri ve tuşları susturmak için önceden hazırlanmış olan hikâyeleri ortaya atıp, gerekçeler oluşturup toplumu böyle ikna edeceğini sanıyor bu iktidar. Ama yanılıyor. Bugün Halk TV'nin Türkiye'de milyonlarca izleyicisi var. Dolayısıyla milyonlarca izleyiciyi bu anlamıyla bu iktidarın yanıltamayacağını, bu şekilde bir karartmanın üstünün örtülemeyeceğini bilmesi gerekiyor. Bugün Türkiye'de tepkiler çok büyük. Bugün insanların duygusal olarak da siyasi olarak da toplumsal olarak da tepkileri son derece büyük."

Hatimoğulları, günlerdir Türkiye'nin gündemini meşgul eden fon kriziyle ilgili TBMM'de komisyon görüşmelerinin başladığına işaret ederek, şöyle devam etti:

"Böylesi bir zamanda televizyon ekranlarının karartılması aynı zamanda bu yolsuzlukların, yüzyılın fon vurgununun üzerini örtmek anlamına da geliyor. Çünkü bu anlamıyla muhalif olan bütün basını susturmak, mevcut olan iktidarla ilgili tek bir negatif yorum yapılmasına izin vermemek demek, bu dünyada görülmemiş bir basın sansürüdür. Kendi işlenen suçların üzerini örtmek için yargı yoluna başvurarak Türkiye'deki çeşitli kurumların, iktidarın elindeki kurumların devreye sokulmasıyla bu operasyonların gerçekleşmesi asla kabul edilebilir değildir. Buradan bir kez daha diyoruz ki Halk TV ekranlarını karartamazsınız. Yurttaşın haber alma hakkına müdahale edemezsiniz. Basının özgürce haber yapma hakkını elinden alamazsınız. Burada yapılan bu operasyon, şafak operasyonu ve yayın akışına doğrudan müdahale asla kabul edilemez. Bu müdahale Türkiye'deki milyonlarca yurttaşın haber alma hakkına yapılmış bir müdahaledir. Biz Halk TV'yle ve bütün Halk TV ailesiyle dayanışma içindeyiz. Sonuna kadar basın özgürlüğü için mücadele edeceğiz.

İnsanların ya da kurumların sosyal medya erişim hesaplarının engellenmesi, bu susturmaya eklenen yeni halkalar. Neredeyse her gün yüzlerce X hesabının engellendiğine, sosyal medya erişim engelinin olduğuna tanıklık ediyoruz. Bunları biz asla kabul etmiyoruz. Türkiye böyle manzaraları askerî darbe dönemlerinde görmüştür. Bu kadar ekranın karartıldığını, Kenan Evren'le bütünleşmiş olan 'gazeteler makas makas' dediği, böyle formüle edilen anlayışa biz şimdi ne yazık ki en ağır şekliyle bir kez daha tanıklık ediyoruz. Halk TV ailesine bir kez daha geçmiş olsun dileklerimizi iletiyoruz. Dayanışma içinde olduğumuzu bir kez daha ifade ediyoruz ve iktidara buradan net olarak sesleniyoruz. Basını sansürlemekten artık vazgeçin. Türkiye'yi karanlık bir tabloya sürüklemekten artık vazgeçin. Basını özgür olmayan bir ülkede özgürlükten ve demokrasiden asla bahsedilemez. Dayanışma içinde olmaya devam edeceğiz.

Şimdi biz burada bu konuşmamızı gerçekleştirirken arkadaşlarım aktardı. Polis şimdi Halk TV'nin Ankara ofisinin kapısına gelmiş durumda. Kuvvetle muhtemel İstanbul'da yaptıkları aramanın, taramanın, hukuki olmayan, yeri olmayan aramanın, taramanın birini daha galiba burada gerçekleştirecekler. Şimdi birazdan daha fazla bilgi sahibi olacağız. Kolluk kuvvetiyle güç uygulayarak gerçekleşen bu operasyonlar kelimenin tam anlamıyla antidemokratiktir. Kayyum rejimini tahkim etmektir. Kayyum rejimini kalıcı hale getirmektir. Bunu asla kabul etmiyoruz."

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Orange Blossom Türkiye’ye geliyor: İstanbul ve Ankara’da sahne alacak
content:
Fransa çıkışlı elektronik müzik ve dünya müziği kolektifi Orange Blossom, ekim ayında İstanbul ve Ankara’da konser verecek. Elektronik altyapıları Orta Doğu ezgileri, Arapça vokaller ve geleneksel enstrümanlarla buluşturan grup, Türkiye’deki dinleyicileriyle bir araya gelecek.

1990’lı yıllardan bu yana müzik üreten ve Fransa’nın Nantes kentinde kurulan Orange Blossom, elektronik müzik ile farklı coğrafyaların geleneksel müzikal unsurlarını bir araya getiriyor. Trip-hop ve dünya müziği ekseninde üretim yapan kolektifin müziğinde Orta Doğu ezgileri, yaylılar, ritmik döngüler ve elektronik beat’ler öne çıkıyor. Meksika, Mısır ve Fransa gibi farklı ülkelerden müzisyenleri bir araya getiren grup, farklı müzik geleneklerinden beslenen bir sound oluşturuyor.

Orange Blossom’ın Türkiye’deki dinleyici kitlesiyle kurduğu bağda Türk müziğine ve sufi geleneğine duyduğu ilgi de etkili. Grup, özellikle Konya’da verdiği konserlerin ardından yaptığı açıklamalarda Mevlana’nın şehriyle kurduğu bağa ve sufi müziğin kendileri üzerindeki etkisine değindi. Ney ve saz gibi geleneksel enstrümanlara duydukları ilgiyi de dile getiren kolektif, bu müzikal unsurları kendi üretimlerinde elektronik altyapılarla bir araya getiriyor.

Grubun Türkiye’de geniş bir dinleyici kitlesine ulaşmasında “Ya Sidi” adlı parçası da etkili oldu. Parçanın “Çukur” dizisinde kullanılması, Orange Blossom’ın Türkiye’de daha fazla tanınmasına katkı sağladı.

Orange Blossom’ın müziğinde elektronik ritimler; Arapça vokaller, yaylılar ve farklı coğrafyalardan gelen geleneksel ezgilerle birleşiyor. Bu müzikal yapı, grubun canlı performanslarının da temelini oluşturuyor.

Kolektif, ekim ayında İstanbul ve Ankara’da vereceği konserlerde elektronik müzik ile dünya müziğini buluşturan repertuvarını dinleyicilerle paylaşacak.

Konserlerde kapı açılışı saat 20.00’de, performans başlangıcı ise saat 22.00’de yapılacak.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Kay Pacha / Equipo Pueblos Originarios del SERPAJ
title: Lecko Zamora: una voz Wichí por el 12 de octubre
content:
Y llegamos una vez más al 12 de octubre, fecha muy simbólica y oportuna para hacer recordar que significó y significa para los pueblos originarios, que fue el comienzo de una invasión, un genocidio y un sistema colonizante en todo sentido.










https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/12-de-octubre.mp3




https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/12-de-octubre.mp3




Descargar archivo




Pero ahora, a pesar que se quiera volver al Día de la Raza, los hermanos y hermanas aprovechan la oportunidad para hace oír sus voces, sus reclamos y en general denunciar la situación de racismo, violencia y despojo territorial que vienen sufriendo.







Por eso en esta oportunidad han tenido lugar a lo largo y ancho de nuestro país, numerosos actos, movilizaciones  y marchas en donde se manifestaron las denuncias y reclamos por estas situaciones.







Uno de los reclamos urgentes en estos momentos es el cese de los desalojos de comunidades de diversos pueblos y territorios. Todos los documentos que se conocieron por estos días difunden ampliamente la difícil situación que están atravesando varias comunidades, como ser la Lof Melo en la Provincia de Neuquén.







Afortunadamente la existencia de estas movilizaciones revela el espíritu de resistencia y lucha de las comunidades, que utilizan todas las herramientas necesarias en su defensa y contra un aparato jurídico y represivo que  responde a los intereses de quienes ambicionan sus territorios para sus ambiciones de lucro y de explotación de sus bienes naturales.







Todas estas situaciones denunciadas son bien conocidas y siempre las difundimos, pero en esta oportunidad queremos compartirle algo diferente, algo que si bien es una denuncia en general, está hecha con una hermosa y poética presentación.







Presentamos la voz de Lecko Zamora, escritor, artista, gestor cultural y referente de la cultura wichí, quien expresa en forma muy personal lo que todos venimos denunciando sobre el 12 de octubre.







El Micro Kay Pacha se realiza con el apoyo de la organización Otto per Mille-Chiessa Valdense.

Lecko Zamora: una voz Wichí por el 12 de octubre

title: Διήμερη εκδήλωση της Κοινότητας Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών στο Πάντειο, 24 & 25/10
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης: 

Διήμερη εκδήλωση της Κοινότητας Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών στο Πάντειο, 24 & 25/10










Οι εκδηλώσεις του διημέρου θα μεταδοθούν από το OmniaTV

:







YouTube




PeerTube




Facebook
















Ανοιχτό κάλεσμα προς την κοινωνία




Χωρίς τη συλλογική δράση, οι ιδέες κοιμούνται στα κεφάλια και στις βιβλιοθήκες. Η γέννηση της πολιτικής ελευθερίας συμβαδίζει με τον αγώνα για τη συλλογική ιδιοποίηση της θεσμίζουσας αρχής.




— Eduardo Colombo




Ως Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών καθ’ όλη τη διάρκεια του πολύμηνου και πολυεπίπεδου αγώνα ενάντια στα τελευταία σχέδια του κράτους και του κεφαλαίου βαδίσαμε και αγωνιστήκαμε πλάι πλάι με τους συντρόφους μας απεργούς πείνας μέχρι θανάτου Αριστοτέλη Χαντζή και Suzon Doppagne και από κοινού με όλους τους ανθρώπους των κινημάτων και της αλληλεγγύης. Ανθρώπους από ευρύτερες κοινωνικές ομάδες που αναγνώρισαν αυτόν τον αγώνα της Κοινότητας ως έναν συλλογικό αγώνα της κοινωνίας που αφορά όλες και όλους, συγκροτώντας ένα ευρύ κοινωνικό μέτωπο.




Και όπως αγωνιστήκαμε συλλογικά, νικήσαμε και συλλογικά!




Έχοντας κλείσει λοιπόν τον πρώτο μεγάλο κύκλο νικηφόρα, είναι ξεκάθαρο πως αυτό που έχουμε να υπερασπιστούμε δεν είναι μόνο αυτή η συγκεκριμένη νίκη ή μια ρωγμή που αποτέλεσε μια στιγμή στον χρόνο ή μια αυτοαναφορική συνθήκη εντός της οποίας βρίσκει τον εαυτό της η Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών. Η παρακαταθήκη αυτού του αγώνα και της νίκης στο παρόν και το μέλλον απλώνεται μπροστά μας αναδεικνύοντας μια τεράστια δυνατότητα: Να ξαναχτίσουμε το συλλογικό φαντασιακό του κόσμου της αλληλεγγύης, της καθημερινής αντίστασης απέναντι στην εξαθλίωση, τον φόβο, την υποταγή, την εξατομίκευση, αντιτάσσοντας την αυτοθέσμιση των κοινωνιών μας και τη συγκρότηση κοινοτήτων, οπουδήποτε οι άνθρωποι αγωνίζονται, στις γειτονιές, σε πόλεις και χωριά, στους χώρους δουλειάς, στα σχολεία και τα πανεπιστήμια, στον δημόσιο χώρο.




Υπό αυτό το πρίσμα καλούμε σε μία διήμερη εκδήλωση στις 24 και 25 Οκτώβρη στις 17.00 στο Πάντειο Πανεπιστήμιο, (Νέο Κτήριο, Αίθουσα Σάκη Καράγιωργα Ι) για να συζητήσουμε πάνω στους κεντρικούς άξονες που δομήθηκε ο αγώνας αυτός, στις διαφορετικές μεθόδους και στα εργαλεία που χρησιμοποιήσαμε, καθώς και να δούμε συλλογικά και συνολικά τα σημεία που οδήγησαν στη νίκη αλλά και τις αδυναμίες, τις αστοχίες και τα λάθη που υπήρξαν. Αλλά κυρίως να εστιάσουμε στη συλλογική δυνατότητα που ανοίχτηκε μέσω αυτού του αγώνα και που πρέπει να διευρύνουμε. Να ενώσουμε τις αντιστάσεις μας για να δημιουργήσουμε τους όρους μιας κοινής δύναμης και να μετατρέψουμε την αλληλεγγύη από αντανακλαστικό σε σταθερή κοινωνική σχέση. Γιατί οι αγώνες κερδίζονται όταν συναντιούνται και όταν αναγνωρίζουν και συμπληρώνουν ο ένας τον άλλον.




Την πρώτη μέρα της εκδήλωσης, στο πλαίσιο ενός πρώτου απολογισμού, θα παρουσιαστεί από πλευράς της Κοινότητας η επιλογή του συγκεκριμένου αγώνα υπό τις συγκεκριμένες συνθήκες, οι πυλώνες πάνω στους οποίους οικοδομήθηκε, οι μέθοδοι και τα εργαλεία που χρησιμοποιήθηκαν, με αιχμή την απεργίας πείνας ως βασικό επαναστατικό μέσο για την επίτευξη της νίκης, καθώς επίσης και τα πρώτα συμπεράσματα και η προοπτική που ανοίγεται για το επόμενο διάστημα. Θα ακολουθήσουν διευκρινιστικές ερωτήσεις από τους παρευρισκόμενους, που θα απαντηθούν από την Κοινότητα, προκειμένου να προετοιμαστεί το έδαφος για την επόμενη ημέρα της εκδήλωσης.




Τη δεύτερη μέρα συλλογικότητες, οργανώσεις και ατομικότητες θα προβούν σε τοποθετήσεις, συμπεράσματα και απολογισμό του αγώνα, της στρατηγικής και των τακτικών του, καθώς και σε κριτικές αλλά και προτάσεις για τη συνέχεια.




Σας περιμένουμε όλες και όλους




—

Ή θα νικήσουμε ή θα νικήσουμε / Either we will win or we will win,

Συνέλευση Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών (ΣΥ.ΚΑ.ΠΡΟ.) / Assembly of Squatted Prosfygika (SY.KA.PRO.)

title: EMEP MDK Üyesi Şükran Doğan’a ‘NATO’ soruşturması
content:
Ankara — Emek Partisi (EMEP) MDK Üyesi Şükran Doğan, 7-8 Temmuz’da Ankara’da gerçekleşen 36. NATO Zirvesi’ne dair sosyal medya paylaşımları nedeniyle “halkı kin ve düşmanlığa tahrik” suçlamasıyla ifade verdi.

Emek Partisi İstanbul ve Ankara il örgütlerinin, Emek Gençliğinin ve gazetemiz Evrensel’in NATO Zirvesi’ne ve NATO gözaltılarına dair X paylaşımlarını yeniden paylaşan Doğan, Eryaman Karakolu’nda ifade verdi.

“Partimin paylaşımlarını retweet’lediğim için ifade verdim” diyen Doğan, Ankara’da uzun yıllar il yöneticiliği yaptığını da hatırlattı. “NATO zirvesinin üzerinden neredeyse 3 ayı aşkın bir süre geçti. Hâlâ NATO’yla ilgili sosyal medya paylaşımlarının soruşturma konusu yapılıyor olması ilginç. Cezaevinde onlarca NATO tutuklusu var” diyen Doğan, “Bu nasıl bir öfke” diye sordu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

David Sirotafounder and editor-in-chief of The Lever.

"Master Plan: The Hidden Plot to Legalize Corruption in America"

The midterm elections are in less than three weeks, on November 3. With Republican majorities in both chambers of Congress on the line, the Trump administration has thrown its time and resources into holding rallies in newly competitive states. We take a look at key Senate races in Georgia, Texas, Michigan and Maine with The Lever’s David Sirota. Ultimately, says Sirota, election results will hinge on voter turnout. “Will there be that surge of turnout based on how unpopular Trump is and how bad the affordability crisis is?” And, if they win, can Democrats then “deliver” on their promises?

David Sirotafounder and editor-in-chief of The Lever.

"Master Plan: The Hidden Plot to Legalize Corruption in America"

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now! I’m Amy Goodman.

With the midterm elections less than three weeks away, could the Democrats win back control of the House and the Senate? Election Day is November 3rd. Democracy Now! will be doing a four-hour broadcast from 8:00 to midnight Eastern Time that day. But at least 47 states and Washington, D.C., have early voting, with voters already casting ballots in some states. All 435 House seats and 33 Senate seats are on the ballot, in addition to some statewide races and ballot measures.

The list of battleground Senate states has been growing. As many as 10 Senate seats could be flipped, including several states that have been longtime deep-red Republican seats. Competitive races now include Ohio, Alaska, Texas and Kansas. Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the Senate in nearly a century. To win the Senate, Democrats need to flip four Republican seats and hold three of their own. They must hold Michigan, where Dr. Abdul El-Sayed is running against Republican Mike Rogers for an open seat.

President Trump’s been on the campaign trail. He spoke at a rally in Wasilla, Alaska, Tuesday, where incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan is facing off against Democratic challenger Mary Peltola, former congressmember and tribal judge. If she and Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota and Deb Haaland, running for governor in New Mexico, to win, it would be a historic three Native American women in the governorships and the Senate. This is President Trump speaking in Alaska.

PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: On November 3rd, we’re going to send one of the best and most respected senators in D.C., Dan Sullivan, the real — the real Dan Sullivan. … I’m talking about the real Dan Sullivan, not the fake Dan Sullivan, not the Dan Sullivan put up by the “Dumocrats.” … I want you to do me one big favor: pretend that I’m on the ballot. Because here’s what happens: Every time I’ve been on the ballot, we win. … So, in conclusion, if you elect a Republican House and a Republican Senate November 3rd, you get $5,000.

AMY GOODMAN: Key issues raised by challengers and voters have been the economy, the war in Iran, the cost of gas, immigration, data centers and corruption.

To discuss all this and more, we’re joined by David Sirota, founder and editor-in-chief of The Lever. He’s author of Master Plan: The Hidden Plot to Legalize Corruption in America.

Why don’t we go through a number of the states, beginning in Georgia, David, and talk about the overall picture? What’s at stake here? As we talk, President Trump is surprising many by going through this deep-red state tour, which indicates he is fearful of losing not only the House, but the Senate, and, of course, what that could mean for, for example, investigations of him.

DAVID SIROTA: Yeah, I mean, it’s kind of incredible that Trump is out on the campaign trail, in particular in red states, in the sense that he is helping turn the election into even more of a referendum on himself when he is deeply unpopular in polls. So, in a sense, I think, at one level, he is doing the Democrats a big favor by being so extra visible in the states where the Democrats are trying to expand the map. You know, states like Kansas, states — even potentially, if you believe polls, states like South Carolina appear to be in play, the Democrats challenging in the polls there. Florida also a pretty red state.

You mentioned Georgia. Georgia is a different situation, where that’s a state where the Democrats have to hold that state. There’s an incumbent, Jon Ossoff, there. Georgia, a real purple state. And Ossoff has done a fantastic job of turning the race into a referendum on his own Republican challenger. His Republican challenger is a member of Congress. So, he has essentially turned the race into — in an anti-incumbent year, he has effectively tried to, and I think succeeded at, turning the race into a referendum on his opponent and made his opponent out to be, effectively, the incumbent, Mike Collins. And he’s brought up Collins’ association with people who are linked to white nationalism.

But across all of these races, I do think —

AMY GOODMAN: Let me go to — I want to play a clip of Jon Ossoff, the current Democratic senator, speaking to supporters in Athens, Georgia, last month.

SEN. JON OSSOFF: Five days after his father was reelected, Prince Don Jr. becomes a partner at 1789 Capital, a venture firm founded by right-wing activists and Trump donors. 1789 Capital then buys a stake in Vulcan Elements, a tiny startup that says it plans to produce the high-tech magnets needed in drones, missiles and satellites.

And about a month after Don Jr.'s venture firm buys its stake in Vulcan Elements, Pentagon officials learn that Peter Navarro, a convicted criminal, Don Jr. close friend and a top White House official, wants the Pentagon to give your tax dollars to Vulcan Elements. One Pentagon official said, quote, “The call came from the White House. We have to get this done.” And, Athens, to be clear, getting this done means funneling your money to the president's son’s investment.

And so, of course, like clockwork, on November 21st, just three months after Don Jr. and his friends bought their stake, Vulcan gets a $620 million taxpayer loan from Pete Hegseth’s Pentagon, paid for with your money. See, while the world burns and you pay more for everything, your tax dollars become the royal family’s wealth, because it pays to be a Trump, especially when the whole world knows daddy’s a crook.

AMY GOODMAN: That’s Jon Ossoff. He faced off last night in a debate, and one of the major issues that was raised is: Is he running for Senate, or is he running for president? And that’s true of a number of the people who are running for governorships or Senate, David Sirota.

DAVID SIROTA: Yeah, I mean, that’s a big question for Jon Ossoff. And I think in that clip, I think it’s important to note that what Ossoff is doing there, I think pretty successfully, and you’ve seen this with James Talarico and some others — James Talarico running in Texas — is trying to connect the corruption issue with the affordability crisis. And this is a key theme that we talked about in Master Plan, our — The Lever's podcast, where the corruption issue for many years has been a kind of abstraction. People don't like corruption. People understand the government — there’s a lot of corruption in the government, but that it becomes a much more salient issue when people have a better understanding of how the corruption is raising their prices and creating the affordability crisis. Ossoff has made that a central theme. James Talarico, running for Senate against Ken Paxton in Texas, has made that a central theme, tracing the donations that Paxton has gotten to his votes to expand data centers.

AMY GOODMAN: David, I want to play a clip. This was an ad released by James Talarico, who is ahead. And this is the first time in decades a Democrat ahead of the Republican in the race for Senate. This is James Talarico’s ad.

JAMES TALARICO: Twelve million dollars. That’s how much Ken Paxton’s corruption has cost Texas taxpayers in legal fees and settlements. Guys like him always expect you to pick up the check. I’ve passed bills to lower the cost of housing, healthcare and property taxes. In the Senate, I’ll take on the data centers raising our costs and fight to end the wars driving up gas prices. I’m James Talarico, and I approve this message.

AMY GOODMAN: So, that’s James Talarico. And you heard our election headline. The Wall Street Journal has published video of the Texas Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton, the Republican nominee for Senate, partying in Dubai in 2024, New Year’s Eve, with two indicted fugitive healthcare executives and a woman not his wife. Two men had been indicted months before on federal healthcare fraud charges and didn’t return to the United States. One of the healthcare executives had donated $190,000 to Paxton. And Talarico’s response online was “A party with multiple fugitives, and Ken Paxton is still the sketchiest guy in the room.” And let’s be clear, Ken Paxton, who, to many people’s surprise, was endorsed by President Trump over longtime Senator Cornyn, has been indicted by his — has been impeached by his own party, David Sirota.

DAVID SIROTA: Yeah. So, this race is really the pinnacle of the Senate race in terms of how it embodies the themes in this election. I mean, you have a cartoonishly corrupt Republican Senate candidate against a new-generation populist Democrat. And it’s worth adding that Talarico has really cast himself as an anti-oligarch, anti-billionaire candidate. I mean, I would not call him necessarily a Bernie Sanders candidate, but, clearly, a lot of the themes that you heard in the 2016 and 2020 elections with Bernie Sanders in the primaries there, these are being echoed on the campaign trail by Talarico and by other Democrats, even in these purple and red states, which I think is a reminder of how much the so-called Overton window has shifted in American politics, where those themes, those anti-corruption, populist, anti-oligarch themes, are now very mainstream.

AMY GOODMAN: OK, you mentioned Michigan. The Senate candidates just recently debated. This is Republican Mike Rogers, followed by [sic] Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, in an exchange over U.S. support for Israel and the war in Iran, in a debate held in Grand Rapids. El-Sayed is blaming rising gas prices on the war.

DR. ABDUL EL-SAYED: It is insane, $80, $80 to fill up your gas tank. And yes, I would support pausing the federal gas tax. But there is one thing that is actually causing this. It’s the war in Iran, a war that has been cheerled by my opponent since the beginning, called it a win-win-win. I don’t know about you, but when I go to the gas tank, I don’t feel like I’m winning. I don’t feel like our country is winning.

MIKE ROGERS: His policies will raise your — your — the cost of every gallon of gasoline, number one, raise your utility rates, cause you $20,000 for a Medicare for All plan that takes away private insurance from individuals. It is a disaster. We cannot afford Abdul.

AMY GOODMAN: Talk about this race, David Sirota.

DAVID SIROTA: Again, another marquee race here. I mean, this is a race where, as I mentioned before, Bernie Sanders’ themes being central here. I mean, Abdul El-Sayed was very aligned with the Bernie Sanders wing of the Democratic Party, won a very, very difficult primary, with tons of money, tens of millions of dollars, spent against him. He wins this primary. He is ahead in the polls. And he is continuing to campaign on those themes.

It’s important that you underscored how central the war is in that race. Mike Rogers has been an embodiment of the national security state, and Abdul El-Sayed’s campaign has put that front and center, spotlighting his role in creating the surveillance state when Mike Rogers was in Congress, his role, his investments in data centers — again, data centers becoming an affordability issue. I think that’s key, that linking the data center buildout to higher electricity prices.

And I think the thing is, with this race, which is very important, is if Abdul El-Sayed wins running as a kind of Bernie Sanders-style populist in one of the marquee swing states in the country, it will destroy the argument from the corporate Democrats, at the center of the Democratic Party, that you have to be an archconservative, corporate kind of Democrat in order to win swing states. I think that’s why a lot of corporate Democrats inside the Democratic Party are afraid of Abdul El-Sayed winning. They know that it’s key for him to win in order to win the Senate, but they also know it will destroy their argument that the Democratic Party has to continue nominating more corporate-aligned candidates.

AMY GOODMAN: Let’s remember, he’s a doctor, Abdul El-Sayed, and he wrote a book, Medicare for All. That’s a major issue for him. But I want to turn to what is a major issue for President Trump. This is during a rally in Tennessee Saturday, repeatedly calling Abdul El-Sayed “Mohammed” and calling him a jihadist.

PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: Like Mohammed El-Sayed — I call him Mohammed. Somebody said, “His name isn’t Mohammed; it’s Abdul.” I said, “To me, it’s Mohammed.” I’m the president. I can call him whatever the hell I want. To me, he’s Mohammed, and he’s a radical jihadist.

AMY GOODMAN: That’s President Trump. Congressmember Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez said, “If Abdul can win in Michigan, anyone can win anywhere.” Your thoughts, David Sirota?

DAVID SIROTA: Yeah, I think that’s absolutely right. I mean, I think that’s why his race is so important. And I think — so, he’s taken on the headwinds of the Democratic Party first in the primary, the corporate Democratic faction spending tens of millions of dollars to vilify him and cast him as a terrorist sympathizer. Now he’s in a general election where Donald Trump is using all sorts of Islamophobia to amplify that message. And El-Sayed is campaigning for things like Medicare for All. And so, I think Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez is absolutely right. If Abdul El-Sayed can win a race like this in such an important so-called blue wall state, it means that his politics, what he represents, can win literally anywhere in the country.

AMY GOODMAN: I wanted to ask about whether predictions are overstated about who can win. In the primaries, progressives were surprised by the Wisconsin loss of Francesca Hong, who was polling very strongly. And then, of course, you had Dr. El-Sayed, who won the primary in a very close race with a sitting congressmember.

DAVID SIROTA: Yeah, I think we should all be skeptical of what the polls actually say. I mean, the question of whether there’s going to be a blue wave — is it a blue wave, a surge for Democrats? Is it potentially a red undertow, essentially a drag on the Republican Party? And how much of a drag? These are open questions, because I think the way polling has worked in the last few election cycles, we’ve seen a lot of polls that have not been accurate. And there’s a question about whether — are Republicans not answering polls because they don’t — they don’t answer the phone to pollsters or they don’t want to talk to pollsters? There are all these questions about this.

So, I am skeptical of all of these polls. I think it’s impossible to know what’s going on, beyond the fact that I do think it’s a safe bet that Donald Trump is deeply unpopular. So, it ultimately ends up being a turnout question. How much of a blue wave in terms of a turnout among Democratic voters? Will there be that surge of turnout based on how unpopular Trump is and how bad the affordability crisis is?

AMY GOODMAN: David, let’s go to Maine. Trump’s tariffs have been a major issue there. This is another key race for Democrats. An exchange last week in a debate between this longtime sitting Republican senator, Susan Collins, and Democratic candidate Troy Jackson.

SEN. SUSAN COLLINS: Troy mocked it, but I was successful in getting concrete, pulp and road salt removed from the tariff list.

TROY JACKSON: I didn’t mock the fact that she got road salt back. I mocked the fact that — what about everything else? I mean, we can’t eat road salt. And the thing about it is, is that everything that she’s doing with the Iran war and stuff like that, there’s going to be so many less people that’ll be able to afford to drive that I’m not even sure the road salt’s going to be worth anything, either.

AMY GOODMAN: And that is Troy Jackson, former Maine state Senate president, former logger, and longtime Senator Susan Collins, who’s dealing with a number of issues, from tariffs to her support for Brett Kavanaugh, which enraged the pro-choice community of Maine. She said she couldn’t have predicted he would vote to overturn Roe v. Wade. David Sirota?

DAVID SIROTA: Yeah, I mean, Susan Collins is doing what she always does when she’s running in a tough race in a Democratic-leaning state, which is insist that she’s an independent voice, that she’s separate from the Republican Party. And what Troy Jackson is doing is constantly pointing out how that’s not true, how she’s enabling the Republican Party. They’ve actually mocked her, I think pretty effectively, when she constantly says she’s concerned about the actions of her party, actions that she is supporting.

And what you saw in that clip is her trying to also make a very traditional argument that, “Hey, you may not like me very much, Democratic voters or independent voters, but I’m bringing home the bacon.” And what Jackson did, I think quite effectively, in that clip is turn that around and say, “You may say you’re bringing back road salt, but there are much larger macro issues that make how much you’re bringing home to the state a relatively minuscule issue compared to the fact that nobody can afford the basic necessities of life.”

Now, Maine has not elected a Democratic senator in a very, very long time, and so I do not count Susan Collins out. She is a very, very tough incumbent. But this would be the year.

AMY GOODMAN: And, of course, Bernie Sanders is, though, very popular, and he was just with Troy Jackson. He’s from neighboring Vermont. And, of course, he’s been going around the country. David Sirota, as we wrap up this discussion — again, we’re going to be doing a special on election night, and we’ll continue to cover these issues — your thoughts on what exactly would happen, both if there was a Senate-House Democratic takeover, and if there isn’t, if it’s House goes Democrat and the Republicans remain in charge of the Senate? And do you think, if there was a Senate-House Democratic sweep, that President Trump would be impeached again?

DAVID SIROTA: I don’t think President Trump will be impeached. I think that you’ve seen a lot of Democrats say they don’t want to pursue impeachment. They think that’s a — that path has been fruitless.

I think what you will see is, certainly, if Democrats win, much more scrutiny, using committee chairs, using subpoena power to scrutinize the self-dealing corruption of the Trump administration. I think you’ll see scrutiny potentially on Trump’s Cabinet secretaries, then brought before Congress to testify on all sorts of corruption allegations.

I think the question is going to be, for Democrats, if they win power: What do they actually stand for? And that is an unanswered question that’s going to be litigated also in the 2028 Democratic presidential primary. But I think the — if you look at 2006, a similar moment — second-term Republican president, Democrats win — there was a lot of excitement when Democrats won back Congress in 2006, then won back the presidency in 2008. But soon after that, in 2010, Democrats lost that congressional majority. And part of the reason, I think, for that was there were raised expectations of promises of delivering things, and then a lot of things were not delivered, and the public was disillusioned.

And I think that’s the big danger if Democrats win. If they win, they can stop some of what the Trump administration is doing. They have a sort of congressional veto power over some things. Will they use that power to cut off funding for the Iran war? A big question. Will they use that power to really push forward a real set of healthcare reforms? Another big question. But if they do not deliver, if they are perceived to have gained back power and they do not deliver, they could end up being a delivery system for an even worse Donald Trump. And I think that is a huge question if they end up taking the first step by winning Congress.

AMY GOODMAN: David Sirota, I want to thank you for being with us, founder and editor-in-chief of The Lever, author of the Master Plan: The Hidden Plot to Legalize Corruption in America. We’ll talk about what’s become a major election issue this year, data centers, tomorrow with Paris Marx, author of Hyperscale. We’ll speak to him on Thursday.

Coming up next, federal agents raid the home of Democratic Congressmember Ilhan Omar after President Trump has threatened and attacked her, calling her garbage for years. Stay with us.

AMY GOODMAN: “Souty” by Emel Mathlouthi, here at Democracy Now!’s studios.
