Unfortunately, the “left-wing scene’s” understanding of transformation often remains “a magical one, in which agency is presented as a mystery” (ibid.). To enable self-organization, Marcks further argues that it is necessary to “distance oneself from the Marxist dogma of trade union unity and advocate for alternative unions. For hardly anyone would claim that the established unions, with their hierarchical central apparatuses, could serve as embryonic forms of an egalitarian-socialist society” (Marcks 2018a). Autonomous unions are a “suitable breeding ground” for such transformative efforts, insofar as they address concrete interests and are ideologically “less prescriptive” than volatile political groups (ibid.). This potentially “successful transformative grassroots organizing” serves to mobilize and empower people to win struggles and enable a “counter-society” with genuine counter-power—one that is not a niche project but a mass movement (Marcks 2018b). This leads Marcks to a course of action marked by contradictions that can be described as paradoxical. The goal is not to “force utopia into reality, but rather to arrive at a new one through engagement with reality. The syndicalist revolt is therefore relative; it focuses on current possibilities […]. It does not shy away from contradictions, but works with them—in order to overcome them” (ibid.). This could be achieved through a strategic “meso-politics” that connects different levels and, building on trade union organizations, develops tangible and communicable visions of transformation (ibid.). According to Schmidt and van der Walt, this is what “mass anarchism” strives for (Schmidt/van der Walt 2009: 21). The discussion of direct action and self-organization leads back to that of the understanding of politics. In this quotation, the contrast between “direct” versus “political” action. Instead of the latter, one could speak of “political struggles” that do not refer to the state (ibid.: 138). The autonomous organizational form of the syndicalist union aims to empower and mobilize its members to wage class struggles through direct action. Coupled with the claim to be both a “struggle organization” and the “nucleus of the new society,” great importance is attached to raising the consciousness and shaping the agency of its supporters. In anarchist syndicalism, this specific form of education is conceived as directly linked to one’s own practice. This rejects the position that the path to a libertarian-socialist form of society can be achieved solely or primarily through education and enlightenment (Malatesta 2014i: 205), even though it was necessary to eliminate “one’s own authoritarian upbringing” (Malatesta 2014a: 49) and the ignorance of the exploited and promote self-determination (Malatesta 2014h: 197). Pouget’s statement can be regarded as paradigmatic in this context:

“Direct action thus has an incomparable educational value: it teaches people how to think, decide, and act. It cultivates independence, fosters individuality, and encourages initiative, which it drives. And this abundance of vitality, this expansion of the ‘self,’ in no way contradicts the economic solidarity that unites workers, for it does not stand in the way of common interests but rather harmonizes and strengthens them […]. Direct action thus frees people from the stranglehold of passivity and lack of will […]. It teaches them to will, rather than limiting themselves to obedience, and to exercise their sovereignty, rather than ceding their share of it to a delegate. In this way, it reverses the fundamental social tendency, so that human energies, instead of being exhausted in wretched and depressing inactivity, find in righteous application the fertile ground they need for their continuous growth” (Pouget 2014d: 142f.).

Workers’ growing awareness of their own situation and the broader social context is a building block for their emancipation when viewed in conjunction with the practice of solidarity and revolt, which simultaneously counteract isolation. Ultimately, however, the real goal remains the socialization of wealth by the working class itself (Pouget 2014b: 79). Far from being merely a rebellious reflex, this is a strategic consideration (see Pouget 2014d: 138f.). Rocker emphasizes that, unlike in Marxist social democracy, anarchism does not reduce people to their role as wage laborers in capitalist society, thereby linking ethical aspects with strategic and organizational ones: “The starting point of his reflections on the nature of society is the individual. Not the individual as an abstract, shadowy concept, detached from their social environment, but as a social being, connected to their fellow human beings through thousands of material, intellectual, and emotional relationships” (Rocker 1900). Accordingly, the development of class consciousness in anarcho-syndicalism is, by its very nature, to be understood not as the instrumental creation of a new collective identity, but as a voluntary association of self-empowering individuals. Rocker, too, supports the view that labor struggles themselves are

“the best school of education for workers, for the practical application and deepening of their social sensibilities and their personal initiative within the framework of mutual aid and solidarity-based cooperation. […] In this way, the organization for economic struggle becomes for him a lever in his ongoing struggle against the forces of exploitation and oppression and, at the same time, a bridge across which workers will pass from the hell of the capitalist state system into the realm of socialism and freedom” (Rocker 1924a).

To build a socialist society directly and from the bottom up, syndicalist unions are needed as spaces for preparation, experience, and the raising of consciousness. Schmidt and van der Walt refer to Rocker regarding the “educational impact” of unions, which is particularly important when—in opposition to the passivity fostered by the theory of impoverishment prevalent in social democracy—emphasis is placed on changing one’s own structures. Independent thinking, action, and class consciousness do not develop on their own, but rather from concrete experiences in the immediate lived world of those involved (Schmidt/van der Walt 2009: 183f.). This includes the importance of anarchist pedagogy, the effectiveness of which, of course, is difficult to measure. As part of education, the perspective should also be broadened beyond local labor struggles to encompass a pluralistic, networked, and transnational labor movement. For this reason, Cornelissen, for example, collected and compared data on the rights workers have won, the specific relationship between unions and employers, and the degree of union autonomy in various countries (Cornelissen 2015d: 93–108). Divergent conditions—for example, regarding social structure and the behavior of employers—must be specifically addressed in order to develop adequate strategies without thereby abandoning the transnational character of anarcho-syndicalism (Cornelissen 2015f: 138; see Schmidt and van der Walt 2009: 7, 170).

The social-revolutionary transformation strategy of anarcho-syndicalism aims to take over production and all social functions, which is to be carried out by the workers through self-management. This “industrial democracy,” as Cornelissen called it, stands in “sharp contrast to the authoritarian system of governance in production […]” (Cornelissen 2015c: 74). Building on the socialization of the means of production, the state, too, should be socialized (see Cantzen 1997: 90–95). To this end, it is necessary to counter false notions, such as those of “miraculous catastrophes,” the supposed “iron law of wages,” and the “theory of impoverishment.” Pouget considers the notion that the collapse of the state-capitalist social system would occur on its own to be a fundamental misjudgment of the (alleged) laws governing capitalist development. This assumption, he argues, leads to passively waiting for a revolution (Pouget 2015d: 147). In contrast, he again cites direct action as a self-driven and empowering form of action (ibid.: 140). Cornelissen writes that the “collapse theory of the old Marxists is just as categorically refuted by facts as the theory of the disappearance of the middle classes and the growing impoverishment of the masses” (Cornelissen 2015f: 140). Rather, capitalism would collapse or fall into crisis as a consequence of social development—and, within that, of labor struggles as well, one might add.[8] Thus, acute crises seem “inevitable and will likely, in and of themselves, accelerate the development of a society dominated by capitalism into a different society of a socialist or communist nature. It would, however, be wrong to seek to set these acute crises and inevitable catastrophes against general social development” (ibid.: 143). Instead of believing that class antagonism would automatically continue to intensify, the syndicalists would want to “make history themselves.” Cornelissen counters the accusation that this amounts to “voluntarism” by arguing that appealing to the revolutionary will of the workers is necessary, since “enthusiasm” is not necessarily widespread among the working class (Cornelissen 2015c: 82). Pouget echoes this view: “[E]xcessive suffering is not a catalyst for revolt!” This means that every hard-won relief is an absolute prerequisite for the further organization of the working class. This is all the more true for those who live in social misery, are in a state of material and moral dependence, and are therefore unable to rebel. Instead, the confrontation with employers enhances the dignity and consciousness of the workers and must, of course, aim at the abolition of state capitalism as a whole (Pouget 2015d: 152ff.). In response to the “so-called ‘iron law,’” Pouget argues that wage levels, working conditions, working hours, freedom of association, etc., do not follow an inevitable course of development but are rather a matter of the struggles waged over them (ibid.: 148). This, however, requires that state socialists, syndicalists, and anarchists fill the discourse on the workers’ takeover of industry with concrete ideas, rather than allowing it to remain a vague phrase. Ultimately, this happens “through hard experiences,” which also applies to “the powerful weapon of the general strike” (Cornelissen 2015e: 136). Rocker also writes that socialism cannot be achieved by following pseudo-scientific laws—that is, historical materialism. He further explains that capitalism and the state do not contain any seeds of socialism that could be brought to “maturity”—this, he argues, is a quasi-religious dogmatic belief. Recalling his formulation in a letter to Landauer, he writes:

“No, socialism will not come to us because it must come with the inevitability of a law of nature; it will come to us only when people muster the firm will and the necessary strength to bring it into reality. Not time, not economic conditions, but only our innermost insight, our will, can build the bridge that leads us from the world of wage slavery into the new territory of socialism” (Rocker 1900).

The task, then, would be to overcome “social democratic ideology,” which leads workers to the mistaken belief that they have nothing better to expect from present-day society (Rocker 1924a). Marcks points out that the notion of a dictatorship of the proletariat is also flawed because it assumes that “everything else would follow from the driving forces of history” (Marcks 2018b). Accordingly, he also criticizes what he sees as the widespread contemporary belief among vulgar anarchists, insurrectionists, and Marxists “in magical turns of history. […] [T]he idea that transformation can only be consciously shaped once the new society has developed in the ‘womb’ of the old [is] synonymous with spontaneism. Both negate the creative power of the present and place their trust in a quasi-divine power that will already set the course for the revolution” (ibid.). In anarcho-syndicalist germ theory, the unfolding of a libertarian-socialist society is conceived on the basis of the organizational forms and relationships of existing unions: “The new social forces, which have developed slowly, bit by bit, under the old order—like the germ in the egg—then break through the shell of laws and customs. A new social life has suddenly emerged and is ready to blossom,” as Cornelissen (2015f: 142) puts it (cf. Pouget 2014a: 74). Peiró views three essential steps as prerequisites for the social revolution: First, an “organized force” is needed to appropriate and defend the means of production and land ownership; then the technical preparation for taking over production and administration; and finally, the preparation for a (coordinated) distribution system for the products (Peiró 1986: 43). He therefore calls for a return to factory and workshop committees, which would have more than just an administrative character but would serve to support the “economic machinery of revolutionary syndicalism” (ibid.: 44). The self-management of production is the ultimate goal. However, the “success of this task depends on the network of relationships that was established even before the revolution among the unions of the various industrial sectors and professions. The prior establishment of such a system of relationships of a pre-revolutionary character must be based on the principles of a social doctrine that serves as a guide and driving force when the revolution breaks out” (ibid.). The development of their own networks is therefore a crucial element for the syndicalist transformation. In this regard, Peiró sees himself in a dual role:

“We anarchists must, as far as possible, build our own world even within the capitalist world—but not on paper, through poetry, or in philosophical—high-flown—night work, but on the ground of practice, by inspiring confidence in our world of today and tomorrow. For the confidence we instill in the proletarian masses is directly related to the possibilities of forming an organized force that takes over and defends the land, all means of production and tools, consumption, transportation, and trade” (ibid.: 46).

However, the initial optimism and fighting spirit later gave way to pragmatism, if not outright resignation. This does not make Pouget’s view incorrect—that social change is inevitable to the extent that class consciousness, autonomy, and organizational capacity are expanded (Pouget 2014c: 116). In practice, however, the anarcho-syndicalist pursuit of autonomy proves to be significantly more complicated. Cornelissen addresses a recurring gap in the theory of the syndicalist labor movement, namely the question of how the management of production should function in the context of the (concretely conceived and directly implemented) socialization of the means of production. In doing so, he counters the view that workers do not know how complex modern industrial production could be managed. In this context, the concept of self-management is not primarily about taking over the technical management of factories—after all, shareholders have just as little knowledge of it. Rather, it is particularly the capitalists’ ownership of the companies that must be abolished (Cornelissen 2015c: 79, cf. Cornelissen 2015f: 147). Since this is a long-term goal, Marcks advocates for adopting long-term strategies and focusing on small, incremental successes (Marcks 2018a). In his view, a deeper engagement with syndicalist theory and practice would help avoid the dead ends of current theories of transformation (ibid.). After all, the syndicalist theory of embryonic forms—which does not aim for a revolutionary rupture—would be entirely plausible, since it takes the “existing” as its starting point and thus “would counteract the crude notion held by some on the left that anything that does not always concern the whole would inevitably be swallowed up by the system” (Marcks 2018b). Nevertheless, “building the ‘new society within the shell of the old’ […] does not mean seeking out and expanding the new within the existing order, but rather constructing something new and finding points of connection within the existing order from which it can draw resources. […] It means acting from within the existing conditions without relying solely on them” (ibid.: 7). Despite the emphasis on the day-to-day struggles of the labor movement, as has already been the abolition of class society remains the goal of anarcho-syndicalism, which distinguishes it from other labor movements (Schmidt/van der Walt 2009: 22). Thus, for Pouget at the dawn of the 20th century, the

“the social question is not a purely material problem. To be happy and content, the ‘daily bread’ is not enough for us; we also want to be free from all forms of coercion and domination. We want to be free, dependent on no one, and to relate to our fellow human beings only as equals, regardless of all diversity in abilities, knowledge, and roles. The goal, therefore, is to transform the structure of society in such a way that only one group, one class, remains: that of the producers. This decisive transformation can only be achieved on a communist basis […]” (Pouget 2015c: 115f).

The realization that this is a complex task has become increasingly widespread over the years, which is why Cornelissen emphasizes that the “problem and its solution” are distinct (Cornelissen 2015f: 139). It should be noted, among other things, “that ‘capitalism’ is by no means a uniform economic order and that, in reality, there are different strata of capitalists who, because of their immediate interests and despite their common origin, fight one another and may differ in terms of their relationships with producers and consumers” (ibid.). Thus, the development toward socialism and communism cannot be understood as a linear process (ibid.: 142), as evidenced by the fact that an increase in common ownership is predicted. A leveling out of the distribution of private property might represent a step in the right direction. What is decisive, however, is that “modern social life is dominated by the development of the large capitalist industries […] [and therefore] the decisive struggle for the universalization of prosperity and freedom must also be waged within them” (ibid.: 145). Realistically speaking, taking over companies is significantly more difficult than, for example, founding educational and welfare associations (ibid.: 146). Thus, the struggle within companies remains decisive; it can be waged either revolutionarily or through a “peaceful form of gradual penetration” (Cornelissen 2015g: 158), for which the capacity to strike represents the essential source of power for the organized working class. This could even enable direct union intervention in the management of capitalist enterprises (ibid.: 159), which, however, should be more than just a little more co-determination (ibid.: 167), but rather aim at the appropriation of economic power (ibid. 161f.). Schmidt and van der Walt further point out that there have been ongoing debates within syndicalism regarding the extent to which wage increases (etc.) should be viewed as an end in themselves or, rather, always as a means to achieving the revolution (Schmidt/van der Walt 2009: 137). In doing so, they raise the question of the system itself and argue that a global constellation based, as in the 21st century, on such extreme inequality and its consequences will one day be a thing of the past (ibid.: 10). Since neoliberalism was globally established as the sole capitalist model in the 1980s and 1990s, what is needed is the reshaping of popular and revolutionary class struggles (ibid.: 11). For anarcho-syndicalists, regardless of their vehement emphasis on union organizing and leading labor struggles, the goal is a higher one. The social “upheaval”—which must be conceived primarily in economic terms—aims at a fundamental transformation of today’s “relationships between people—namely, those between wage laborers and capitalists, the ruled and the rulers” (Pouget 2014c: 118), in order to replace them with egalitarian and libertarian ones. In conjunction with the “methods of direct action,” the principle of autonomy, and solidarity, the “idea” of combating and replacing the entire system of domination arises from practical experience. Anarcho-syndicalists lived

“in the here and now, with the greatest possible readiness for struggle, and sacrifice neither the present for the future nor the future for the present. Thus, it follows from this ability to simultaneously meet the necessities of the moment and those of the future—and from the harmony between these two tasks that must be combined—that the ideal to which we aspire is thereby neither obscured nor neglected, but on the contrary becomes clearer, more precise, and more readily recognizable” (Pouget 2014d: 145).

Thus, the revolution is “a matter of everyday life.” This does not, however, involve a desire to return to earlier phases of capitalism, which Cornelissen considers reactionary (Cornelissen 2015f: 137). Rather, all “social revolutions that can arise in modern countries and have a deeper impact than mere political upheavals, […] can only be the result of ongoing economic transformations that have characterized social life in recent decades” (ibid.: 141f.). He describes these trends—which he views as strong forces toward the democratization of enterprises—as the “penetration of socialism,” evident, among other things, in the necessity of state social policy and in forms of worker self-organization (ibid.: 143f.), which is why he consequently advocates for the strengthening of works councils (Cornelissen 2015l: 128). Rocker confirms that political parties lack, for the

“social reorganization of the social organism no less than anything else […]. Social movements and new social formations are not brought about by state decrees and legal regulations imposed from above; they may develop from the very heart of the masses, from the free interplay of all the creative forces within the people, which are hindered in their natural unfolding and gradually stifled entirely by the routine of a government—no matter how revolutionary it may always appear—that is geared toward cookie-cutter work and dead mechanization” (Rocker 1924a).

This is illustrated by the example of Russia, where trade unions and councils were reduced to instruments of the state (ibid., cf. Schmidt/van der Walt 2009: 25), leading Rocker to an extremely sober assessment of revolutionary possibilities. Social alternatives could therefore only be expanded through practical experiments, education about freedom and solidarity, and the defense of important achievements (Rocker 1928). To return to the beginning of this section, we can once again quote Santillián, who asserts that “on the political level, we want to replace the principles of authority and their embodiment—the state and the machinery of oppression—with free agreement among social groups. On this issue, however, we anarchists are very isolated and will occupy a special position even during a victorious revolution” (Santillián 1986: 139, cf. Schmidt/van der Walt 2009: 25). In doing so, he emphasizes an underlying ethical dimension that is inherent in anarcho-syndicalism. This is also evident in his emphasis on the necessity of establishing unity within the working class. This unity arises

“the general interest of all […] and [serves] to guarantee the freedom of the individual within the collective. “Our common basis for understanding is the recognition of our different characters, temperaments, and upbringings. We should also share a mutual understanding based on respect. Our common goal is: the abolition of capitalism and the totalitarian state, in order to help the revolution achieve victory” (ibid.: 144).

Burdened with this ethical weight, it becomes clear why anarchist syndicalism constantly finds itself in tension with politics that are challenged through strikes, boycotts, sabotage, and other forms of struggle and practices (see Rocker 1924c).

In summary, it can be stated that the reference to the concept of politics—and, beyond that, the relationship to the political dimension—in anarchist syndicalism is mixed. Pouget’s vehement and forceful rejection of politics serves as the starting point for demonstrating that this tendency toward autonomy exhibits distinct anti-political traits. Even more clearly than in other tendencies, genuine anarcho-syndicalism contrasts politics with the economy as an anti-political sphere. If, at the same time, a social-revolutionary claim is to be upheld, this orientation ultimately leads to a void that must be addressed. Unlike Pouget, Cornelissen proceeds from the premise of the importance of political movements that coexist alongside syndicalism and are intended to interact with it within a libertarian communism, as advocated by Peiró and Santillán. Schmidt and van der Walt refer to this strategy as organizational dualism, which in the practice of social struggles rarely follows an orderly plan but rather arises from the differences and coordination among various groups. To a certain extent, this reflects the contradictions that the autonomous labor movement has faced—and continues to face—in practice. This concerns, first and foremost, the de facto heterogeneity of the working class—both in terms of its political-economic positioning and its cultural and ideological positioning within society as a whole. Second, there have been experiences of political parties attempting to co-opt the autonomous labor movement. The organizational dualism of syndicalist unions and anarchist-communist groups is the first response to this. Here, platformism represents the most pronounced variant of a political organizational form that (in terms of the history of ideas) can still be considered anarchist. The second response is that “syndicalism is self-sufficient.” This entails, at the very least, the danger of trade union dogmatism and reductive economism. Rocker’s reflections outline a third possibility, according to which anarcho-syndicalists themselves occasionally resort to political means in the rather rare cases where these appear strategically sensible. The question of when political means should be used, however, remains open and is continually contested. Cornelissen’s reflections highlight the gray area between extra-parliamentary political movements and autonomous social movements. Rocker, too, demonstrates an ambivalent relationship to politics, though he is far from a fundamentalist rejection of it. Nevertheless, this tension does not seem easily resolvable, as political issues repeatedly disrupt autonomous union activism and a critique of politics is reemerging within anarcho-syndicalism. Therefore, even for this anarchist tendency striving for autonomy, one can assume a paradoxical concept of politics.

[1] The confrontational calls for practical class struggle in anarchist syndicalism, its emergence from disillusionment with all previous political regimes, and the rejection of the politicization of the socialist movement exhibit some theoretical and many rhetorical elements of the “anti-politics” of “populist” anti-elitist protest movements—which de Saint-Victor (2015) denounced and from which he clearly distances himself. For “when the people know that they have nothing more to expect from a change in political power, then all that remains for them is to protest against all politicians without distinction” (ibid.: 27) (→ 2.3.2).

[2] I have since presented the anarchist understanding of politics, as discussed in subsection 3.4, in a less academic manner in the article “Anarch@-Syndicalism and (Anti-)Politics” (Eibisch 2022b).

[3] In direct contrast to the later account by Schmidt and van der Walt (2009: 9; 18f.; 41; 170; 241), Cornelissen, in his engagement with Eltzbacher’s study (1900), emphasizes the plurality of anarchism (Cornelissen 2015b: 46). Building on this, however, he criticizes the lack of clarity within anarchism and points out that Eltzbacher fails to recognize its further development in the form of anarcho-syndicalism, which, among other things, entails a near-total departure from the individualistic notion of “unrestricted autonomy of the individual.” With this “evolution of anarchism,” however, the self-determination of individuals is not restricted but rather preserved within the collective organization of labor interests (ibid.). These theoretical assumptions arise precisely from the practice and experiences of workers, who constitute the bulk of anarchism (ibid.: 48f.).

[4] From this perspective, Pouget opposes the philosophy of Rousseau, the “theorist of democratic servitude” (Pouget 2014a: 60), since the concept of social contracts is a bourgeois theory. In the spirit of Kropotkin, he argues against social Darwinism and in favor of the solidarity and sociability of all people. The “spirit of renunciation” preached in religions is equally at work in liberalism. Drawing on the anarchist understanding of social freedom, Pouget criticizes the state as a bad form of order that oppresses the masses and serves only a privileged minority. In this statement, the anarchist in Pouget is undoubtedly alive and well. Accordingly, he views citizenship and bourgeois democracy as an “illusory community” linked to the “superstition” of “popular sovereignty” and “fatherland” (ibid.: 65). The bourgeois revolution merely renovated the “facade of the state,” with democracy acting as a “stumbling block” to social progress. It can thus be said that the differentiation of politics as a social sphere—analogous to the separation of the modern state—must be understood in connection with the expansion of its bureaucracy and political parties.

[5] In this sense, Rocker called on his comrades in 1924 to be “active non-voters.” Anyone who refrains from voting out of a lack of awareness stands “in his or her mental attitude even lower than the voter” (Rocker 1924c). The person “who goes to the ballot box because he is guided by the sincere belief that the ballot is a means of creating better social conditions proves, at any rate, that he possesses social sensitivity and is willing to intervene in the course of events” (ibid.). This makes it clear that Rocker feels compelled, precisely because of widespread disillusionment with politics, to bring forgotten anarchist principles back into focus. Elections should be rejected not out of dogmatism, but on the basis of decades of experience with autonomous social movements (Rocker 1924c).

[6] One conflict in which this tension crystallized was the earlier split in the IWW between the Detroit faction led by Daniel De Leon and the Chicago faction led by James Connolly. The labor leader De Leon formed a syndicalist political party beginning in 1895. Although its representatives viewed parliamentary activity as secondary and elections as inconsequential, they thereby strayed from one of the fundamental principles of syndicalism, leading to a split in 1908 because the “Chicago IWW” explicitly opposed elections and removed all references to the political sphere (Schmidt/van der Walt 2009: 161f.). The French CGT, too, explicitly presented itself as “apolitical” or even “anti-political” after 1895—and thus saw itself in alignment with the anti-authoritarian wing within the First International (ibid.: 142f.). Van der Walt and Schmidt demonstrate that syndicalists did not reject political issues but rather saw them as subsumed within the revolutionary unions, wh ly they spoke out against “political action” (ibid.: 193f.).

[7] Pierre Monatte (1907/1972) takes the opposite position.

[8] Incidentally, this argument—and its elaboration below—anticipates a core theorem of the operaist movement, which emerged in Italy in the 1960s. The organized and conscious working class itself would actively shape history, to which companies would respond, for example, by restructuring production processes, adjusting working conditions, or setting wage levels (see Birkner/Foltin 2010: 19–24). Post-operaist theorists, such as Hardt and Negri or Holloway (2006), also emphasize this as a fundamental theoretical building block.

author: Unknown
title: Solidarité face à la répression des lycéen.nes !
content:
Ces deux dernières semaines, la Legal Team Paris 

IDF

 a accompagné plus d'une centaine de jeunes confronté.es à la répression et leurs proches. On vous partage un compte rendu de ce qu'on a constaté. Car mieux comprendre la répression permet de mieux l'esquiver

 

!




Ces deux dernières semaines, la Legal Team Paris 

IDF

 a accompagné plus d'une centaine de personnes en garde à vue et devant les tribunaux, et encore plus de proches de personnes brutalement réprimées. 




Les avocat.e.s avec qui on travaille ont assuré des gardes à vue à Aubervilliers, Bobigny, Choisy-le-roi, La Courneuve, Les Lilas, Nanterre, Noisy le Sec, Paris, Stains, Saint-Denis, Villeneuve la Garenne, Vitry et Vincennes et des déférrements dans les tribunaux de Bobigny, Créteil, Nanterre et Paris.




Sans surprise, les flics ont visé presque exclusivement des enfants racisé.e.s.


Les jeunes nous ont rapporté des insultes, des violences bien vénères avec pour certain.e.s des séquelles graves. Ce n'est pas étonnant mais on ne peut que constater qu'il n'y a aucune limite dans cette violence, les flics interpellant et brutalisant parfois des enfants très jeunes de 11 ou 12 ans. 


En banlieue plusieurs mineur.e.s n'ont pas pu avoir d'avocat.e désigné.e ou commis.e d'office en garde à vue alors que c'est obligatoire.


Plusieurs d'entre elleux, n'ont pas non plus pu prévenir leurs parents, alors que là aussi c'est obligatoire.


Il y a aussi eu des refus de médecin. 


Un mineur a été détenu pendant 10h hors de tout cadre légal sans notification de placement en garde à vue.


Les parents n'ont pas été épargnés avec des insultes et des mensonges très fréquents pour les inquiéter.




On veut souligner que plusieurs jeunes ont été interpellé.e.s non pas pendant des actions, mais directement chez elleux ou devant leur bahuts plusieurs jours après les faits reprochés, les flics ayant visionné des vidéos sur les réseaux sociaux leur permettant de les identifier.


A ce titre, on vous partage quelques rappels concernant la sécurité numérique pour se protéger les un.es les autres à diffuser massivement autour de vous : 




 Sécurisez vos téléphones : désactivez la reconnaissance faciale et mettez-vous un code de déverrouillage de téléphone béton (pas de date de naissance, pas de 0000, pas de 1234, pas de 1312 ou autre code trop simple)

 Ne postez pas de vidéos et photos d'actions sur les réseaux : cela met en danger vos camarades et vous même

 

! 

 Même si cela peut constituer une infraction, en garde à vue refusez de donner vos codes de téléphone : ton tel est une mine d'or pour les policier.e.s (snap, msg, géologie, photos, videos...) qui obtiendront des preuves qui pourront mettre dans la merde toi ou d'autres personnes.




La 

GAV

, en plus d'être destinée à réduire le nombre de jeunes sur les blocus en les interpellant et les enfermant, est une mesure qui constitue une peine en tant que telle. En effet, son objectif est de traumatiser pour désinciter à recommencer. Mais l'État s'est rarement arrêté à la 

GAV

 dans la répression des lycéen.nes depuis 2 semaines.




Sur les mineur.e.s placé.e.s en garde à vue qu'on a suivi avec la 

LT

 un tiers d'entre elleux sont sorti.e.s sans suites, un tiers ont été déféré.e.s et sont passé.e.s devant lae délégué.e du procureur avec des alternatives aux poursuites (souvent avec des convocations à des stages de citoyennetés) et un tiers sont passé.e.s devant le juge des enfants.




Pour les majeur.e.s, on a suivi une dizaine de comparutions immédiates. La plupart sont sorti.e.s sous contrôle judiciaire, certain.e.s avec des obligations de pointage hebdomadaire. 




Une meuf trans étrangère passée en comparution immédiate est sortie du tribunal sans contrôle judiciaire mais a été placée dans un 

CRA

 pour hommes. Elle a passé sa journée au 

CRA

 en salle d'isolement craignant des violences, avant d'être finalement libérée.




Le tribunal judiciaire de Paris a prévu l'ouverture d'une chambre spéciale pour les manifs/blocages le 26 novembre pour tous les renvois de comparutions immédiates. Notez la date, il y aura besoin d'un max de soutien

 

!




En plus de cette répression policière et judiciaire, la répression disciplinaire a bien été entamée. Les convocations pour les conseils de disciplines pleuvent. Plusieurs personnes ont déjà été exclues de manière définitive de leur lycée. Dans les semaines à venir il y a d'autres conseils déjà prévus à Garge lès Gonesse, Mennecy, Montreuil, Paris, Villiers Saint Frédéric...




Des proviseur.e.s ont indiqué vouloir porter plainte contre leurs élèves.




Si vous êtes profs ou AEDs, mobilisez-vous au sein de vos établissements pour créer un rapport de force localement : refusez les conseils de discipline et exigez l'absence totale de sanction pour les élèves mobilisé.e.s. En cas de maintien du conseil accompagnez les élèves visé.e.s (courriers de soutien, rassemblement de parents d'élèves et personnels, ...). 




Si vous avez des infos sur des conseils de discipline à venir, vous pouvez nous contacter par mail sur cdiscipline@proton.me. On s'organise pour vous accompagner. ​​​​​​​Si le conseil de discipline est déjà passé, contactez nous également. Dans certains cas on peut envisager de contester une décision de conseil de discipline devant le tribunal. 




Face à cette répression, ne lâchons rien

 

!!




Continuez à tracter et faire tourner les infos d'antirep en 

AG

, sur les blocus, en manif, et sur les réseaux sociaux (on a lancé une page Instagram : legalteam.paris.

IDF

). 




Si vous avez besoin de tracts, contactez-nous et on pourra se rencarder pour vous en filer.




Mille mercis à toutes les personnes qui ont filé de la thune pour rémunérer les avocat.es qui interviennent non-stop depuis deux semaines.




On vous remet le lien de la cagnotte de solidarité : 

http://shorturl.re/stoprep

 - hésitez pas à l'alimenter ou à la faire tourner, on en a bien besoin :)




Dans la semaine à venir, en cas de situation urgente (personne interpellée, violence policière) contactez-nous par téléphone, de préférence par signal, voire par WhatsApp au 07.52.85.71.11.




Sinon privilégiez les emails : stoprepression@riseup.net




Si les jeunes subissent une répression aussi violente c'est qu'iels visent juste et que le pouvoir souhaite tout simplement les traumatiser et les isoler pour les inciter à ne pas recommencer. La réponse à cette répression ne peut être que la défense collective et la solidarité. 




Alors vive les lycéen.ne.s, vive la lutte, bismillah c'est les ténèbres

 

!! 🥷 🎆

author: Aaron Ernest Cruz
title: IP leaders condemn Ombudsman’s dismissal of illegal arrest cases vs police
content:
IN FRAME: Indigenous rights defenders Julieta Gomez and Niezel Velasco successfully filed the position paper against the police officials behind their violent arrest and four years of detention, before the Office of the Ombudsman today, November 14. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat.

Indigenous Peoples (IP) rights defender, Niezel Velasco, and Manobo activist, Julieta Gomez, filed a motion for consideration after the Ombudsman dismissed on Monday, October 12, the countercharges they filed against the Philippine National Police (PNP) officers involved in their illegal arrest.

Read: Detained for nearly 4 years over false charges, rights defenders file countercharges vs police

Velasco and Gomez challenged the decision, asserting that this action is a major step toward defending their rights and holding state forces accountable for the human rights violations committed not only against them but also against IP communities facing harassment and intimidation by state forces.

“The dismissal of the countercharges against the police is unacceptable and unjust. We were imprisoned for almost four years, and now they will just let the perpetrators who violated our rights go free? This office [Ombudsman] is useless,” Velasco said in a statement.

On June 25, the Ombudsman dismissed the countercharges of Velasco and Gomez, claiming that the case has no prima facie evidence or an initial proof that reached minimum legal threshold that would support their claim. The office also called the charges “self-serving.”

In the filed motion, they said that Velasco’s arrest is not valid as the name written in the arrest warrant is for “Mary Jane Velasco.” They also proved that the firearms and explosives were planted.

The filed countercharges against P/Smsgt. Jehrome D. Chico, P/Cpl. John Ronoel J. Conde, Pat. Julius Edward L. Mahinay, Pat. Mary Grail A. Waclin, and Pat. Magdalena D. Lipata are False Testimony Against a Defendant, False Testimony in Other Cases and Perjury in Solemn Affirmation, Unlawful Arrest, and Liability for Planting of Evidence.

Aside from criminal charges, the police are also facing administrative charges of Conduct Prejudicial to the Best Interest of Service, Grave Abuse of Authority, Grave Misconduct, and Oppression.

Velasco said that the police officers should be imprisoned for the violations they did “to know what it feels like to be jailed.”

The case stemmed from the illegal arrest of Gomez and Velasco on murder, attempted murder, and illegal possession of firearms and explosives on July 16, 2021. It was dismissed on April 8, 2025 by the Quezon City Regional Trial Court.

Read: A step closer to full justice: Indigenous people rights defender acquitted of charges

Under the Marcos Jr. administration, Karapatan said that there are 757 total political prisoners as of 2026. Most of the cases bear the same pattern that both of them experienced.

Of the 757 total political prisoners, 150 arrests happened under the present administration.

IP group Katribu Kalipunan ng Katutubong Mamamayan ng Pilipinas (Katribu) condemned the dismissal of countercharges, stressing that this action only worsens the culture of impunity.

“The decision of the Ombudsman shows the lack of accountability from the state who continuously violates human rights. In the experience of IP and activists, the planting of evidence and trumped-up charges are used for a long time to suppress their demand to defend ancestral land and self-determination,” Katribu said.

Velasco said that activists are being easily jailed while the police along with other state forces are not being held accountable for the crimes they commit. “The Office of the Ombudsman only shows that they are the true protector of criminals who are police and military,” Velasco said. (AMU, RTS, DAA)

title: Tuncer Bakirhan û Nêçîrvan Barzanî civiyan
content:
Hevserokê Giştî yê DEM Partiyê Tuncer Bakirhan û heyeta pê re ji bo beşdarî Foruma MERI bibin çûbûn Hewlêrê. Du roj in Bakirhan li Hewlêrê serdanan dike. Tuncer Bakirhan li Hewlêrê bi Serokê Herêma Kurdistanê Nêçîrvan Barzanî re hevdîtinek kir.



















Foruma MERIyê ya 2026an: Tuncer Bakirhan û Mazlûm Ebdî li Hewlêrê ne




12 Cotmeh 2026










Serokatiya Herêma Kurdistanê li ser naveroka hevdîtinê daxuyaniyek belav kir.




Di daxuyaniyê de hate diyarkirin ku her du aliyan bal kişandiye ser girîngiya sûdwergirtina ji vê derfeta dîrokî ya ji bo pêkanîna aştiyê û Bakirhan û Barzanî gotine nabe ku ev derfet ji dest here. Di daxuyaniyê de hate gotin ku pêwîstiya piştgiriya hemû aliyan a ji bo pêvajoyê jî hatiye axaftin.




Di daxuyaniyê de hat destnîşan kirin ku Serokê Herêma Kurdistanê piştgiriya xwe ya ji bo pêvajoya aştiyê aniye ziman û amadekariya xwe ji bo her alîkariya pêwîst a ji bo serxistina pêvajoyê nîşan daye.




Nêçîrvan Barzanî her wiha bal kişandiye ser girîngiya aştiyê ya ji bo ewlehî û aramiya Bakurê Kurdistanê û Tirkiyeyê û tevahiya herêmê.




Tuncer Bakirhan jî spasiya xwe û partiya xwe ya ji bo helwest û hewlên berdewam ên Serokê Herêma Kurdistanê aniye zimên ku piştgiriyê dide pêvajoyê.







Hewler'de düzenlenen MERI Forumu'nun ilk gününe katıldık. Forumda bölgenin geleceğine dair çok verimli tartışmalar yürütüldü. Forum vesilesiyle Kürdistan Bölgesi Başkanı Sayın Neçîrvan Barzanî, KYB Genel Başkanı Sayın Bafil Talabanî, Sayın Îlham Ahmed, Sayın Qubad Talabanî ve Sayın Mazlum Abdi ile bir araya geldik. Ev sahipliği için MERI'ye ve Kürdistan Bölgesi yönetimine teşekkür ederiz.


— Tuncer BAKIRHAN (@tuncerbakirhan) 

October 12, 2026

author: Darío Aranda
title: "Debemos cuidar el hogar que habitamos, el hogar-cuerpo, el hogar-tierra"
content:
Por Sergio Sánchez




Pablo Bruno creció entre un barrio popular de la capital cordobesa y el paisaje de las sierras. Oriundo del barrio General Pueyrredón, el joven cantante, guitarrista y compositor pateó las agitadas calles de su ciudad y conectó tempranamente con la fuerza vital de la naturaleza. “También crecí en el barrio Centro América, que es donde vivían mis abuelos. Fueron los dos lugares donde me he criado, unas raíces bien cordobesas”, resalta el músico de 28 años. “Siempre estábamos en la calle con la changada, andando en bicicleta, jugando a la pelota, echando moco. Agradezco esa niñez, porque la pude disfrutar”, dice. “Además, mis viejos desde chiquitito siempre me llevaron a las Sierras Chicas de Córdoba. Empecé a ir desde los 4 años para allá y le agarré amor al monte. En paralelo, con mis abuelos íbamos siempre al campo”, recuerda.




“Entonces, el barrio, las sierras y el campo fueron los tres lugares a donde me crie”, sintetiza Bruno, quien acaba de publicar su cuarto disco de estudio, 

Hogar

 (2026), una obra que justamente habla de cuidar la casa propia: la íntima y la social; la espiritual y la comunitaria.




"Entré en el vuelo de la palabra hogar como filosofía. Lo más importante que podemos hacer es 

cuidar ese hogar que habitamos, ese hogar-cuerpo, ese hogar-tierra

, que es lo mismo", grafica el cantautor antes de presentar el disco el viernes 16 de octubre a las 21 en JJ Circuito Cultural (Jean Jaures 347). "

En las canciones está ese cuidado hacia la sierra, la naturaleza, que es el lugar más presente que tenemos para habitar y cuidar

. Hace unos días venía de Mendoza, de San Rafael, y un amigo me decía: 'Nosotros estamos defendiendo el agua'. Más allá de la palabra lucha, porque es una defensa que tenemos que realizar como tribu para las nuevas generaciones".




Con el acento puesto en la música de raíz folklórica, el disco recorre diferentes estados emocionales y climas musicales, desde la cumbia "Luna de los desvelos" hasta la introspectiva y despojada "Sentirme hogar", pasando por la chacarera percusiva "Donde el milagro hecha brotar", la reflexiva "Zamba del juglar", la instrumental “Canción de otoño” o la chacarera comunitaria "Ahicito en los encuentros".




Foto: Prensa Pablo Bruno




“Encontrarnos, compartir el pan/ construir en hermandad/ Volvamos a lo simple/ militemos la paz/ Donde el amor construye/ un puente al hogar”, canta como un manifiesto de vida en “El abrazo de hogar”. 

"En la comunidad entra la familia, las amistades, la tribu con la que uno comparte y la naturaleza

; el sitio que uno elige vivir y cuidar", sostiene el artista en torno al concepto.




—

¿De dónde nace tu necesidad de defender el monte, el agua y las sierras?




—En las Sierras Chicas he compuesto más de la mitad de mis canciones. Es un lugar donde no llega el agua, estuve viviendo un tiempo ahí. Hay todo un sistema de riego y cuando llueve se llenan los tanques. Entonces, la lluvia está relacionada con la bendición. Uno cuando no tiene el agua se da cuenta de la importancia y la vitalidad máxima que tenemos. Uno aprende a habitar una conciencia del cuidado. En Córdoba estamos muy acostumbrados a gente que lava los platos y deja la canilla abierta. Y hay sitios donde el agua falta.




—

¿Y una canción puede ser un instrumento o herramienta para despertar una reflexión?




—Hace unos días estaba cantando una canción inédita en San Rafael, que en un momento dice: "Agua tesoro del mundo". También dice: "Vivo feliz cantando/ con la esperanza firme en la canción". Creo que desde el arte, en este caso desde la música, es sumamente importante poner en palabras ciertas cuestiones, porque la gente siempre se sensibiliza más a través del arte. Porque toca células más sutiles. Y va a despertar algo a través de una canción, una poesía o una obra de teatro. El arte siempre es fundamental para habitar esos espacios. Estamos atravesando un presente particular en relación a 

la lucha por el agua

. Y en Mendoza le están poniendo el cuerpo a esa causa hace mucho tiempo.




—

¿Sentís una responsabilidad social de hablar sobre determinados temas que te incomodan en esta época?




—Lo siento algo muy personal y de búsqueda artística. Es importante cantarle a lo que veo en cuanto a injusticias o maltrato hacia la naturaleza. O sobre otras cosas, como cantar hacia adentro de uno mismo. Habitar esos lugares implica una responsabilidad muy linda. No me sale cantar por cantar. Siento que cobra sentido cuando hay una palabra a la hora de cantar y compartir. Pero del mismo modo respeto a cada artista con su camino.




—

También te has expresado sobre el cuidado de la universidad pública y el respeto por la memoria en contexto de dictaduras y pueblos originarios.




—Son temas que me sensibilizan y me atraviesan como historia. No he vivido una dictadura, pero sí he compartido con gente que en su mirada hay una nostalgia, una tristeza muy fuerte. Entonces, en una mirada uno puede empatizar. Tiene que ver con escuchar y sensibilizarse con parte de nuestra historia como país y continente. También me gusta estudiar acá en Córdoba sobre los comechingones y los sanavirones que habitaron estas tierras; la gente que hacía sus casa-pozo acá en Córdoba. Estoy en ese camino, a nivel nacional y latinoamericano, de conocer cada vez más nuestra ancestralidad, que es tan rica y que me llena. Latinoamérica tiene una riqueza cultural y ancestral sublime.




Foto: Pablo Bruno




En este sentido, una de las canciones que sobresalen en el disco es 

“Cordillera y quebracho”, una chacarera que reflexiona sobre los desmontes y reivindica a los organismos de derechos humanos

. La particularidad también es la participación del cantor y guitarrista santiagueño 

Raly Barrionuevo

, afincado hace varios años en Unquillo. "Hablando con Raly, que vive por acá, le comenté que me gustaría que participe en la canción, porque cuando la compuse escuchaba su voz", cuenta Bruno. "

'Yo soy argentino y elevo mi canto/ latinoamericano, cordillera y quebracho'

, dice la letra. La importancia de la unión de Latinoamérica. Raly es un referente, me he criado escuchando su música. Es hermoso que haya estado y compartido conmigo", resalta el artista que, dice, admira y siente afinidad artística con 

Duratierra

. Mery Murúa, Paola Bernal, 

Ramiro González

, Lisandro Aristimuño y 

José Luis Aguirre

, entre otros.




"Cordillera y quebracho" es una canción que compuso hace un tiempo. "En Buenos Aires estaban por cerrar un hospital público histórico y ahí empezó a brotar la idea de la canción. Empecé a escribir de varias cosas y vi fotos del actual Gobierno utilizando imágenes con el Nunca Más de una forma muy incoherente; poniendo en dudas ciertas cosas que ya estaban muy firmes en la memoria de la argentinidad", recuerda. "Ni hablar acá en Córdoba que siempre atravesamos desmontes y que 

intentan quemar gran parte de los bosques

 para hacer negocios inmobiliarios

. Toda esa sensación me movilizó y también la importancia de nuestra educación pública, que es una de las mejores del mundo. La canción también nombra a las Abuelas de Plaza de Mayo como ejemplo de lucha en todo el mundo. Una lucha con firmeza y amorosidad".




La entrada 

"Debemos cuidar el hogar que habitamos, el hogar-cuerpo, el hogar-tierra"

 se publicó primero en 

Agencia de Noticias Tierra Viva

.

title: CNT convocará huelga general el 11 de noviembre para reclamar salarios dignos y el derecho a la vivienda
content:
La Confederación Nacional del Trabajo (CNT) ha acordado por consenso de todas sus regionales convocar huelga general el próximo 11 de noviembre. La organización anarcosindicalista se suma así al llamamiento del Sindicato de Inquilinas para impulsar una jornada de movilización en torno al acceso a la vivienda y el encarecimiento del coste de la vida.




La convocatoria plantea siete objetivos que relacionan las condiciones laborales con el acceso a una vivienda digna. Entre ellos figuran el incremento generalizado de los salarios, la reducción progresiva de la jornada laboral hasta las 30 horas semanales, el aumento de las pensiones públicas y la adopción de medidas que garanticen la estabilidad en el empleo y en el acceso a la vivienda habitual.




Uno de los ejes de la huelga es que el coste de la vivienda resulte compatible con unos ingresos dignos. CNT reclama que las personas trabajadoras no tengan que destinar más de un tercio de su salario neto mensual al pago de la vivienda, así como una reducción y regulación efectiva de los precios del alquiler. La tabla reivindicativa incluye el establecimiento de contratos de arrendamiento indefinidos, mecanismos de protección frente a las subidas abusivas de las rentas y medidas que impidan que los desahucios pongan en riesgo la continuidad laboral de las personas afectadas.




La organización también reclama medidas contra la especulación inmobiliaria y a favor de la función social de la vivienda. Entre sus propuestas figuran la posibilidad de expropiar inmuebles residenciales vacíos en manos de fondos de inversión y sociedades especulativas cuando concurran las condiciones planteadas en la tabla reivindicativa, así como un impuesto progresivo sobre la riqueza y la gran propiedad inmobiliaria destinado a financiar políticas de vivienda social. Asimismo, plantea la suspensión de los desahucios de vivienda habitual cuando no exista una alternativa habitacional adecuada y la coordinación de las administraciones, los servicios sociales y las empresas para evitar situaciones de exclusión.




La tabla reivindicativa incluye también un incremento de las pensiones públicas, contributivas y no contributivas, vinculado a la evolución salarial y al principio de suficiencia de las prestaciones. CNT plantea que su financiación y carácter público se refuercen mediante mayores cotizaciones empresariales a la Seguridad Social.




Desde la organización se vincula esta convocatoria con el conjunto de las condiciones de vida y de trabajo. «

La vivienda no puede abordarse al margen de los salarios y las condiciones laborales. Necesitamos que los ingresos permitan cubrir las necesidades básicas, que la jornada deje tiempo para vivir y que el acceso a una vivienda digna no dependa de soportar alquileres inasumibles

», declaró Nieves Román, secretaria general del sindicato.




La huelga se convoca en un contexto de movilización laboral en distintos sectores. En la Comunidad de Madrid, el profesorado de la educación pública tiene convocada una huelga indefinida desde el 14 de octubre, que se suma a las que ya se están produciendo por el resto del estado. Las trabajadoras de educación infantil de 0 a 3 años mantienen otra huelga indefinida iniciada en abril. En el ámbito sanitario, los sindicatos médicos han protagonizado sucesivas movilizaciones durante 2026 en el conflicto por el Estatuto Marco. Estas convocatorias responden a reivindicaciones específicas de cada sector, pero reflejan la existencia de conflictos laborales que siguen abiertos.




CNT señala asimismo la necesidad de que la movilización tenga en cuenta a quienes sufren con mayor intensidad la precariedad y la falta de protección laboral. Entre estos colectivos se encuentran las mujeres que desempeñan trabajos de cuidados, frecuentemente infravalorados, y las personas migrantes, que pueden afrontar mayores obstáculos para defender sus derechos laborales y sociales.




«

La defensa de la vivienda digna tiene que ir acompañada de la defensa de los derechos laborales y de los servicios públicos. Queremos que esta convocatoria contribuya a conectar las distintas luchas y a dar respuesta a los problemas cotidianos de quienes sostienen la sociedad con su trabajo

», concluyó Román.




La convocatoria del 11 de noviembre busca reunir estas reivindicaciones en una jornada de movilización que vincule el derecho a la vivienda con el poder adquisitivo, el empleo, las pensiones y la protección social. CNT plantea que la huelga sirva también para dar continuidad a las luchas y fortalecer la organización colectiva de las personas trabajadoras.




La entrada 

CNT convocará huelga general el 11 de noviembre para reclamar salarios dignos y el derecho a la vivienda

 se publicó primero en 

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

title: Milano, la fabbrica degli arresti falsi: persone innocenti sacrificate per fare carriera
content:
La Procura di Milano indaga su un sistema di arresti costruiti con false accuse e verbali manipolati. Tra le vittime un sedicenne. Nelle chat degli agenti: «Gli abbiamo rovinato la vita». Un’inchiesta che scuote la credibilità della Polizia locale e solleva interrogativi sui controlli e sull’impunità.




da 

Osservatoriorepressione




Un ragazzo di sedici anni viene fermato, accusato di detenzione di droga e resistenza a pubblico ufficiale. La versione ufficiale racconta un intervento antidroga e un arresto giustificato dai comportamenti del giovane. Ma nelle conversazioni tra gli stessi appartenenti alla Polizia locale di Milano emerge una storia radicalmente diversa. Una agente, che non risulta indagata, contesta ai colleghi le modalità dell’intervento: la droga non sarebbe appartenuta al ragazzo, la resistenza sarebbe stata attribuita a un adolescente trascinato giù dalla bicicletta e schiacciato sull’asfalto. Secondo la sua ricostruzione, gli sarebbe stato contestato un reato mai commesso. E in una delle conversazioni acquisite dagli investigatori compare la frase che restituisce tutta la gravità della vicenda: «Gli abbiamo rovinato la vita».




Non è una denuncia proveniente dall’esterno, né soltanto la versione di una persona arrestata che contesta l’operato degli agenti. Sono parole pronunciate da chi aveva partecipato all’intervento e che, confrontandosi con un collega, ne metteva in discussione la legittimità. È uno degli elementi più inquietanti dell’inchiesta della Procura di Milano, raccontata da Rosario Di Raimondo su la Repubblica il 9 ottobre e approfondita nei giorni successivi da altre testate. Un’indagine che ipotizza l’esistenza di un sistema di arresti illegali, costruiti attraverso informatori, cittadini utilizzati come esche e verbali contenenti circostanze che gli agenti avrebbero falsamente dichiarato di avere osservato.




Le contestazioni sono tuttora al vaglio dell’autorità giudiziaria e le responsabilità penali devono essere accertate. Ma la dimensione dell’inchiesta impedisce già di liquidarla come una semplice irregolarità procedurale. Secondo le ricostruzioni pubblicate, gli indagati sono arrivati a sedici, compresi due civili utilizzati come esche; sei agenti sono al centro della richiesta di custodia cautelare in carcere avanzata dai pubblici ministeri Giovanni Tarzia e Francesca Celle. Cinque erano già stati arrestati nell’agosto scorso, prima che la misura fosse attenuata. Tra i reati contestati a vario titolo figurano arresto illegale, falso, calunnia e peculato. L’inchiesta prende in esame numerosi episodi e oltre trenta contestazioni, anche se gli interventi direttamente al centro della ricostruzione del presunto sistema sono, allo stato delle notizie disponibili, dieci.




Una macchina per produrre arresti




Il meccanismo descritto dagli inquirenti non assomiglia a un errore occasionale commesso durante un intervento concitato. Secondo la Procura, sarebbe stato un metodo ripetuto, nel quale la selezione delle persone da colpire, la costruzione delle operazioni e la successiva redazione degli atti seguivano uno schema riconoscibile.




Al centro c’era un informatore con precedenti penali, inserito nell’ambiente dello spaccio, che indicava agli agenti le persone da arrestare e i luoghi nei quali cercare gli stupefacenti. Ma l’informatore non avrebbe agito per semplice collaborazione con le autorità. Secondo gli investigatori, aveva interessi propri nella gestione della piazza di spaccio e utilizzava il rapporto con gli agenti anche per colpire persone considerate concorrenti o nemiche. In una conversazione intercettata, uno degli indagati osservava che l’uomo voleva liberarsi dei propri avversari. Un altro descriveva il rapporto come reciprocamente vantaggioso.




Se questa ricostruzione verrà confermata, ci troveremmo davanti a un rovesciamento della funzione stessa dell’attività antidroga: non più l’apparato pubblico che utilizza informazioni per perseguire reati, ma un soggetto coinvolto nel mercato illegale che orienta l’azione degli agenti secondo i propri interessi. La forza coercitiva dello Stato sarebbe stata così messa, almeno in alcuni episodi, a disposizione delle rivalità interne a quel mercato.




La seconda parte del meccanismo prevedeva l’impiego di persone esterne alla Polizia locale, utilizzate come esche per avvicinare i bersagli e organizzare incontri finalizzati alla presunta cessione di stupefacenti. Non si trattava, secondo l’accusa, di normali attività investigative regolarmente autorizzate. La Procura contesta l’utilizzo di modalità sotto copertura non consentite agli agenti coinvolti e, soprattutto, la successiva rappresentazione falsificata di quanto avvenuto.




Il passaggio decisivo arrivava infatti con la compilazione dei verbali. Una volta fermata la persona, gli agenti avrebbero descritto operazioni differenti da quelle realmente compiute, arrivando a dichiarare di avere assistito direttamente a cessioni di droga che, secondo gli investigatori, non erano mai avvenute. In questo modo la ricostruzione destinata al magistrato avrebbe trasformato una situazione costruita artificialmente in un arresto apparentemente regolare.




Da Corsico a Milano, la flagranza costruita




Uno degli episodi più significativi riguarda un intervento del luglio scorso. Secondo la ricostruzione investigativa riferita da RaiNews, un uomo sarebbe stato attirato a un appuntamento con un’esca a Corsico, fuori dal territorio comunale milanese. Gli agenti lo avrebbero quindi caricato su un’automobile e trasportato nei pressi di un distributore di benzina a Milano, dove sarebbe stata simulata una situazione di arresto in flagranza.




La circostanza è particolarmente rilevante perché non riguarda soltanto un particolare inesatto inserito in un verbale. Riguarda il luogo stesso dell’intervento, la sequenza degli avvenimenti e la rappresentazione dei presupposti giuridici dell’arresto. Se confermata, significherebbe che gli agenti avrebbero modificato la scena dell’operazione per attribuirle una legittimità che non possedeva nelle condizioni reali in cui si era svolta.




È anche attraverso gli approfondimenti su queste operazioni e l’esame delle comunicazioni tra gli agenti che l’indagine ha assunto dimensioni più ampie. La documentazione digitale avrebbe consentito agli investigatori di confrontare ciò che veniva raccontato privatamente con ciò che era stato dichiarato negli atti ufficiali. Proprio questo confronto costituisce uno dei nuclei più importanti dell’accusa: le discrepanze non riguarderebbero soltanto valutazioni soggettive, ma fatti materiali, presenze, luoghi e comportamenti attribuiti alle persone arrestate.




«Siamo… stupefacenti»: le chat che smentiscono i verbali




Il gruppo WhatsApp utilizzato dagli agenti aveva un nome che oggi assume un significato particolarmente amaro: «Siamo… stupefacenti». Al suo interno, secondo l’inchiesta, venivano commentati gli interventi e gli arresti. Ma il contenuto di quelle conversazioni non coincideva sempre con le versioni riportate nei documenti ufficiali. È questa distanza tra il linguaggio privato degli operatori e gli atti destinati alla magistratura che ha permesso agli investigatori di ricostruire il presunto sistema.




Il caso del sedicenne è particolarmente grave proprio perché una collega avrebbe contestato apertamente ciò che era stato fatto. Il ragazzo, secondo la ricostruzione riferita nelle conversazioni, era stato fermato mentre si trovava in bicicletta, trascinato a terra e accusato di possedere droga rinvenuta altrove. La stessa agente avrebbe denunciato l’attribuzione di una resistenza che, a suo giudizio, non si era verificata. Non era quindi soltanto in discussione la provenienza dello stupefacente, ma l’intera costruzione delle accuse.




Un elemento merita di essere sottolineato: l’agente che espresse quelle contestazioni non risulta indagata. Le parole sulla vita rovinata appartengono a lei, non a una confessione collettiva dei sei agenti accusati. La distinzione è importante, ma non riduce la portata delle conversazioni: dimostra che, almeno in quell’occasione, all’interno dello stesso gruppo operativo esisteva una contestazione esplicita delle modalità dell’arresto.




L’indagine solleva quindi anche una questione relativa ai meccanismi di controllo interno. Se un’operatrice aveva riconosciuto e denunciato informalmente una condotta che considerava illegittima, quali strumenti aveva per segnalarla formalmente? Quali controlli venivano effettuati sulle relazioni di servizio? Chi verificava la corrispondenza tra le operazioni realmente svolte e i risultati comunicati ai superiori? Sono domande che non riguardano soltanto la responsabilità penale degli indagati, ma l’organizzazione del lavoro e le garanzie predisposte per impedire abusi.




Gli arresti come risultati da esibire




Un altro elemento emerso dall’inchiesta riguarda il rapporto tra numero degli arresti e avanzamento professionale. Secondo gli investigatori, alcune conversazioni tra gli agenti suggeriscono che l’elevato numero di operazioni potesse essere utilizzato per sostenere le ambizioni di carriera della commissaria Ilenja Sabato, indicata come responsabile della squadra. Nelle conversazioni riportate dalla stampa si fa riferimento alla possibilità di ottenere una posizione organizzativa, con il relativo riconoscimento economico.




Non è ancora dimostrato che questa fosse la motivazione effettiva delle condotte contestate. Ma il tema è rilevante perché mette in discussione un criterio frequentemente utilizzato per rappresentare l’efficienza delle politiche di sicurezza: il numero degli arresti.




Quando un’amministrazione misura i risultati prevalentemente attraverso quantità di controlli, denunce, sequestri e arresti, diventa indispensabile interrogarsi su come quei risultati vengano prodotti. Un numero elevato di persone fermate non dimostra, da solo, una maggiore tutela della collettività. Può documentare un’attività investigativa efficace, ma non dice nulla, se isolato dal resto, sulla legittimità delle procedure, sulla fondatezza delle accuse o sugli esiti giudiziari.




L’inchiesta milanese mostra il rischio più grave che può manifestarsi quando il risultato statistico diventa un obiettivo autonomo: la persona sottoposta a controllo rischia di trasformarsi in uno strumento attraverso il quale produrre un risultato professionale. Non più un individuo titolare di diritti, ma un arresto da registrare, un’operazione da comunicare, un numero da aggiungere al bilancio dell’attività repressiva.




Le accuse di appropriazione di beni e di utilità ricevute dall’informatore aggiungono un ulteriore livello alla vicenda. Secondo quanto riportato da Repubblica, tra gli episodi esaminati figurano la consegna di gioielli a una commissaria e l’appropriazione di una bicicletta elettrica del valore di circa mille euro da parte di un agente. Anche queste circostanze dovranno essere verificate giudiziariamente, ma indicano che l’indagine non si limita alla contestazione di procedure investigative irregolari.




Il potere di scrivere la verità ufficiale




La questione più importante che emerge da questa storia riguarda il valore attribuito alla parola di chi indossa una divisa. Un verbale di polizia non è una semplice opinione. È un atto pubblico che entra nel procedimento penale e contribuisce alla formazione delle decisioni giudiziarie. La sua funzione presuppone che chi lo redige descriva fedelmente ciò che ha visto e compiuto, senza inventare circostanze, alterare sequenze o attribuire a una persona comportamenti inesistenti.




È necessario ricordare che il giudice non è obbligato a credere automaticamente a ogni affermazione contenuta in un verbale: deve valutare gli elementi disponibili secondo le regole del procedimento. Ma è altrettanto evidente che gli atti redatti dagli operatori costituiscono spesso una parte essenziale della prima ricostruzione dei fatti, soprattutto quando l’arrestato non dispone immediatamente di immagini, testimoni o altri elementi per contestarli.




La disparità è concreta. Da una parte ci sono operatori pubblici dotati di poteri coercitivi, strumenti investigativi e capacità di produrre documentazione ufficiale. Dall’altra può esserci un sedicenne, una persona migrante, un lavoratore precario o qualcuno che non conosce sufficientemente il sistema giudiziario e non dispone delle risorse necessarie per difendersi efficacemente.




Se un verbale contiene fatti inventati, il problema non riguarda soltanto il falso documentale. Riguarda la possibilità che un’intera procedura giudiziaria venga orientata da una ricostruzione non corrispondente alla realtà. L’arrestato può perdere la libertà, subire conseguenze familiari, scolastiche e lavorative, affrontare spese legali e portare per anni le conseguenze di un’accusa infondata.




Non è stato possibile verificare, dalle fonti consultate, l’intero percorso giudiziario e la durata dell’eventuale privazione della libertà del sedicenne. Sarebbe quindi scorretto attribuirgli una specifica permanenza in carcere senza ulteriori riscontri. Resta il fatto che la Procura contesta la legittimità dell’intervento e che le conversazioni pubblicate descrivono un’accusa ritenuta falsa dalla stessa agente che vi aveva partecipato.




Non basta parlare di mele marce




La difesa degli agenti respinge la ricostruzione accusatoria. Secondo quanto riportato da RaiNews, i legali riconoscono la discutibilità di alcuni metodi ma sostengono che gli arresti fossero fondati. Sarà il giudice a valutare le richieste cautelari e, nelle successive fasi processuali, le responsabilità individuali.




Ma l’esistenza di un procedimento penale non esaurisce la questione istituzionale. Se venisse confermato che più operatori hanno partecipato ripetutamente alla costruzione di arresti illegali, non basterebbe spiegare tutto attraverso la condotta deviante di alcuni individui. Occorrerebbe comprendere come abbiano potuto operare, quali controlli siano mancati, perché le anomalie non siano state intercettate prima e quale cultura organizzativa abbia eventualmente favorito la ricerca di risultati a scapito della legalità.




È significativo che il caso di Corsico sia emerso anche grazie alle contestazioni dell’arrestato, alle verifiche sulle immagini e all’attività difensiva. Non è stato sufficiente il verbale a chiarire i fatti: è stato necessario sottoporlo a una verifica esterna. La documentazione prodotta dagli stessi agenti è diventata così oggetto dell’indagine, anziché essere considerata il suo punto di arrivo.




Questo è il nodo che attraversa molte vicende di abusi istituzionali. L’apparato che esercita la forza è spesso anche quello che produce la prima versione ufficiale del suo esercizio. Se mancano strumenti indipendenti di controllo, la possibilità di ricostruire quanto accaduto può dipendere dalla presenza casuale di una telecamera, dalla disponibilità di testimoni, dalla capacità di un difensore di individuare contraddizioni o, come in questa inchiesta, dall’esistenza di conversazioni digitali che raccontano una realtà differente.




La tutela della legalità richiede quindi verifiche indipendenti, tracciabilità delle operazioni, conservazione delle immagini, controlli sui verbali e procedure che consentano agli stessi operatori di segnalare condotte illegittime senza subire pressioni o ritorsioni. Non si tratta di presumere che ogni agente menta. Si tratta di costruire un sistema nel quale nessun agente possa sottrarsi al controllo soltanto perché rappresenta un’autorità pubblica.




La sicurezza non può essere costruita sulla privazione illegale della libertà




C’è infine un problema che riguarda il modello di sicurezza urbana. Milano, come molte altre città, conosce da anni un dibattito nel quale lo spaccio di strada, il degrado e la presenza di persone marginalizzate vengono frequentemente utilizzati per giustificare l’intensificazione dei controlli. Ma proprio in questo contesto il rispetto delle garanzie diventa essenziale.




La lotta allo spaccio non autorizza l’invenzione di reati, l’utilizzo illegale di operazioni sotto copertura o la manipolazione degli atti. La presenza di mercati illegali non sospende i diritti delle persone che vi sono coinvolte e non trasforma la polizia in un soggetto autorizzato a scegliere quali regole rispettare. Se lo facesse, la legalità che si dichiara di difendere diventerebbe il primo principio sacrificato.




Il caso del sedicenne rappresenta il punto più drammatico dell’inchiesta. Una persona ancora minorenne sarebbe stata coinvolta in un’operazione della quale una stessa agente contestava la fondatezza. La gravità non sta soltanto nell’eventuale falsificazione dell’accusa, ma nella sproporzione tra il potere esercitato e la condizione di chi lo ha subito. Per un operatore un arresto può diventare una voce nel resoconto dell’attività svolta. Per chi viene arrestato può rappresentare un evento destinato a segnare profondamente la propria esistenza.




È questa la distanza che le parole emerse dalle chat rendono impossibile ignorare.




L’inchiesta della Procura di Milano deve ora accertare le responsabilità dei singoli e verificare ogni episodio contestato. Ma l’amministrazione comunale e il comando della Polizia locale hanno una questione ulteriore da affrontare: capire se le procedure interne fossero adeguate, quali segnali siano stati ignorati e come impedire che risultati operativi apparentemente positivi nascondano violazioni dei diritti fondamentali.




La legalità non può essere misurata soltanto dal numero delle persone arrestate. Deve essere misurata anche dalla capacità delle istituzioni di impedire arresti illegali e di accertare le responsabilità di chi li compie.




Un sistema di sicurezza nel quale un verbale falso può trasformarsi in una privazione della libertà non ha soltanto un problema con alcuni operatori. Ha un problema con il controllo del potere che ha affidato loro.




E la domanda più urgente non è se sia ancora possibile fidarsi delle divise. È quali garanzie esistano affinché nessuna divisa possa sostituire i fatti con una versione conveniente.

Navenda Lêkolînê ya ASALê rapirsiya xwe ya meha Cotmeha 2026an aşkere kir. 




Rapirsiya "Ajandaya Siyasî ya Tirkiyeyê ya Cotmeha 2026an" di navbera 4-10ê Cotmeha 2026an de hatiye kirin.




Lêkolîna ku li 28 bajaran bi 2 hezar 20 kesan re hatiye kirin. Li gorî lêkolînê CHP bi rêjeya ji sedî 5,1ê daketiye rêza şeşemîn.




Di rapirsiyê de rêjeya kesên bêbiryar û yên ku dibêjin "ez deng nadim" pir bilind e ku ji ber vê yekê nexşeya siyasî hîn zelal nebûye.




Berî belavkirina dengên bêbiryaran, ji sedî 18,8ê beşdaran gotiye ku ew bêbiryar in, ji sedî 15,4 jî gotiye ku ew dê deng nedin û ji sedî 3,6 jî diyar kiriye ku ew ti ramana wan tune an jî naxwazin bersivê bidin.




AK Partî, Partiya NÛ û DEM Partî li pêş in




Piştî belavkirina rêjeyên dengên bêbiryaran, ango yên ku gotiye ew dê deng nedin û yên ku bersiv nedaye, AKP bi rêjeya ji sedî 31,6 di rêza yekem de û Partiya NÛyê bi rêjeya ji sedî 25,2 di rêza duyem de cih girt.




DEM Partiyê bi rêjeya ji sedî 8,8 di rêza sêyem de, MHPyê bi rêjeya ji sedî 8,0 di rêza çarem de û ÎYÎ Partiyê bi rêjeya ji sedî 7,1ê di rêza pêncem de cih girt.




CHP bi rêjeya ji sedî 5,1ê ya dengan di rêza şeşem de ye.




Berî belavkirina dengên bêbiryar




Berî belavkirina dengan, AK Partî ji sedî 19,6, Partiya NÛ ji sedî 15,7 û DEM Partî ji sedî 5,5 piştgiriyê digirin.




MHP ji sedî 5,0, ÎYÎ Partî ji sedî 4,4, CHP ji sedî 3,2, Partiya Zaferê jî ji sedî 2,1 hatine pîvandin.
