author: Administrador
title: Denuncia der Vollversammlung der Kollektive der zapatistischen autonomen Regierungen. A.C.G.A.Z. Gemeinschaftliche Regierungen. Chiapas, Mexiko. 8. Oktober 2026.
content:
Vollversammlung der Kollektive der zapatistischen autonomen Regierungen. (A.C.G.A.Z.) Gemeinschaftliche Regierungen. Chiapas, Mexiko. 8. Oktober 2026.

An die Pueblos Mexikos und der Welt. An die Compañeros und Compañeras des Congreso Nacional Indígena – CNI. An die mexikoweite und internationale Zivilgesellschaft. An die Sexta Nacional e Internacional. An die Menschenrechtsorganisationen. An die alternativen Medien. An die mexikoweite und internationale Presse. An diejenigen, die die Erklärung für das Leben unterzeichnet haben.

Denuncia: Wir prangern energisch und öffentlich den Angriff, das Schikanieren und die Inhaftierung unserer Compañeros der zapatistischen Unterstützungsbasen des Ejido La Culebra, zugehörig zum Caracol 9 Nueva Jerusalen, offizieller Landkreis Ocosingo in Chiapas, Mexiko an – unterstützt von den drei Ebenen der schlechten Regierung der 4T [jetzige Regierung der sogenannten IV. Transformation], mit ihren folgenden Zielsetzungen:

Erstens: Das Hauptziel der schlechten Regierung ist es, den Unterstützungsbasen der EZLN ein Ende zu machen, damit es sie in keinem Dorf, Ejido, Gemeinde, Ortschaft oder Siedlung in Chiapas geben soll. Deshalb greift sie die zapatistischen Unterstützungsbasen direkt an.

Zweitens: Es ist ein Plan der aktuellen schlechten Regierungen, um der zapatistischen Autonomie ein Ende zu bereiten: In diesem Fall möchten sie der autonomen Bildung ein Ende setzen, sowie ihrer autonomen Regierung. Und ebenso wollen sie die verschiedenen ehrenwerten Organisationen, die es gibt, erledigen.

Drittens: Durch Personen im Ejido La Culebra, die der politischen Partei, welche der Pyramide Gestalt gibt, der Partei der Bewegung der nationalen Erneuerung [Morena] angehören – wurden am 21. September 2026, um 16:00, unsere vier Compañeros der zapatistischen Unterstützungsbasen inhaftiert: wegen dem einzigen Delikt, sich zu weigern, ihre Kinder in die offizielle Schule einzuschreiben, denn unsere Compañeros haben ihre eigene autonome Schule. Als sie sahen, dass unser Compañeros ihren Widerstand aufrecht erhielten, begannen sie sie zu demütigen, zu bedrohen, unter Druck zu setzen, 2.500 Pesos Strafe zu zahlen und ein Dokument zu unterschreiben.

Diese Compañeros wurden daraufhin von den [zapatistischen] autonomem Verantwortlichen der Zone eingeladen, zu informieren, was ihnen gerade geschieht. Bei der Rückkehr ins Ejido wurden sie erneut gerufen, und es wurde ihnen gesagt, dass sie ein erneutes Delikt begangen haben: indem sie darüber informierten, was gerade passiert und es reine Lüge ist, worüber sie informierten. Deshalb wurden sie erneut mit 2.500 Pesos bestraft; somit sind es 5.000 Pesos für jede*n.

Wegen dieser Aktionen sind zwei unserer Compañeros gekommen, um die Verantwortlichen der Zone darüber zu informieren. Und am 3. Oktober 2026 wurde der Compañero SEBASTIAN PEREZ GUTIERREZ wegen des Delikts, seine Kinder nicht in die offizielle Schule zu schicken, inhaftiert. Sie sagten ihm, es wären blanke Lügen, worüber sie erzählt [informiert] hätten. Als die 24 Stunden Haft um waren, wurde er am 4. Oktober 2026 vor den Vorsitz des Ejido geführt, und sie forderten von ihm, seine Kinder in die offizielle Schule zu schicken. Der Compañero leistete Widerstand, indem er sagte, jene haben kein [Recht], das zu erzwingen, denn sie selbst haben ja einen eigenen autonomen Bildungsbereich. Deshalb wurde ihm gedroht, wurde er unter Druck gesetzt, eine Strafe von 10.000 Pesos zu zahlen. Der Compañero leistete Widerstand und akzeptierte es nicht, deshalb steckten sie ihn erneut in den Knast.

Am 4. Oktober 2026, um 17:00 wurde unser Compañero DANIEL LOPEZ AGUILAR inhaftiert. Sein Delikt besteht darin, die Compañeras gefahren zu haben, die von den autonomen Autoritäten der Zone geladen waren, um über diesen Fall zu informieren.

Viertens: Am 4. Oktober 2026 wurden 16 Compañeras der Unterstützungsbasen vor den Ejido-Vorsitz gerufen, einer nach der anderen. Ihnen wurde gesagt, sie hätten den Fehler begangen, vor ihren autonomen Autoritäten Lügen zu erzählen und müssten somit eine Strafe von 500 Pesos anerkennen. Als gesehen wurde, dass unsere Compañeras ihren Widerstand aufrecht erhalten, die Zahlung der Strafe über 500 Pesos nicht zu akzeptieren, wurden sie gedemütigt, gezwungen, unter Druck gesetzt und bedroht, vor die Vollversammlung des Ejido gestellt zu werden, wenn sie nicht akzeptieren. Angesicht der Druck- und Droh-Situation akzeptierten die Compañeras, baten sich aber einen Zahlungsaufschub von 20 Tagen aus.

Fünftens: Dem Compañero MIGUEL ANGEL CRUZ DÍAZ wurde eine Strafe von 2.000 Pesos sowie 24 Stunden Knast auferlegt, weil er argumentierte, dies [s.o.] sei ungerecht, und sagte, es sei ein Recht zu informieren und einen Verteidiger/ Verteidigung zu suchen.

Drei andere Compañeros Unterstützungsbasen, mit Namen MARIANO PEREZ LÓPEZ, MARCOS LÓPEZ MENDOZA und ANTONIO PÉREZ LÓPEZ, welche Gemeindepolizisten sind, wurden auch inhaftiert und später mit 150 Pesos für jeden bestraft. Einer wegen des Delikts, zu sehen und zu kommentieren, diese Aktionen seien ungerecht.

Liste der Geldstrafen: SEBASTIAN PÉREZ GUTIERREZ: 8.000 Pesos, sowie 68 Stunden Gefängnis. DANIEL LÓPEZ AGUILAR: 7.000 Pesos, sowie 48 Stunden Gefängnis. SEBASTIAN PEREZ LOPEZ: 5.000 Pesos. FELIPE PEREZ LOPEZ: 5.000 Pesos. MARIANO PEREZ LOPEZ: 5.000 Pesos. MANUEL CRUZ ENCINO: 5.000 Pesos. Gemeindepolizisten: MARIANO PEREZ LÓPEZ: 150 Pesos, sowie 12 Stunden Gefängnis. MARCOS LÓPEZ MENDOZA: 150 Pesos, sowie 12 Stunden Gefängnis. ANTONIO PÉREZ LÓPEZ: 150 Pesos, sowie 12 Stunden Gefängnis. 16 Compañeras, weil sie über das Geschehen informiert haben; jede: 500 Pesos. Insgesamt: 8.000 Pesos. Noch ein Compañero: MIGUEL ANGEL CRUZ DIAZ: 2.000 Pesos, sowie 24 Stunden Knast. FAUSTO DIAZ PEREZ: 1.000 Pesos. FELIPE PERES GUTIERREZ: 1.000 Pesos. JUAN DIAZ PEREZ: 1.000 Pesos. Die drei Letztgenannten, weil sie nicht bei der Anwendung der Ungerechtigkeit gegen ihre eigenen Compañeros interveniert [teilgenommen] haben.

Gesamte Geldstrafen: 48.450 Pesos.

Sechstens: Diese Aktionen von Ungerechtigkeit sind erzeugt durch das Projekt der schlechten Regierung, über welches der Servidor de la Nación [ein Regierungsbeamter] am 24. September 2026 ankam zu sprechen: das Programm der 4T [der jetzigen mexikanischen Regierung]: »Die Schule ist unser« – unter direktem Vorsitz des Lehrers USEBIO CRUZ RUIZ, zusammen mit dem Ejido-Komissionar MARCELO GRUZ PEREZ und seinem Vertreter MANUEL CRUZ HERNANDEZ.

Dieses Programm zwingt sie, mehr Kinder in der Schule zu haben, mit dem Ziel sich derart die ökonomische Unterstützung zu vergrößern. Aus diesem Grund zwingen sie unsere Compañeros, ihre Kinder in die offizielle Schule einzuschreiben.

Siebtens: Ungerechte Aktionen und Dinge, die die drei Ebenen der schlechten Regierungen anordnen gegen die Autonomie unserer Pueblos.

Die Compañeros werden gezwungen, für Landbesitz, Elektrizität, Beiträge innerhalb der offiziellen Schulen zu zahlen, ohne jeglichen Nutzen davon zu erhalten – mit dem Argument der usos y costumbres [traditionellen, üblichen Handhabungen], egal ob diese die individuellen und kollektiven Rechte unserer Compañeros der zapatistischen Unterstützungsbasen verletzen. Wir zahlen diese Abgaben/ Steuern nicht, jedoch erhalten wir auch nichts durch die schlechten Regierungen.

Dies ist, was die falsch benannte 4T lehrt; wir wissen nicht, wie viele Schriftstücke die Vollversammlung [des Ejido] hat; denn sie zwingen trickreich, Blanko-Papiere zu unterzeichnen, ohne den Inhalt zu wissen; mit dem Trug, es handele sich dabei um das Herumreichen der Anwesenheitsliste.

Achtens: Hier nehmen wir die Gelegenheit wahr, Euch zu sagen: Diese Warnung geht an die gesamte mexikanische Bevölkerung. Unsere Compañeros des Ejido La Culebra werden mit der Bildung, dem Bildungsbereich angegriffen, mit dem Programm der 4T: »Die Schule ist unser«. Anderen Pueblos kann dies mit dem Wasser, dem Land, dem Gesundheitsbereich, der Rechtsprechung geschehen, um nur einige zu erwähnen. Somit: Achtung! Geschwister auf dem Land und in der Stadt.

Neuntens: Auch erklären wir, dass wir mit den Repräsentanten der Organisation namens LAS 23 REGIONES [Die 23 Regionen] gesprochen haben, denn wir wussten, sie haben Leute ihrer Organisation innerhalb des Ejido. Wir vertrauten ihnen, denn sie versprachen, mit ihren Compañeros zu reden. Aber anstatt sie losgingen und mit ihren Leuten persönlich redeten, dass sie unsere Compañeros nicht weiter angehen sollen, taten sie dies nur mittels Mails.

Als wir sie das zweite mal riefen, sagten sie, sie hätten sich bereits distanziert, gehörten nicht mehr ihrer Organisation an und hätten mit dem Problem nichts mehr zu tun. Wir wussten dann, dass sie gelogen haben, denn zwei Anführer der »23 Regionen« haben ihre Compañeros dabei unterstützt, als angeblich die letzte Vereinbarung getroffen wurde: Wo unter Demütigung und Druck erzwungen wurde, ein Dokument zu unterschreiben, um ihre Kinder in die offizielle Schule einzuschreiben und zu bestätigen: was sie den autonomen Autoritäten der Zone erzählt haben, seien reine Lügen gewesen.

Zehntens: Brüder und Schwestern der Pueblos Mexikos und der Welt, wir glauben nicht, dass es in diesem kapitalistischen System Hoffnung auf Gerechtigkeit gibt, denn immer haben sie auf der Grundlage von Ungerechtigkeiten gelebt. Jedoch wollen wir Euch sagen, was für uns zapatistische Pueblos Gerechtigkeit bedeutet: dass unsere Compañeros in Widerstand und Rebellion weiter fortfahren werden; so wie wir von der schlechten Regierung nichts erhalten, geben wir ihr auch nichts. Das heißt, unsere Compañeros werden weder Abgaben für Strom noch für Land zahlen.

Unsere Compañeros des Ejido La Culebra werden dort leben, und dort werden sie kämpfend sterben. Deshalb werden sie mit ihrer autonomen Schule fortfahren, sie werden nicht die ungerechten Geldstrafen zahlen, im Gegenteil: die übergebene Menge an Geldstrafe muss zurückgegeben werden.

Diese Aktion der Ungerechtigkeit kann jede*r verstehen; denn es ist klar zu sehen: Es ist der Plan des Herrn, des Vorarbeiters, des Verwalters und Aufsehers der Vierten Transformation.

Elftens: Wir wissen, dass die Regierungen der 4T (MORENA-PVEM-PT-Parteien) mit solchen Sabotagen auch die Reise nach Mexiko-Stadt, um die Familien Sucherinnen zu umarmen, verhindern möchte.

Das alles, weil es sie sorgt, dass die Lüge »Alles läuft gut in Mexiko, alle sind glücklich« auffliegt.

Warum zwingen sie nicht die tausenden von Privatschulen, worin tausende Familien ihre Kinder haben? Weil alle wissen, das Bildungswesen, das die Regierung gewährt, ist Müll, und weil sie Angst haben, dass diese Familien rebellieren. Sie verletzen [mit der Erzwingung in offizielle Schulen sich einzuschreiben] auch die Verfassung und die Menschenrechte der Pueblos originarios.

Zwölftens: Wenn sie die Reise für das Leben – Kapitel Mexiko so sehr sorgt, ist es doch sehr einfach: Es reicht, die Forderung nach Wahrheit und Gerechtigkeit aller Gruppen, Kollektive, Organisationen und Bewegungen der Familien Sucherinnen zu erfüllen. Somit bräuchten sie sich nicht mit uns zu treffen. Und anstatt nach Mexiko-Stadt würden wir nach Guadalajara, in Jalisco gehen, um ihnen sauberes Wasser aus Quellen zu bringen, die von der Mutter Erde und ihren Bewahrer*innen geschützt werden.

Dreizehntens: Und all das, weil die Wahlen kommen, und sie Wahlausweise sammeln für ihren üblichen Betrug und um dem organisierten Verbrechen zu gefallen.

Pueblos Mexikos und der Welt, wir möchten Euch sagen: Hier machen wir weiter, und hier werden wir weitermachen mit unserem Plan, wir sehen uns bald in Mexiko-Stadt.

Hochachtungsvoll. Gemeinschaftliche Regierung der 12 zapatistischen Caracoles.

author: anred
title: «De acá me sacan muerto»: intentaron desalojar a una comunidad mapuche tehuelche en favor de una empresa
content:
El operativo se realizó el jueves 8 de octubre en el paraje La Japonesa, sobre la costa del río Colorado. La Policía de Río Negro y personal judicial llegaron al territorio de la comunidad Lof Peñi Núñez-Álvarez para ejecutar una orden de desalojo impulsada por la firma Exelia S.A. Tras la resistencia y la tensión generada, los efectivos se retiraron y el procedimiento quedó suspendido. El conflicto tiene antecedentes judiciales y de violencia contra integrantes de la comunidad. Por ANRed




La comunidad mapuche Lof Peñi Núñez-Álvarez enfrentó el jueves un nuevo intento de desalojo en el paraje La Japonesa, departamento de Avellaneda, provincia de Río Negro. Efectivos policiales y personal del Poder Judicial se presentaron en el territorio para ejecutar una orden de desahucio en el marco de una causa promovida por la empresa Exelia S.A. El operativo estuvo encabezado por el oficial de Justicia Marcelo Orofilo.




Desde el territorio, integrantes de la comunidad denunciaron la presencia de niños y niñas y anunciaron que permanecerían en el lugar para defender sus viviendas y sus animales. Ante la gravedad de la situación, reclamaron el acompañamiento de organizaciones sociales, comunidades originarias y organismos de derechos humanos.




Finalmente, la Policía se retiró y el desalojo quedó suspendido. Sin embargo, la amenaza judicial continúa vigente y mantiene a las familias en estado de alerta.




Una disputa territorial con antecedentes




El conflicto judicial se remonta a una sentencia de abril de 2023, cuando el Juzgado Civil de Choele Choel hizo lugar a la demanda de Exelia S.A. y ordenó el desalojo de tres fracciones del Lote X. La decisión alcanzó terrenos ubicados en La Japonesa, donde las familias mapuches tehuelches desarrollan actividades de subsistencia y crían animales.




En junio de 2026, el Superior Tribunal de Justicia de Río Negro rechazó un recurso presentado por la defensa de la comunidad, dejando firme la orden de desalojo. La resolución fue cuestionada por quienes defienden el territorio, que reivindican la ocupación ancestral y los derechos reconocidos a los pueblos originarios.




En agosto, los representantes legales de la comunidad promovieron un planteo de nulidad. Sostuvieron que las parcelas mencionadas en la orden judicial no coincidirían con los terrenos que efectivamente ocupan las familias. Según la presentación, un informe de agrimensura permitió identificar diferencias entre las fracciones incluidas en el mandamiento y las tierras donde viven y desarrollan su economía de subsistencia.




El expediente también expone una discusión sobre la documentación que acredita la propiedad. Según reconstrucciones periodísticas, Exelia S.A. se constituyó en 1974 y en 1978 recibió las fracciones en disputa mediante un aporte de capital de su entonces titular, Umberto Francisco Conforti. La reconstrucción de la cadena de titularidad anterior y el arraigo histórico de las familias forman parte de los cuestionamientos al reclamo empresarial.




Exelia S.A. y las tierras en disputa




La firma Exelia S.A. es la demandante que obtuvo la sentencia favorable para recuperar las fracciones en litigio. La comunidad y referentes del Parlamento Mapuche Tehuelche cuestionan el origen de los títulos y denuncian que la disputa reproduce una historia de desplazamientos de familias indígenas en la zona.




Según los testimonios recogidos por medios regionales, las familias Álvarez y Núñez tienen vínculos con ese territorio que anteceden a la constitución de la sociedad anónima. Sus integrantes sostienen que sus abuelos y padres vivieron allí durante generaciones y que la crianza de ovejas, chivas, vacas y caballos constituye parte de su forma de vida.




Referentes mapuches también describieron un proceso histórico en el que empresas llegadas desde Buenos Aires se presentaron con documentación sobre los campos y, en algunos casos, dejaron a las familias originarias en condición de puesteras. Tras el abandono de esos territorios por parte de algunas firmas, varias familias regresaron a reivindicar los lugares donde habían vivido sus antepasados.




El conflicto de La Japonesa vuelve a poner en discusión la distancia entre los títulos registrales invocados en los tribunales y los derechos territoriales de comunidades indígenas cuya presencia histórica es anterior a la formación de las sociedades que reclaman esos predios.







URGENTE | RÍO NEGRO: INTENTAN DESALOJAR A LA COMUNIDAD ÁLVAREZ NÚÑEZ




En el paraje La Japonesa, sobre la Costa del río Colorado, efectivos policiales junto a un oficial de Justicia se presentaron este miércoles para avanzar con el desalojo de integrantes de la Comunidad Mapuche Lof Peñi Núñez-Álvarez.




Según denuncian desde la comunidad, el oficial de Justicia se identificó como Marcelo Orofilo. En el territorio permanecen integrantes de la comunidad, entre ellos niños y niñas, y anunciaron que resistirán el desalojo.




La situación tiene antecedentes judiciales. En abril de 2023, el Juzgado Civil de Choele Choel hizo lugar a una demanda de Exelia S.A. y ordenó el desalojo de tres fracciones ubicadas en el paraje La Japonesa.




En junio de este año, el Superior Tribunal de Justicia de Río Negro rechazó el recurso de queja presentado por integrantes de la comunidad, dejando firme esa instancia del proceso.




Sin embargo, en agosto la comunidad presentó un nuevo planteo de nulidad. Allí sostuvo que las parcelas sobre las que se pretende ejecutar el desalojo no se corresponden con las tierras que efectivamente ocupan, donde viven y desarrollan su economía de subsistencia. El expediente judicial registra además que el mandamiento de desahucio se encontraba en proceso de ejecución.




La comunidad reivindica la posesión actual, tradicional y pública del territorio y sostiene que su presencia en la zona se remonta a varias generaciones. El conflicto se encuentra atravesado por el reclamo territorial mapuche y por la discusión sobre el reconocimiento de sus derechos indígenas.




Desde el territorio realizan un llamado urgente a las comunidades mapuche de la zona, organizaciones sociales y organismos de derechos humanos para acompañar la resistencia y permanecer atentos ante el avance del operativo.




Asimismo, responsabilizan al Gobierno de Río Negro por cualquier hecho de violencia que pueda producirse durante el procedimiento.




— ANRed #30Años (@Red__Accion) 

October 8, 2026







En 2021 denunciaron una agresión contra el lonko




El intento de desalojo no es un episodio aislado en la historia de la comunidad. En agosto de 2021, integrantes del Parlamento Mapuche Tehuelche de Río Negro denunciaron una grave agresión contra Alberto Núñez, lonko de la comunidad Álvarez Núñez. En aquel entonces, Núñez circulaba en moto junto a otro integrante de la comunidad cuando fueron atropellados y posteriormente golpeados y amenazados para que abandonaran el territorio. El hecho ocurrió en un contexto de conflicto territorial y de reclamos por el relevamiento de las tierras indígenas.




La denuncia se produjo después del denominado Foro Consenso, realizado en Bariloche, donde se debatió la posesión de tierras en la Patagonia con participación de sectores empresariales y políticos. Organizaciones mapuches advirtieron entonces sobre el crecimiento de los discursos estigmatizantes y su relación con el hostigamiento hacia las comunidades.




Los antecedentes de violencia denunciados por la comunidad muestran que la disputa no se limita a un expediente judicial: también comprende la defensa cotidiana de las familias frente a las amenazas y presiones para abandonar el territorio.




La defensa del territorio continúa




La comunidad Lof Peñi Núñez-Álvarez reivindica la posesión actual, pública y tradicional de las tierras, así como su derecho a continuar viviendo allí y sosteniendo sus actividades productivas.




El caso se inscribe en un escenario más amplio de conflictos territoriales en Río Negro y otras provincias, donde comunidades indígenas enfrentan órdenes de desalojo, litigios por la propiedad y denuncias de criminalización. La situación adquiere especial relevancia en un contexto de cuestionamientos a las políticas de protección territorial indígena y de avance de los intereses privados sobre tierras rurales.




Aunque el operativo del jueves terminó con el retiro de los efectivos, la amenaza de desalojo no desapareció. Las familias continúan defendiendo su permanencia en La Japonesa, mientras reclaman que se respeten sus derechos territoriales y se investiguen las irregularidades que denuncian en el proceso de adjudicación de las tierras.

La principal central obrera del país marchó “para visibilizar la realidad del sector productivo y alertar sobre la difícil situación que atraviesa, en especial la de las PyMEs, principal sostén del empleo” en un documento donde advirtió por “un deterioro general de la calidad de vida de la población que pone en riesgo la paz y la convivencia”. Continúa pendiente el anuncio de una medida de fuerza.

La manifestación “en defensa de la industria nacional” partió de la sede del Sindicato de Mecánicos y Afines del Transporte Automotor (SMATA) y fue hasta el ex Ministerio de Industria, en la ciudad de Buenos Aires, con la participación de sindicatos y movimientos sociales.




El acto central estuvo a cargo del triunvirato que conduce la central. Allí, el cosecretario Cristian Jerónimo, dirigente de las y los empleados de la industria del Vidrio, dijo en su discurso: “Acá está el motor que mueve la Argentina, acá está la fuerza del trabajo, acá estamos los que creemos en la justicia social, los que no estamos dispuestos a entregar nuestras conquistas, nuestros derechos”, afirmó.




Y agregó: “Acá estamos los que queremos una Argentina distinta y lo tienen que escuchar estos funcionarios que están acá enfrente nuestro”. El dirigente exigió al Gobierno que convoque “a una mesa de producción”, al sector empresario y a los representantes de los trabajadores para discutir “qué clase de modelo de país queremos”.

Jerónimo cuestionó: “Antes de hablar de recuperar nuestras Malvinas, piensen en los 15 millones de compatriotas que están sumergidos en la pobreza, dejen de ser caraduras”, dijo, y preguntó: “¿Dónde están los 18 mejores meses que nos prometieron? Lo único que vemos es cómo se siguen perdiendo puestos de trabajo, cómo se endeudan las familias”.




El cosecretario general también apuntó contra el Congreso y la dirigencia política en general: “La política toda, que se dejen de hacer los distraídos. El Congreso, basta de joder. El pueblo realmente se va a enojar y los va a pasar por encima. Necesitamos el compromiso de la dirigencia política del campo nacional y popular”. En ese marco, reivindicó un “Estado presente, transparente”, y advirtió: “No creemos en un Estado subsidiario, pero tampoco creemos en un Estado que se desentienda de los problemas estructurales que tiene la gente”.







EL PUEBLO TRABAJADOR SALIÓ A DEFENDER EL FUTURO DE LA ARGENTINA




Frente a un modelo que privilegia la especulación, profundiza la recesión y condena a miles de familias a la incertidumbre, el movimiento obrero organizado reafirmó su compromiso con la producción nacional, el empleo y la justicia social.




Necesitamos un país que produzca, genere oportunidades y garantice derechos.




— CGT (@cgtoficialra) 

October 9, 2026







La marcha fue convocada bajo el lema “Las Malvinas son argentinas, la industria nacional también” y contó con la participación de dirigentes del transporte, servicios y comercio exterior, entre ellos Juan Carlos Schmid (CATT), Daniel Mallotti (Aduana), Mariano Vilar (Conductores Navales), Juan Pablo Brey (Aeronavegantes), Graciela Aleñá (Viales Nacionales), Roberto Coria (Guincheros) y Mario Preiss (Caucho), entre otros representantes gremiales.




En el escenario, entre ellos, reapareció Eduardo Duhalde, máximo responsable político de la Masacre de Avellaneda el 26 de junio de 2002 donde fueron asesinados Maximiliano Kosteki y Darío Santillán.




La jornada culminó con el anuncio de que la CGT se sumará el jueves próximo a la quinta Marcha Federal Universitaria el 15 de octubre, donde confluirán con las dos CTA y organizaciones estudiantiles, políticas y sociales.




Compartimos el documento de la CGT:




Las Malvinas son Argentinas, la industria nacional también




​El diagnóstico de situación es claro: estamos ante un gobierno que lleva adelante un modelo político, económico y social monitoreado por el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI), en función de intereses que no son los nuestros. Un modelo que está destruyendo el sistema productivo nacional, sobre todo el de las pequeñas y medianas empresas, con aumento de la desocupación, deterioro de los ingresos y de las condiciones laborales, brutal caída del consumo interno y signos claros de recesión; alta presión impositiva, desplome de la inversión, falta de financiamiento y costos desmedidos de los servicios públicos.




​Las consecuencias también son claras y están a la vista: una situación social angustiante, creciente pobreza y marginalidad; cientos de miles de hogares con carencias alimentarias severas y un endeudamiento familiar descontrolado que dispara graves alarmas en materia de salud mental; jubiladas y jubilados en condiciones de precariedad existencial que no pueden comprar siquiera sus medicamentos; personas con discapacidad sin atención; desfinanciamiento del sistema de salud, del sistema educativo, de la investigación científica, de la obra pública, de la infraestructura vial y del transporte. En definitiva, un deterioro general de la calidad de vida de la población que pone en riesgo la paz y la convivencia.




Hoy nos movilizamos en defensa de la industria nacional para visibilizar la realidad del sector productivo y alertar sobre la difícil situación que atraviesa, en especial la de las PyMEs, principal sostén del empleo. Este achicamiento no solo involucra quebrantos empresariales, sino que también implica un daño que agudiza las dificultades en la cadena de pagos y debilita los entramados productivos regionales. No estamos proponiendo una economía cerrada, sino la necesidad de configurar una apertura comercial inteligente, en función de nuestros recursos y de nuestras posibilidades, pero con la certeza de que ningún país se desarrolla sin industria.







MARCHAMOS CONTRA EL INDUSTRICIDIO: “NO PODEMOS PERMITIR QUE DESTRUYAN EL PAÍS DE ESTA FORMA”




El movimiento obrero organizado volvió a expresarse en defensa de la industria, el empleo y la soberanía productiva.




“Nuestro principal propósito es luchar por las fuentes de trabajo, el pan en la mesa y, sobre todo, por el desarrollo de una industria que fue modelo”.




— CGT (@cgtoficialra) 

October 9, 2026







​No hay dos velocidades en este programa económico vigente: hay dos economías. Una, para muy pocos, concentrada en sectores que capturan la mayor parte de la renta. Y la otra, la de la microeconomía popular, que transitamos cotidianamente las grandes mayorías, donde «la plata no alcanza» y la situación de las y los trabajadores -ocupados, subocupados, precarizados y desocupados- es cada vez peor.




Este gobierno ya ha dado claras muestras de que las argentinas y los argentinos no son su prioridad. En su fanatismo ideológico, todos los días confirma su insensibilidad, su falta de empatía y la clausura de toda posibilidad de diálogo institucional.




​Por tanto, en defensa de una Argentina con producción, desarrollo y trabajo digno, nos cabe la tarea de organizar allí donde todavía no hay organización y de construir alternativas consistentes, políticamente confiables y participativas, capaces de conmover y contener a todas aquellas personas y organizaciones que no queremos convalidar este estado de cosas: el de un país para unos pocos.




​Frente a estas propuestas del «sálvese quien pueda», nosotros proponemos otra idea de sociedad, donde la dignidad del trabajo, como experiencia solidaria de intercambio y colaboración, siga siendo una construcción colectiva a favor del bien común y del desarrollo personal y familiar, en el marco de una comunidad integrada.




​




Porque NO HAY LIBERTAD SIN JUSTICIA SOCIAL




​CONSEJO DIRECTIVO NACIONAL




8 DE OCTUBRE DE 2026

La CGT movilizó “en defensa de la industria nacional”

author: Tom Sullivan
title: Housing protests lead to general strike in Spain
content:
“I haven’t managed to defend my house, but I have tried so that others can learn how to defend theirs.” These were the words of an 87-year-old Madrid woman, Maricarmen, who posted a video from her hospital bed after Spanish authorities evicted her from the apartment she had lived in for the past 71 years. In the video, she promoted an upcoming protest at Madrid’s Plaza del Sol “so that we can eliminate this problem once and for all”.

Her eviction sparked a fire across the Spanish state. Within days, protesters had set up an encampment in the Plaza del Sol, famously the site of mass anti-austerity protests in 2011. They quickly spread to dozens of other cities, along with mass protests. A few days later came the first victory of the movement, when the vulture fund that had bought Maricarmen’s apartment building agreed to allow her to return with a new, eight-year contract and her rent capped at 30 percent of her pension.

But this victory only fuelled the protests. On Saturday 3 October, nationally coordinated rallies saw around half a million people protest across the country. Three days later, the country’s two major union confederations called a general strike.

Few recent examples illustrate the power of protest as clearly as the last two weeks in the Spanish state. When the authorities forced their way into Maricarmen’s apartment, she was meant to be just another of the nearly 70 people who are evicted from their homes every day across the country. But the footage of her being removed on a stretcher into an ambulance tapped into a rage that millions of people feel living at the whim of the housing market.

In Spain, it is particularly sharp. Over the last decade, rental prices have risen by more than 80 percent, according to the National Institute of Statistics. And the market is becoming increasingly concentrated in the hands of a small minority. From 2008 to 2025, the share of single property owners fell by 4 percent, while the share of people with at least ten properties rose by 35 percent, according to a recent government report.

These statistics prove the main point of the Tenants’ Union, the group leading the protests: the main problem is that under capitalism, housing is a commodity for investors to make a profit from and not a basic good provided to all people. They’ve combined this general perspective with a series of concrete demands, including automatic renewal of rental contracts, a 50 percent rent reduction, and the expropriation of empty properties.

Importantly, the union’s approach has been to spread the protests, while also raising new, more radical slogans as the movement developed. In the first few days, the movement played out under the generally defensive slogan “Not one more Maricarmen”. But as the movement exploded, the slogan shifted to “towards a general strike,” directly calling on the two major union confederations to call one.

Since Maricarmen’s eviction, the government of Pedro Sanchez’s Socialist Party (PSOE) and its junior partner Sumar, heavily influenced by the Communist Party, has scrambled to respond. It put forward two bills in parliament, including measures such as a pause on evictions until 2030 and indefinite rental contract extensions, with twelve months’ compensation for tenants if landlords break the agreement. However, the government is a minority in parliament and, among other parties, it relies on the centre-right Catalan independence party, Junts, to pass any laws. Junts joined the right to defeat the two bills.

Even though the government put forward the bills knowing they would be defeated, the fact that they included reforms like a pause on evictions until 2030 illustrates the power of the movement. Similarly, the movement’s rejection of the bills as inadequate testifies to mass popular support for genuine solutions to the housing crisis and a radical approach to achieving them. A recent poll published in elDiario.es showed 73 percent support for a general strike, 58 percent support for the main encampment in Madrid, and that 40 percent of people would be prepared to engage in a rent strike.

With the bills defeated, however, Sanchez is dissolving parliament and calling snap elections for 29 November. It’s a shrewd political move. His message will be simple: the right-wing parties used their majority to block housing reform, so a majority Socialist Party government is necessary to get real action.

But Sanchez’s record shows how fickle this message is. He is a pro-capitalist, centre-left leader who has capitulated to the right on nearly every issue. On a key political issue in recent years, immigration, he has supported the hardline Fortress Europe approach, including deals with the Moroccan government to stop refugees from entering Spain. And although he has made some progressive symbolic gestures, like recognising Palestinian statehood and using tough language against US President Donald Trump, military spending has increased on his watch. Finally, over his eight years in government, he has done nothing to address the housing crisis, yet now seeks to campaign on the issue.

The Tenants’ Union has not refrained from attacking the Socialist Party and its junior partner, the Sumar coalition, in which the Communist Party is a major force. One of their main lines has been: “Eight days of people’s power has done more than eight years of progressive government”. Similarly, the union has publicly accused Sumar of cynically attempting to channel the protests into their own re-election campaign.

The movement therefore faces a major test in the coming election period. Several encampments made important statements, saying they would not wind them up just because of the election. A spokeswoman for the Tenants’ Union told the media, “Our struggle will not wait for some electoral calendar”. The next challenge is to make the general strike as big as possible and not let the election suck the air out of the movement.

Union officials are undoubtedly trying to subordinate the general strike to the government’s re-election campaign and have yet to announce a date. But the declaration of a general strike is a huge victory for the movement. It has lifted people’s expectations about what’s possible and how to achieve it. And the fact that it took barely two weeks from Maricarmen’s eviction to achieve it shows the potential for mass movements to grow.

The general strike is the most powerful tool the working class has. Millions of ordinary people will collectively withdraw their labour and impose their class interests on the bosses and government. By doing so, workers in the Spanish state are teaching us all how to deal effectively with the housing crisis.

author: Unknown
title: AB-Çin mutabakatı: Hibrit araç ihracatı yarıya inecek, Çin pazarına erişim iyileştirilecek
content:
Fotoğraflar: Unsplash, Kolaj: Evrensel

Avrupa Birliği (AB) ve Çin, hibrit araç ihracatının yarıya indirilmesi, Çin pazarına erişimin iyileştirilmesi ve nadir toprak elementlerine yönelik ihracat lisanslarının kolaylaştırılması konusunda "ortak anlayışa" vardı.

AB Komisyonunun Ticaretten Sorumlu Üyesi Maros Sefcovic, Çin Ticaret Bakanı Wang Wentao ile Pekin'de gerçekleştirdiği görüşmenin ardından yaptığı açıklamada "AB-Çin ticaretinin gerçek anlamda yeniden dengelenmesi gerekiyor" ifadesini kullandı. Sefcovic, Bakan Wentao ile bu doğrultuda ortak bir anlayışa ulaştıklarını bildirdi.

Sefcovic, söz konusu anlayışın hibrit elektrikli araç (HEV) ve şarj edilebilir hibrit elektrikli araç (PHEV) ihracatının yarıya indirilmesini, Çin pazarına erişimin iyileştirilmesini ve nadir toprak elementlerinin ihracatına yönelik lisans süreçlerinin daha da kolaylaştırılmasını kapsadığını belirtti.

Varılan ortak anlayışı "ilk adım" olarak nitelendiren Sefcovic, gerçek anlamda gösterilen iş birliği çabasını ve samimi yaklaşımı memnuniyetle karşıladığını ifade etti. Sefcovic, tarafların ocak ayına kadar yeniden bir araya geleceğini söyledi.

AB ile Çin arasında son dönemde elektrikli araçlara uygulanan gümrük vergileri, ticaret dengesizlikleri ve Çin'in nadir toprak elementlerine yönelik ihracat kısıtlamaları nedeniyle ticari gerilimler yaşanıyor.

AB, Çin pazarına erişimde karşılaşılan engellerin kaldırılmasını ve kritik ham madde tedarikinin güvence altına alınmasını isterken, taraflar ticari anlaşmazlıkların müzakereler yoluyla çözülmesine yönelik temaslarını sürdürüyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: ABD ve Rusya'nın dizel anlaşması: Moskova, milyonlarca ton dizel yakıt tedarik edecek
content:
ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin ile yaptığı görüşmede, Rusya'nın ABD ve küresel piyasalara milyonlarca ton dizel yakıt tedarik etmesi konusunda mutabık kaldıklarını bildirdi. ABD Hazine Bakanlığı da Rusya menşeli dizelin satışı, teslimi, gemiden boşaltılması ve ithalatı dahil ilgili işlemlere 7 Nisan 2027'ye kadar izin verdi.

Truth Social hesabından konu hakkında paylaşım yapan Trump, Putin'le yaptığı görüşmenin "son derece başarılı" geçtiğini belirterek "Rusya'nın Amerikan ve küresel pazara derhal 300 bin tonun üzerinde, kasım ayı boyunca ilave 500 bin ton ve hemen ardından da 1 milyon ton dizel yakıt tedarik etmesi konusunda mutabakata varıldı" ifadesini kullandı.

Trump, Rusya'nın buna ek olarak dizel rafinerilerinin durumuna bağlı olarak kısa süre içinde 3 milyon ton dizel yakıtın teslimatını yapacağını kaydetti.

Hürmüz Boğazı üzerinde "tam kontrolü" olduğunu savunan Trump, Rus enerjisine yönelik bu duyurunun da etkisiyle ABD'de ve dünyada dizel fiyatlarının hızla düşerek rekor düşük seviyelere ineceğini​​​​​​​ öne sürdü.

Trump, daha düşük fiyatların özellikle ABD'li çiftçiler, hayvancılıkla uğraşanlar ve nakliyeciler için öncelik taşıdığını vurguladı. Bunun önemli bir duyuru olduğunu belirten Trump, ayrıca İran'ın nükleer silaha sahip olmasına izin verilmeyeceğini kaydetti. ABD Hazine Bakanlığı geçici lisans yayımlayacak

Öte yandan, ABD Hazine Bakanlığının sosyal medya hesabından yapılan açıklamada, Rus motorininin küresel piyasaya arzına izin vermek amacıyla geçici bir genel lisansın derhal yayımlanacağı bildirildi.

Açıklamada, "Bugün, Başkan Trump'ın talimatı doğrultusunda, Yabancı Varlıklar Kontrol Ofisi (OFAC), Rus motorininin küresel piyasaya arzına izin vermek amacıyla geçici bir genel lisansı derhal yayımlıyor" ifadesine yer verildi.

Trump'ın açıklaması sonrası Kremlin'in internet sitesinde Putin'in imzasıyla yayımlanan açıklamada, "Rus tarafı, ABD ve dünya piyasalarına petrol ve petrol ürünleri tedarik etmeye hazır olduğunu teyit etti. Bunun küresel ekonominin tamamına olumlu yansıyacağına inanıyorum" denildi.

Putin, görüşmede Ukrayna krizinin çözümüne yönelik olasılıkların kapsamlı şekilde değerlendirildiğini, İran'daki durumun ve ikili ilişkilerin çeşitli boyutlarının da ele alındığını belirtti.

İki ülke liderleri arasındaki doğrudan temasların sürdürülmesi konusunda mutabık kaldıklarının altını çizen Putin, başkanlık yönetimleri, istihbarat servisleri ve diğer kurumlar arasındaki işbirliğinin de devam edeceğini kaydetti.

Ukrayna Devlet Başkanı Volodimir Zelenskiy, Rusya’ya yönelik yaptırımların hafifletilmesini “açık bir zayıflık göstergesi” olarak nitelendirerek, “Rusya, dizel yakıtın karşılığını daha fazla terör ve ihanetle ödeyecektir. Rusya'nın petrol ürünleri satmasına izin vermek, sona erdirilmesi gereken bir savaşa yatırım yapmak anlamına gelir.” dedi.

Trump’ın, Putin ile bir telefon görüşmesi gerçekleştirdiğini ve bu görüşmenin farklı bir sonuca yol açtığını belirten Zelenskiy, kısa süre önce Avrupa’nın Rus oligarklara yönelik yaptırımları kaldırma kararı aldığını hatırlatarak, “O tarihten bu yana Rus saldırıları ve insanların çektiği acılar yalnızca arttı” ifadesini kullandı.

Rusya’nın, üzerindeki baskının hafifletilmesini sağlayacak kapalı kapılar ardındaki anlaşmalara bel bağladığı görüşünü dile getiren Zelenskiy, “Rusya ile gerilimin açık ve kalıcı biçimde azaltılmasını öngören bir anlaşma olmadan Rusya'ya yönelik yaptırımların hafifletilmesi, açık bir zayıflık göstergesidir. Bu, Rusya'nın işine yarar; daha fazla insan öldürmesine, savaşı daha uzun süre sürdürmesine, Amerika'ya daha da az saygı göstermesine ve dünyaya daha büyük kayıplar ve zararlar vermesine olanak tanır” ifadelerini kullandı. Zelenskiy, Ukrayna’nın gerilimi azaltmaya yönelik karşılıklı adımlar atmaya hazır olduğunu vurgulayarak, Rus petrol rafinerilerine ve diğer petrol tesislerine yönelik saldırılarının, Moskova’nın Ukrayna'nın enerji sektörüne karşı saldırılarına cevap olduğunu kaydetti. ABD’ye, Rusya’nın Ukrayna’daki enerji altyapısına saldırmaması halinde Rus petrol rafinerilerine saldırmayacakları bir anlaşma önerisinde bulunduklarını anımsatan Zelenskiy, ABD’nin bu uzlaşmayı sağlayabilecek güce sahip olduğuna dikkati çekti. Zelenskiy, “Putin'e verilen hediyeler, barış getirmeyeceği gibi medeni dünyaya da hiçbir fayda sağlamayacaktır. Rusya, dizel yakıtın karşılığını daha fazla terör ve ihanetle ödeyecektir. Rusya'nın petrol ürünleri satmasına izin vermek, sona erdirilmesi gereken bir savaşa yatırım yapmak anlamına gelir, oysa bu savaş uzatılmamalıdır. İhtiyaç duyulan şey, Rusya ile karşılıklılık temelinde gerilimin gerçekten azaltılmasıdır” değerlendirmesinde bulundu.

Zelenskiy ayrıca, ABD'nin Ukrayna'nın savunmasına adil biçimde destek vermesini ve Rusya ile bu doğrultuda güçlü bir görüşme gerçekleştirmesini beklediklerini sözlerine ekledi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Mario Trujillo
title: Resisting the Menace of Federal Data Consolidation
content:
In the past two years, the federal government has unlawfully consolidated data exposing our private information.

This consolidation has been chaotic but generally came in three rolling waves: It started with DOGE, moved to agency-to-agency data sharing with ICE, and then attempted data-driven purges of state voter rolls.

We all deserve to live in a world where the data we use to pay our taxes, receive benefits, and vote is not combined and weaponized against us. The amalgamation of data leads to mistakes, abuses, and a lack of trust in institutions meant to protect us. Overall, it can chill our participation in society. This is particularly true for groups disfavored by this administration—especially immigrants and protesters.

Congress highlighted similar abuses—including the creation of enemies lists and snooping on activists and federal employees—following the McCarthy and Watergate eras. And the increasing use of computers to magnify those harms led Congress to pass a slate of protections like the federal Privacy Act of 1974.

The good news is that many people have stepped forward to resist the federal government’s unprecedented and unlawful data consolidations. Many groups, including EFF, have filed lawsuits to enforce our data privacy laws, and many states have, too. Legislators at the federal and state levels have worked to expose and oppose these surveillance programs. And many people have protested for their right to data privacy.

Existing data privacy protections have been essential in the past two years, but they can be improved. This should include: narrowing loopholes and increasing enforcement in existing laws, limiting the government’s purchase of data on the commercial market, and passing a comprehensive consumer privacy law.

Starting on January 20, 2025, President Trump created DOGE—essentially renaming an existing agency originally meant to modernize government technology. Rather than engage in modernization, DOGE quickly obtained high-level access to sensitive databases across the government that store millions of people’s personal records—including at the Office of Personnel Management (OPM), the Social Security Administration, and the Treasury Department.

DOGE was staffed with people with little government or cybersecurity knowledge and who often had conflicts of interest. DOGE’s early aim was not always clear, aside from gaining “prompt access to all unclassified agency records” and the “sharing and consolidation” of those records.

The result? The indiscriminate firing of government employees and the decimation of important agencies that focused on consumer protection and foreign aid. It also resulted in clear misuses of data. For example, while working with DOGE at the Social Security Administration, one individual signed an outside agreement with an advocacy group with the aim of using SSA data to find evidence of alleged voter fraud and “overturn election results in certain States.”

DOGE’s data access and consolidation violated the federal Privacy Act, which limits the sharing and consolidation of government databases. Many groups stepped in to sue. For example, EFF and our co-counsel at Lex Lumina LLC and Democracy Defenders Fund, on behalf of two public employee unions (AFGE and AALJ), sued the OPM for unlawfully disclosing federal workers’ information to DOGE. After EFF and others secured early victories, the government sought to end the lawsuits by firing many DOGE agents and removing their access to records. A great deal of damage remains in need of a judicial remedy.

Even as DOGE’s influence diminished, federal agencies have attempted to share, compare, and seize large databases, in order to target immigrants. In some cases, they have succeeded. This happened with tax records at the IRS, Medicaid data from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), and public housing data from the Department of Housing and Urban Development. The Department of Agriculture also sought to collect databases regarding Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Programs (SNAP) from states.

Many groups have filed lawsuits to block this anti-immigrant-motivated data consolidation, alleging it violates privacy protection laws. EFF filed amicus briefs in support of two of these lawsuits: Centro de Trabajadores v. Bessent, which concerns IRS data; and California v. HHS, which concerns Medicaid data (and where we teamed up with EPIC and Protect Democracy). Most recently, states have stepped up to challenge the federal government’s attempted seizure, for immigration enforcement purposes, of state commercial driver’s license data held by the American Association of Motor Vehicle Administrators, a non-profit organization.

This data consolidation for immigration enforcement has also included government purchase of commercial products. This includes ICE’s purchase of commercial location data without a warrant, and its interest in “Big Data and Ad Tech providers.” ICE also has contracts with companies like Palantir, which help organize all the datasets the agency collects.

The right to vote is fundamental to every democracy. That’s why EFF has long advocated for cybersecurity in voting systems, to make sure every vote is properly counted.

Voter purges are a longstanding threat to the right to vote. State and local officials regularly delete people from the voter registration rolls, often for bad reasons and without adequate notice. This has a disparate impact against people of color.

Now the federal government is trying to purge voters, too. To do so, it has consolidated our data in three ways. First, it is using an old data system called SAVE for a new purpose: checking voter eligibility. Second, it has seized voter information from states. Third, it has created a federal list of eligible voters.

As a direct result, people with a right to vote will be purged from voter rolls because of erroneous data. Others will be intimidated from voting or registering. And all registered voters suffer a violation of their data privacy rights: information collected for one purpose is being used against them for another purpose.

Since 1986, the federal government has operated SAVE, which stands for Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements. It is not a database, but it facilitates easy access to databases. It is used to determine whether immigrants and naturalized citizens are eligible for various government benefits, such as food stamps.

In 2025, the federal government started using SAVE for a new purpose: checking voters’ eligibility. Further, SAVE now provides access to new databases and allows bulk searches. More than 60 million voters have been run through SAVE, and 21,000 were flagged as potential noncitizens who are ineligible to vote. Erroneous flags have caused purges of lawful voters – such as Anthony Nell.

A case called League of Women Voters v. DHS challenges this expansion of SAVE. The plaintiffs are represented by CREW, Democracy Forward, the Fair Elections Center, and EPIC. A federal judge held this program unlawful and set it aside. DHS appealed and asked for a stay of this order, and a federal appellate court denied the stay. Unfortunately, the U.S. Supreme Court granted the stay, exercising its controversial “shadow docket” authority by a six-to-three vote.

Federal employees in DHS’s “Fraud Detection and National Security Unit,” which ordinarily investigates alleged immigration fraud, have been re-assigned to examine voter eligibility. A whistleblower alleges that employees have been directed to go to state election agency websites, enter some of a voter’s personal information, and thereby access more of it. This may violate state laws requiring a person, before accessing a voter’s information, to attest they are that voter or have that voter’s authorization.

Since 2025, the federal government has demanded that at least 48 states hand over their voter information. At least 16 states have complied. The federal government is running this information through SAVE, searching for voters to purge.

The federal government has sued 30 states for refusing to comply. So far, courts have dismissed 25 of these suits. There’s also a lawsuit against this data grab, titled Common Cause v. DOJ, brought by CREW, Protect Democracy, and the ACLU.

In March 2026, President Trump issued an executive order requiring DHS to create a list of people who are U.S. citizens, aged 18 or older, and residents of the state. The order also requires DOJ to prosecute anyone, including state and local officials, who provides a ballot to a person who is not eligible to vote in federal elections.

In California v. Trump, 24 states allege that this executive order violates the Constitution’s separation of powers. A federal judge enjoined this program, and an appellate court denied a stay. But the U.S. Supreme Court by a six-to-three vote granted a stay, which allows the program to move forward. (By a seven-to-two vote, the Court denied a stay of an injunction against a different part of the same executive order, which concerned mail-in ballots.) Another legal challenge, titled EPIC v. USCIS, alleges that the new federal voter eligibility list violates the Privacy Act as well as the separation of powers.

It is encouraging to see so many people, groups, and states step forward to protect our data privacy from these unlawful waves of federal data consolidations. Still, more work remains. For example:

The Privacy Act of 1974 has proven a critical bulwark. But after a half century, it could use a refresh. For example, Congress should close its loopholes and expand its enforceability.

Law enforcement agencies must be prohibited from avoiding the Constitution’s warrant requirement by buying our personal data from brokers. For example, Congress should pass the “Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act.”

We need a comprehensive consumer data privacy law, among other reasons to reduce the flood of our personal data that corporations provide to law enforcement agencies. Legislators should check out EFF’s “privacy first” framework.

In the meantime, there’s no time like the present to practice surveillance self-defense, like using strong passwords and disabling your phone’s ad identification.

title: 15 yaş altına sosyal medyayı yasaklayan yönetmelik Resmi Gazete'de yayımlandı
content:
Fotoğraf: Zulfugar Karimov/Pexels

Resmi Gazete’de yayımlanan yeni yönetmeliğe göre, 15 yaşından küçükler sosyal ağları kullanamayacak.

Resmi Gazete'de yayımlanan "Sosyal Ağ Sağlayıcı Tarafından Çocuklara Özgü Ayrıştırılmış Hizmet Sunulmasına ve Yaş Doğrulamaya İlişkin Yönetmeliği" ile 15 yaşını doldurmamış kimselere sosyal medya hesabı açma, kullanma ve yönetmenin engelleneceği duyuruldu.

Mevcut hesapların, 31 Mart 2027'ye kadar doğrulanması zorunlu kılınırken 15-18 yaş arası çocuklar için hesapların varsayılan olarak gizli olacağı, mesajlaşmanın kısıtlanacağı, canlı yayın açılması ve rehber senkronizasyonunun yasaklanacağı "ayrıştırılmış hizmet" modeli uygulanacak.

Bununla birlikte ailelerin çocukların ekran süresini, harcamalarını ve hesap ayarlarını denetleyebileceği Türkçe destekli ebeveyn kontrol araçları da ebeveynlere sunulacak.

Yönetmelik, 1 Kasım 2026'da yürürlüğe girecek.

5 soruda sosyal medya yasası: 15 yaş altını neler bekliyor?

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Supreme Court delivers landmark decision on Indigenous offenders and victims
content:
A Supreme Court of Canada decision on Friday has clarified the factors that judges should account for when a defendant and victim are both Indigenous.




The landmark case, 

R. v. Cope

, concerns Harry Arthur Cope, a Mi’kmaw man from Nova Scotia who pleaded guilty to assaulting his partner, a Mi’kmaw woman, in 2021.




The Supreme Court weighed in on a trial judge’s decision to sentence Cope to five years in prison and the Nova Scotia Court of Appeal’s decision to reduce that sentence to three years.




On Friday, the Supreme Court upheld the Nova Scotia Court of Appeal’s ruling, which accounted for Cope’s mental illness and substance use.




“The sentencing judge should have linked the mental health factor to the offender’s moral blameworthiness on the aggravated assault offence, but failed to do so,” wrote Justice Michelle O’Bonsawin, writing for the majority of the judges. “The court of appeal was therefore correct to intervene and it arrived at a just and appropriate sentence.”




Four of nine judges sided with the Nova Scotia provincial court’s original ruling, which dismissed recommendations from community members who proposed no further jail time and opted for a treatment program instead.




Anne Crawford, an Iqaluit lawyer who handles family and domestic violence cases, said the Supreme Court judgement uplifts the role that Indigenous victims, their families and their community should play in criminal sentencing.
















“It provides emphasis on the value of women, mothers and partners,” said Crawford, who has previously worked as a defence lawyer. “I think it’s part of a broader shift in Canadian society towards accountability for offenders.”




That shift includes changes to the Criminal Code that came into effect in June, she said. The law now defines murders “that occur within a pattern of coercive” behaviour toward an intimate partner as first-degree murders, and it asks courts to consider life imprisonment when somenone commits manslaughter within such a pattern.




“I don’t think our courts come anywhere near addressing what victims need,” Crawford added about the landmark judgement. “(But) I do think it comes closer to holding offenders to account.”




Twenty intervenors, including provincial and community prosecutorial services, legal aid centres, and organizations representing lawyers and Indigenous women, all participated in the hearings, held Dec. 11 and 12 at the Supreme Court in Ottawa.




Philippe Boucher, a doctoral candidate in legal studies at Carleton University, serves as a Gladue report writer, which provides judges with a portrait of an Indigenous offender before they decide the length and severity of a sentence.




He said the court’s message is that condemning violence doesn’t always require longer prison sentences.
















The Supreme Court judgement also provides guidance on how judges should balance their responsibility to avoid imprisonment when offenders are Indigenous with protecting Indigenous women and girls, Boucher said.




O’Bonsawin proposed a three-step test. Judges must first assess the gravity of the offence and responsibility of the offender in light of the Indigeneity of both the offender and the victim.




Second, they must identify what the sentence is meant to achieve while considering denunciation and deterrence, a key addition to the Criminal Code after the National Inquiry into Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls.




Third, they must chose a proportionate sentence with everything in context.




“What the Supreme Court said this morning is that denunciation and deterrence doesn’t automatically mean a custodial sentence, it doesn’t mean prison, and it can also be another alternative to detention,” he said.
