title: Fon skandalının siyasi ayağını haberleştiren gazeteciler Sevinç ve Balcı tutuklandı
content:
İstanbul'da fon krizini haberleştiren gazetecilere yönelik soruşturma, 9 Ekim Cuma günü iki tutuklamayla sonuçlandı. Gazeteci Şaban Sevinç ile Sözcü editörü Mustafa Balcı, İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığının talebi üzerine çıkarıldıkları sulh ceza hâkimliğince tutuklandı.




Gazetecilere Türk Ceza Kanunu'nun 217/A maddesinde düzenlenen “halkı yanıltıcı bilgiyi alenen yayma” suçlaması yöneltildi.




Aynı soruşturma kapsamında ifadeleri alınan gazeteciler Murat Ağırel ve İsmail Saymaz ise adli kontrol şartıyla serbest bırakıldı.




Soruşturmanın temelinde, Eylül 2026'da 7 portföy yönetim şirketinin işlemlerine yönelik incelemeler ve bu şirketlerin yönettiği yatırım fonlarından bazı siyasetçilerin, kamu görevlilerinin ve yakınlarının olağanüstü kazançlar elde ettiği iddiaları bulunuyor.




Gazetecilere yönelik soruşturmalar, fonların yönetimi ve yatırımcıların uğradığı kayıplar konusunda süren tartışmanın siyasi bağlantılar üzerinden iktidar çevrelerine yöneldiği sırada başladı. 



















Gazetecilere soruşturma: Mustafa Balcı gözaltına alındı




8 Ekim 2026

























Fon krizi sansür gerekçesi oldu: Yargı, haberleri, iktisatçı ve gazetecilerin hesaplarını engelliyor




24 Eylül 2026










Ömer Çelik ve Osman Arıkan Nacar'ın aynı karede 




Mustafa Balcı'nın gözaltına alınmasından önce sosyal medya hesabında yayımladığı fotoğraf, soruşturmanın en dikkat çekici ögeleri arasındaydı. 




Balcı, AKP Sözcüsü Ömer Çelik'in 22 Ağustos'ta Bodrum'da düzenlenen Limak Filarmoni Orkestrası konserine katıldığını ve hemen arkasındaki sırada fon soruşturmasında adı geçen Osman Arıkan Nacar'ın oturduğunu gösteren bir fotoğraf paylaştı. 




Balcı paylaşımında, Yeni Parti Genel Başkanı Özgür Özel'in, Nacar'ın daha önce Çelik'le birlikte tatil yaptığı ve 20 milyar lirayla yurt dışına çıktığını iddia ettiğini aktardı.




Paylaşılan fotoğraf, adı geçenlerin aynı etkinlikte birbirlerine yakın oturduklarını gösteriyor. Balcı da paylaşımında Nacar hakkındaki iddiaları kendisine ait kesinleşmiş bilgi olarak değil, Özel'in açıklamalarına atıfla aktarmıştı. 




Gazeteci, gözaltına alınmadan önce Basın Suçları Bürosunca ifadeye çağrıldığını duyurmuş, söz konusu fotoğrafı işaret ederek çağrının bununla ilgili olabileceğini belirtmişti. Ardından sosyal medya hesabından gözaltına alındığını açıkladı.




Sevinç de Nacar-Çelik ilişkisi iddiası gerekçesiyle suçlandı




Şaban Sevinç de aynı soruşturma kapsamında gözaltına alındı. Başsavcılığın ilk açıklamalarında Sevinç'in hangi sözlerinin veya paylaşımlarının gerçeğe aykırı kabul edildiği ayrıntılı biçimde belirtilmedi. Anadolu Ajansının aktardığı savcılık açıklamasına göre iki gazeteci hakkındaki işlem, AKP Sözcüsü Ömer Çelik hakkında kamuoyunu yanıltıcı açıklamalar yaptıkları iddiasına dayanıyor.




İki bakan hakkındaki fon iddiaları




Murat Ağırel ve İsmail Saymaz'ın soruşturulmasına yol açan gelişmeler ise 7 Ekim'de Sözcü TV'de yayımlanan programda gündeme geldi.




Yeni Parti İzmir Milletvekili Ümit Özlale, fonlardan iki bakanın kazanç sağladığı iddiasını dile getirmişti.




Ağırel, televizyon yayınında bu iddialardan birinin Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat'a yönelik olduğunu söyledi. Hedef Portföy, EFG Enerji ve başka şirketlerin adlarını anarak bazı yatırımcıların fon değerlerindeki yükselişten yararlandığı, ardından soruşturma başlamadan önce yatırımlarından çıktığı iddialarını aktardı.




Saymaz da aynı yayında, Özlale'nin sözünü ettiği bakanlardan birinin Bolat olduğu sonucuna varıldığını belirtti.




Ancak Saymaz daha sonra iddianın kaynağı olmadığını, programda daha önce dile getirilen bir iddiayı tekrarladığını açıkladı.




Bolat iddiaları reddederek iki gazeteci hakkında suç duyurusunda bulundu.




Bakanlığın başvurusunda gazetecilerin açıklamalarının hakaret, iftira, kişisel verilerin hukuka aykırı yayılması ve halkı yanıltıcı bilgiyi alenen yayma suçlarını oluşturduğu ileri sürüldü.




Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanı Mahinur Özdemir Göktaş da kendisi ve ailesi hakkındaki iddiaları reddetti. Göktaş, babasıyla ilgili suçlamaların isim benzerliğinden kaynaklandığını savundu. 




Bolat: "37,8 milyon TL yatırım yaptım, hesabımı kapatmadım"




Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat, 8 Ekim'de yaptığı açıklamada Hedef Yatırım Portföy bünyesinde yatırım yaptığını doğruladı.




Bolat, 26 Şubat 2024'te aile tasarruflarından 37,8 milyon lirayı kira sertifikası niteliğindeki bir yatırım aracına yatırdığını bildirdi.




Ancak fonların tasfiyesine yönelik operasyon öncesinde parasını çektiği, yatırımını iki katına çıkardığı ve hesabını kapattığı iddialarını reddetti.




Bolat, yatırımının hisse senedi değil, "sukuk" olarak da bilinen kira sertifikası olduğunu, hesabının operasyon öncesinde veya sonrasında kapatılmadığını söyledi. 170 milyon liralık işlem iddiasını da reddederek banka kayıtlarının incelenebileceğini belirtti.




Yeni Parti Milletvekili Ümit Özlale ise Bolat'a yönelik 170 milyon liralık işlem iddiasını yineledi ve Merkezi Kayıt Kuruluşu (MKK) işlem numaralarını paylaştığını açıkladı.




Özlale, Göktaş'ın babası Hasan Özdemir'le ilişkilendirdiği 830 milyon liralık fon işlemlerinin de açıklanmasını istedi.




Buradaki temel ayrım, bir bakanın yatırım fonuna para yatırması ve kamu görevinin sağladığı ayrıcalıklı bilgilerden yararlanarak kazanç elde etmesi arasında. Birincisi tek başına suç değil. İkincisi ise sermaye piyasası mevzuatı kapsamında suç oluşturabilir.




Fonlardan 187 milyar lira kazanan 214 kişi ve şirket incelemede




Gazetecilerin tutuklandığı gün, fon soruşturmasının mali boyutuna ilişkin yeni bilgiler de kamuoyuna yansıdı.




Sabah gazetesinin aktardığı ve Serbestiyet'in 9 Ekim'de yayımladığı habere göre, Tera, Pusula ve Hedef fonlarından 100 milyon liranın üzerinde kazanç sağladığı belirlenen 141 gerçek kişi ile 73 şirketin listesi, Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu'na (TMSF) gönderildi.




Haberde bu kişi ve şirketlerin toplam kazancının 187 milyar 653 milyon liraya ulaştığı belirtildi.




Soruşturma kapsamında elde edilen kazançların geri alınması için bildirimlerin başladığı, toplanacak paraların zarar gören yatırımcılara aktarılmasının hedeflendiği bildirildi.




Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek'in açıklamalarına göre soruşturmanın önemli bir bölümünü, fonların tasfiye kararından hemen önceki 13-16 Eylül tarihlerinde yapılan satışlar oluşturuyor.




Yetkililer, bazı yatırımcıların fonlarla ilgili gelişmelerden önceden haberdar olarak satış gerçekleştirdiklerini belirtiyor.




İncelemeye alınan 214 kişi ve şirketin kimlikleri kamuoyuna açıklanmadı. Bildirilen kazanç tutarlarının ne kadarının hukuka aykırı olduğu da henüz kesinleşmiş değil.




Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), 17-18 Eylül'de yedi portföy yönetim şirketine ait 131 fonu tasfiye sürecine almıştı. Karar yaklaşık 456 bin yatırımcıyı ilgilendiriyor. 




Savcılık gazetecilerin hangi bilgileri çarpıttığını açıklamadı




İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı, gazetecilerin ifadeye çağrılmasının gerekçesini "kamuoyunu yanıltıcı açıklamalar yapılması" olarak duyurdu.



















Gazetecilere soruşturma: Mustafa Balcı gözaltına alındı




8 Ekim 2026










Ancak ilk açıklamada gazetecilerin hangi somut bilgilerinin yanlış olduğu, yanlış olduğu ileri sürülen bilgilerin hangi kanıtlarla çürütüldüğü ve kamu düzeninin nasıl tehlikeye sokulduğu belirtilmedi.




TCK'nin 217/A maddesi, yalnızca gerçeğe aykırı bilgi yayılmasını değil; bilginin belirli konulara ilişkin olmasını, kamu barışını bozmaya elverişli biçimde alenen yayılmasını ve failin sırf halk arasında endişe, korku veya panik yaratma saikiyle hareket etmesini de suçun unsurları arasında sayıyor.




Gazetecilerin aktardığı bir bilginin yanlış olduğunun ileri sürülmesi, tek başına suçun oluştuğunu göstermiyor. Tutuklama kararı verilebilmesi için kuvvetli suç şüphesinin somut delillere dayanması ve tutuklama tedbirine neden başvurulduğunun gerekçelendirilmesi gerekiyor.




Sevinç ve Balcı hakkındaki tutuklama kararlarının gerekçeleri henüz kamuoyuna açıklanmış değil. Hâkimliğin neye dayanarak tutuklama kararı verdiği bilinmiyor. 




Basın özgürlüğü tartışması




Gazetecilere yönelik soruşturma, fon krizinde siyasi sorumluluk ve ayrıcalıklı bilgi kullanımı iddialarının yoğunlaştığı bir dönem içerisinde gerçekleşti. 




Basın özgürlüğü bakımından tartışmanın merkezinde, kamuoyunu yakından ilgilendiren mali işlemlerin haberleştirilmesi ile "bilerek yanlış bilgi yayılması" arasındaki hukukça belirlenmiş bir sınır var. Gazeteciler, özellikle kamu görevlileri ve siyasi yöneticilerle ilgili iddiaları araştırma, belgeleri yayımlama ve yetkililere soru sorma hakkına sahip, aslında bu, basının varlık şartı.




İfade ve basın özgürlüğünü güvence altına alan Avrupa İnsan Hakları Sözleşmesi'nin 10. Maddesi de kamu yararını ilgilendiren tartışmalara özel koruma sağlıyor.




Tutuklanan gazetecilerin adil bir yargılama sonucunda cezaevine konulduklarına ilişkin şüphelerin ortadan kalkması için savcılık ve mahkemenin gazetecilerin hangi açıklamalarının suç oluşturduğuna ve bu açıklamaların neden tutuklanmayı zorunlu kıldığına dair gerekçelerini açıkça ortaya koymaları bekleniyor. 




(AEK)

title: White Nationalists Off Secwépemc Territory
content:
There is a growing white supremacist genocide denial movement in so-called Canada.

On September 27th members of the Second Sons, a white nationalist militia, marched on unceded Secwépemc territory carrying racist banners near a former residential school where mass graves of Indigenous children were discovered.

This action was timed to occur three days before National Truth and Reconciliation Day a flawed and limited attempt to acknowledge Canada’s genocide of Indigenous peoples.

The Second Sons are tightly connected to the so-called ‘Active Clubs’ movement and have called to remove non-white people from Canada at gunpoint.

The Secwépemc have a long history of resistance to Canadian colonialism, including the Gustaffson Lake standoff in 1995, and more recently, the Tiny House Warrior movement, launched in resistance to the TransMountain Pipeline project.

White supremacy is inherent to settler colonialism.

Settler anarchists have a special responsibility to support Indigenous sovereignty and confront white nationalists wherever they rear their ugly heads.

Get together. Crew up. Confront white supremacy in all its forms.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Administration, Accused of Crimes Against Humanity, Sanctions Entire ICC
content:
Officials announced the sanctions just hours after the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to a former ICC judge.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Trump administration officials, facing numerous allegations of war crimes in its actions ranging from Iran to Cuba, issued punishing sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday that threaten the future of the entire body and its work to hold war criminals and genocidaires to account.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio, fresh off of his ultra-nationalist speech at the Acropolis this week, said in a video announcing the sanctions that the U.S. is banning “transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate against us.”

The sanctions are slated to cut the court off from using U.S.-based financial services, companies, and even the U.S. dollar after six months — a move that is ruinous for the court’s officials, as the global financial system is highly dependent on the U.S. dollar.

The administration announced the sanctions just hours after Navi Pillay, who was formerly the UN’s human rights chief and an ICC judge, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. Last year, Pillay led the independent UN commission that declared genocide in Gaza. The prize announcement incensed President Donald Trump, who reposted a message saying that the Nobel Committee “shamed itself beyond repair” on Truth Social.

The ICC warned that the sanctions are unprecedented, and called on its 125 member states to fight back against the U.S.’s actions.

“It is an attempt to obstruct the course of justice and to prevent the Court from doing what it was created to do. It is an assault on the rule of law and on the very foundations of the international legal order which strikes at the simple principle that no one stands above the law,” the ICC said in a statement. “Future generations, and above all the victims of mass atrocities, will ask how we responded when an institution created to protect them came under attack.”

The U.S. has already sanctioned 13 other ICC judges and prosecutors in recent months, including numerous officials who have worked on the ICC’s prosecution of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The Trump administration has also previously demanded that the ICC formally end its investigation into U.S. soldier wrongdoing in the U.S.’s invasion of Afghanistan that was already previously put on pause.

Rubio said that the move is about supposedly protecting U.S. sovereignty and shielding American officials and allies from being targeted by the ICC. “Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC,” Rubio said.

Similar claims have previously been debunked by legal experts as an attempt by Rubio to use rhetorical scare tactics to paper over Trump officials’ real desire in dismantling the ICC: impunity for themselves and violent allies like Israel. Trump administration officials have faced numerous accusations of war crimes and violations of international humanitarian law, for their massacres of civilians across numerous fronts; ICE raids and mass deportation campaign; and transfers of weapons to countries committing or implicated in war crimes.

Rather than threaten U.S. sovereignty, the sanctions on the ICC actually threaten the sovereignty of many states and peoples who have been victimized by powerful war criminals with no other method of recourse, critics said.

“By sanctioning the entire International Criminal Court, the Trump administration has taken a sledgehammer to the most important development in international justice in half a century,” said Omar Shakir, executive director for Democracy for the Arab World Now (DAWN). “U.S. sanctions threaten to shut the last viable road to justice for millions of victims of serious crimes, from Gaza and Sudan to Afghanistan and Ukraine.”

DAWN is one of several organizations that have filed lawsuits against previous U.S. sanctions against the ICC. The group called on the European Union to use its Blocking Statute, as it has for previous U.S. sanctions, to prohibit the EU from complying with the sanctions. The group also called on the ICC to prosecute Trump, Rubio, and other U.S. officials for the sanctions, which DAWN Advocacy Associate Isabelle Hayslip said are a crime under the ICC’s founding statute.

A group of eight countries, including the U.K., Germany, and France, said that they “regret and strongly disagree with” the sanctions in a joint statement, but did not commit to any action against them.

European leaders have faced criticism for their inaction in the face of the U.S.’s campaigns to dismantle the ICC and international law at large. “If European countries & other signatories to the International Criminal Court have any self-respect, they’d sanction Rubio & Trump for obstructing investigations of Netanyahu’s war crimes,” said Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland) last month.

The Coalition for the International Criminal Court (CICC), an international group of thousands of civil society groups, called on countries party to the ICC to “mount a coordinated and collective response” to the sanctions. It also called for the EU to activate its blocking statute against the measure.

“States Parties cannot allow coercive measures imposed by a non-State Party to determine whether victims can seek justice,” said Alison Smith, executive director of CICC.

“Words of solidarity are not enough,” added CICC Advocacy Coordinator Zoé Paris.

As Trump cracks down on political speech, independent media is increasingly necessary.

Truthout produces reporting you won’t see in the mainstream: journalism from the frontlines of global conflict, interviews with grassroots movement leaders, high-quality legal analysis and more.

Our work is possible thanks to reader support. Help Truthout catalyze change and social justice — make a tax-deductible monthly or one-time donation today.

author: Darío Aranda
title: 12 de octubre: autonomías indígenas y crisis de la modernidad colonial
content:
Por Roberto Espinoza para 

Debates Indígenas




Las autonomías, autogobiernos y autodeterminaciones pueden ser amazónicas, andinas, de páramos o de costas marinas. Pero en su mayoría son rurales. Eso conlleva la imagen de ser como islas que navegan en mares gigantescos de colonialidad del poder, del saber y del ser. Los peligros de naufragio aparecen cuando añadimos las intensas tormentas globales y nacionales de violencia racista y extractivista de la modernidad colonial, que fueron ocultadas por un tiempo, detrás de la aparente “democracia liberal”, y que hoy profundiza el abierto despojo territorial y arrinconamiento de derechos.




La modernidad colonial engendró y multiplicó dos grandes monstruos globales que hoy enfrentamos: la crisis climática y el autoritarismo racista

. Ambos golpean de manera particular a los pueblos originarios y a los movimientos sociales, porque afectan sus territorios, formas de vida y derechos, pero también porque encuentran en ellos 

sociedades en movimiento, capaces de construir resistencias frente a estas amenazas

. La expansión de las actividades extractivas y las nuevas formas de autoritarismo no son fenómenos aislados: profundizan las condiciones de despojo y desigualdad que históricamente han afectado a estos pueblos.




Las autonomías rurales, urbanas, originarias o sociales pueden nacer y proclamarse formalmente después de una asamblea, un congreso o algún otro evento colectivo. Sin embargo, su origen suele ser mucho más profundo y preceder largamente a ese momento de proclamación. Sus motores suelen encontrarse en conflictos y luchas de gran envergadura por la defensa de los derechos, los territorios, los bienes comunes y las formas propias de vida.




En ese sentido, la autonomía no comienza con una declaración: se va construyendo en la organización cotidiana, en la capacidad de tomar decisiones colectivas y en la experiencia acumulada de enfrentar amenazas y defender derechos.







Foto: Yaymy Mamani Ccallaccassi




Motivaciones de las autonomías




La construcción de la legitimidad propia de las autonomías, en base a la paciente unificación de la heterogeneidad de organizaciones del mismo pueblo, es lo que otorga solidez y raíces estables al proceso. 

El reconocimiento legal del Estado no deja de ser importante y es un derecho a arrancar, pero no es lo prioritario

 y va en segundo lugar. Desde esta perspectiva, primero es necesaria la autonomía de hecho y esto da curso a que más tarde se convierta en una autonomía de derecho. Así, nos basamos en el principio de realidad, antes de lo formal y burocrático.




El territorio es un eje central de las autonomías: es tanto el espacio físico como un sistema integral que articula vida, hábitat, cultura, espiritualidad, colectividad, sostenibilidad de los comunes, de los bienes comunes y de usos comunes que los “comunalizan” con marchas y contramarchas.




Implica pactos sociales u horizontes que cristalizan procesos y liderazgos, como cuidado profundo de las bondades de la naturaleza (madre tierra o 

yakumama

) o hábitat urbano bio cultural. 

El territorio no se limita a una mercancía o lucro del poder

: es un requisito para vivir en paz, mantener la armonía y alcanzar el buen vivir o vida plena.




El relevo intergeneracional exige que las juventudes conozcan y mantengan viva la memoria colectiva, fortalezcan sus vínculos con los procesos de resistencia y contribuyan a recrear nuevos espacios de autodeterminación.




Las autonomías necesitan tener sentido y ser necesarias para sus poblaciones, no solo en su dimensión política, histórica, filosófica o ideológica, sino también para garantizar una mejor calidad de vida integral, en lo cotidiano, personal, familiar y colectivo. Esto es esencial para la permanencia y la unidad de las autonomías, especialmente para manejar las divergencias, evitar la polarización y la fragmentación, que suelen estar conectadas con las disputas por espacios electorales o de poder en el Estado (dos peligros latentes que cercan y fracturan las autonomías sociales).




También 

son fundamentales las resistencias históricas en defensa del territorio

 (en sus dimensiones material, cultural y espiritual) y la participación de las mujeres, con su fuerza y sus propuestas en la acción organizada. Cada generación enfrenta 

el desafío de sostener la defensa autonómica sin subordinarse al Estado

.




En contextos de crisis y violencia, adquieren especial relevancia las respuestas colectivas y reguladas de las guardias indígenas o comunitarias frente a la criminalidad. Finalmente, el relevo intergeneracional exige que las juventudes conozcan y mantengan viva la memoria colectiva, fortalezcan sus vínculos con los procesos de resistencia y contribuyan a recrear nuevos espacios de autodeterminación.




Foto: Yaymy Mamani Ccallaccassi




¿Qué frena y desarticula las autonomías?




Es importante identificar los procesos que penetran al interior de las autonomías, que son alimentados por presiones externas y se pueden normalizar, ya que de no ser resueltos, amenazan con desintegrarlas por dentro. Entre estos factores destaca 

el sistema educativo estatal, privado o religioso, que viene desde fuera de los territorios;

 atrapa a las infancias y juventudes; los encapsula y aleja de las dinámicas familiares y sociales; y quiebra la transmisión de los valores, cosmovisiones y estructuras autonómicas.




Otro problema son los programas asistencialistas del Estado, empresas, organizaciones no gubernamentales, iglesias y partidos políticos

. Por otro lado, las campañas electorales imponen escenarios de demagogia, negocios políticos y polarización, que afectan los procesos organizacionales y, pasada la efervescencia, cuesta retomar los impulsos autonómicos. Se suman a ellos la penetración de las sectas religiosas que destruyen la espiritualidad propia, introducen pugnas en la convivencia comunitaria y dividen a las organizaciones.




Finalmente, se encuentra la creciente violencia que proviene del narcotráfico, de la minería legal e ilegal, de las operaciones extractivistas y de la criminalidad del sicariato, que golpea especialmente en las ciudades.




Por su parte, los partidos políticos

 

parten

 

a los pueblos, comunidades, familias, y organizaciones. La trampa de que el único espacio para cambiar la realidad social es el Estado y los cargos estatales (alcalde, congresista, funcionarios) minimiza, relega y abandona la acción territorial, que es la verdadera acción política social.

 

Peor aún, los partidos políticos optan por la manipulación o instrumentalización de las organizaciones, para las ambiciones de mayor poder partidario.




Finalmente, se encuentra la creciente violencia que proviene del narcotráfico (producción, comercialización y distribución), de la minería legal e ilegal, de las operaciones extractivistas (hidrocarburos, soja, palma aceitera) y de la criminalidad del sicariato, que golpea especialmente en las ciudades. La violencia va de la mano de la descomposición del Estado, la democracia y la corrupción interna de las organizaciones, que genera complicidad con el crimen. El resultado es el asesinato o la persecución de los liderazgos, y el debilitamiento del tejido comunitario, una base esencial de los procesos autonómicos.




Foto: Yaymy Mamani Ccallaccassi




Nuevos horizontes de sentido




Esta revisión sugiere reabrir los debates desde la experiencia de los movimientos sociales y desde la sociedad en movimiento (rural y urbana) en sus dinámicas más profundas. Por eso es necesario potenciar los horizontes de futuro que se generan desde las prácticas autonómicas: 

el autogobierno, el mandar obedeciendo, el

 

Allin Kawsay

 

(el “buen vivir” del pueblo Quechua),

 

Tarimat Pujut

 

(la “vida plena” de los pueblos amazónicos Wampís y Awajún) y

 

Ñandereko

 

(“nuestro modo de ser” en idioma guaraní).

 Así como, en las urbes, la ciudad comunitaria, el hábitat vivo bio cultural, la autogestión urbana y la 

rururbanidad

.




Es relevante no constituir esencialismos inmutables, requerir el accionar colectivo y hacerlo en común, es decir, “comunalizar”. Problematizarlos como cuestiones abiertas a cada giro de los tiempos y realidades. Debemos evitar teorías u “holismos cerrados” que consideran las totalidades sociales locales, nacionales y globales como estructuras fijas, estáticas y dogmáticas. El reto es mantener los enfoques holísticos de los pueblos originarios, que entienden la totalidad como un sistema dinámico, abierto, flexible, interconectado y en constante evolución.




Para avanzar al futuro, no se trata ya de atornillarse a un tipo de lenguaje; ni de esencializar las categorías, conceptos, teorías o el discurso de un movimiento; y menos aún de repetir el egocentrismo de ciertas individualidades. Se trata de proponer sugerencias teóricas motivadoras y, de resolver incoherencias, problemas y preguntas claves. 

Mientras algunos siguen apelando a discursos del pasado, en realidad, se necesitan nuevas teorías y nuevos horizontes de sentido

, desde el impulso de las sociedades y autonomías en movimiento.




Se trata de ir más allá del “modo de producción”

 y de revelar que estamos bajo un patrón global de poder de la 

modernidad colonial y capitalista

, que amenaza toda forma de vida y entra en una crisis generalizada, mediante 

la crisis climática, la desigualdad y el desborde del racismo y la polarización

. No se puede vivir sin mercado ni Estado, pero tampoco se puede sobrevivir dentro de ellos: por eso los Pueblos y Comunas están en la encrucijada de asumir su sobrevivencia y su futuro. Las relaciones sociales de reciprocidad y su expresión en la 

forma social comunal

 deben asumir el reto de expandirse, coexistir e influir sobre el mercado y el Estado. Nunca habrá una sustitución completa, de un tipo de sociedad por otra, y el cambio social tendrá transiciones de interpenetración entre lo viejo y lo nuevo.




Foto: Yaymy Mamani Ccallaccassi




El autogobierno frente al Estado uninacional en crisis




El balance histórico indica que fracasó el cambio social como acto extraordinario, de toma del gobierno por asalto o elecciones, o como ruptura “predestinada” de una sociedad ideal. 

Es inevitable resignificar el cambio social como una mutación social

, que exige una transformación holística, interrelación de múltiples cambios y procesos de larga duración. 

Se debe transformar la colonialidad del poder tiene color, que se constituyó históricamente sobre el dominio de las “razas” indígenas y afrodescendientes

 (“razas” inventadas para justificar el racismo biológico), para marginar a Naciones y Pueblos de Abya Yala.




De este modo, 

el cambio social es inevitable en la vida cotidiana y exige la descolonialidad del poder, del saber y del ser

, en forma simultánea. Pero también es necesario desarticularla en forma diversa y heterogénea en el sexo (desde el patriarcado hasta el feminicidio), el trabajo (la explotación laboral y las formas modernas de esclavitud), los imaginarios (el eurocentrismo), la autoridad (estatalismo) y la naturaleza (el ecocidio, el extractivismo y la tecnolatría).




Esa complejidad implica que 

el Estado puede ser un área importante de lucha, pero no puede ser el único camino

. De ese error estratégico estuvo lleno el siglo XX y siempre terminó en falsas ilusiones y frustraciones. Por eso, será imposible cambiar las cadenas mentales, solo desde la estructura estatal: el Estado es una arena más de luchas, conflictos y desafíos. En el terreno de la autoridad colectiva, se trata de desarrollar estructuras, procesos y visiones, desde el autogobierno de los Pueblos y Comunas, frente a aquellas basadas en el Estado uninacional que hoy se encuentra en crisis.













*

Roberto Espinoza

 es sociólogo peruano, colaborador de organizaciones indígenas y miembro de la 

Red Descolonialidad y Autogobierno

.




La entrada 

12 de octubre: autonomías indígenas y crisis de la modernidad colonial

 se publicó primero en 

Agencia de Noticias Tierra Viva

.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Bought Millions in SpaceX Bonds, Then Eased Space Travel Regulations
content:
Trump’s financial disclosures also show he bought millions in stock from Meta as the company ramps up its AI efforts.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

President Donald Trump made over 500 stock trades in the month of August, recent filings show, including millions of dollars in bonds purchased for SpaceX, just days before the administration loosened regulations that would have affected the company.

According to the most recent disclosures from Trump, the president purchased bonds from the company worth at least $1 million and up to $5 million.

Those trades involving SpaceX occurred on August 18. Two days later, on August 20, Trump issued a memorandum announcing the purported launching of “the golden age of space transportation.” Among other items, the memo seeks to loosen regulations on potential companies that venture into commercial space travel, and directs federal agencies to “incentivize co-development of space transportation infrastructure with private sector partners.”

Trump and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk have had a complicated but mostly friendly history. Musk infused hundreds of millions of dollars into the 2024 presidential election in support of Trump, and led the Trump administration’s “Department of Government Efficiency” initiative that gutted many federal agencies. The two had a brief falling out afterwards, but in recent months seem to have reconciled.

Indeed, Musk sat beside Trump at a recent White House summit on artificial intelligence (AI), and the president awarded him the National Medal of Science on Thursday.

Critics lambasted the trades and subsequent action by Trump to deregulate space travel as unscrupulous.

“There is a conflict of interest. I’m not saying he’s doing anything illegal, but this really gives the appearance of corruption,” said George W. Bush-era White House ethics lawyer Richard Painter.

“Rather than bringing down the cost of gas and groceries, President Trump is using his office to enrich himself,” Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Massachusetts) said. “That’s corruption, plain and simple.”

Trump also purchased up to $25 million in stock from Meta, Facebook’s parent company, which has been ramping up its AI efforts. During the past two months since those stock purchases, Trump has stated that he will reject any efforts to pass legislation that would regulate the AI industry, despite strong support from the public to do so, and has even gone so far as to describe those who want more restrictions or a slowdown of AI development as treasonous.

More recently, Trump has sought to rebrand AI as “super intelligence,” or “SI,” and issued a threat to anyone who continues to use the older phrasing.

“The White House considers anyone that uses the term, ‘Artificial Intelligence,’ as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, ‘Super Intelligence,’ THE ENEMY!” Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social this week.

As Trump cracks down on political speech, independent media is increasingly necessary.

title: La classe lycéenne ! podcast / mayday
content:
Le mouvement lycéen de ces derniers jours a surgi en plein marasme, désastre climatique tous les jours plus aigu, fascisation accélérée, mouvement social à l'arrêt et en une semaine il a bloqué la grande majorité des lycées, empli les rues, saturé l'espace médiatique et donné des idées aux travailleur-euses qui ne savaient plus par où reprendre la lutte.




Cette semaine Mayday donne donc la parole à des dizaines de lycéen-nes rencontrées aux abords des lycées, dans les rues révoltées et les manifs déterminées. Beaucoup de reportages et des voix qui nous parlent des conditions d'étude de la jeunesse, de la galère dans les bahuts de banlieue où tout a commencé, de la rage et de l'envie de se faire enfin entendre, avec aussi des débats animés, des désaccords sur les moyens de la lutte, des profs qui soutiennent et d'autres qui pacifient, des coups de gueule...

title: [BELGIQUE] Lancement de la campagne UNTIL - action de masse contre le Pacte Migratoire
content:
Les 26-27-28 novembre 2026, première action de masse contre le Pacte et le système qu'il représente, vers un monde où toustes ont la liberté de mouvement et l'accès égal aux ressources.




POUR NOUS REJOINDRE, REJOINS LE GROUPE 

SIGNAL

 ET ENREGISTRE-TOI PAR 

MAIL




UNTIL est une campagne contre le Pacte Migratoire de l'Union européenne et son monde - parce que personne n'est libre tant que tout le monde ne l'est pas. L'oppression des personnes migrant.es contribue directement au maintien de la société telle que nous la connaissons : elle est la clé de voûte d'un système qui appauvrit, prive d'autonomie et isole la majorité de la population. Notre objectif est de lutter directement contre cette oppression et construire une alternative jusqu'à ce que nous puissions toustes vivre dans la dignité.




Les 26-27-28 novembre 2026, première action de masse contre le Pacte et le système qu'il représente, vers un monde où toustes ont la liberté de mouvement et l'accès égal aux ressources.




Le Pacte Migratoire fait partie d'un ensemble de mesures qui incarnent la violence sous forme de contrôle global des frontières et d'une surveillance massive et renforcée. Les institutions et les entreprises en tirent profit, les forces de l'ordre et gardes frontières sont de plus en plus militarisés, et le pouvoir politique de cell.eux qui font des personnes migrant.es des boucs émissaires grandit.




Le discours du Pacte, et des acteur.ices qui le défendent, veut que l'immigration soit associé au danger. A travers les pays, cette association est utilisée pour justifier austérité et autoritarisme.




Nous rejetons cette idée. Nous sommes convaincu.es que nous ne sommes en sécurité, et libres, que lorsque nous nous organisons tous ensemble, dans un esprit de solidarité.*




UNTIL refuse l'idée qu'il n'y a pas d'alternative possible, que la société ne puisse que devenir plus stricte, plus violente et plus surveillée.*




UNTIL s'inscrit dans une longue histoire de lutte pour la liberté de circulation. Par cette trajectoire, UNTIL insiste sur la nécessite de poursuivre ce combat. Nous devons, et nous allons, faire naître un autre monde à la place de celui d'aujourd'hui.




Rejoignez-nous fin novembre pour en faire partie. Il faut bloquer le Pacte dès maintenant.




Voir en ligne : Page Instagram @until.everyone.isfree

author: labor4pal
title: If They Can Criminalize the Minnesota 15, They Can Criminalize All of Us (Workers Resist)
content:
Against a backdrop of rising class struggle internationally — from Spain and France to Northern Ireland — the fight against the criminalization of anti-ICE activism, attacks on democratic rights, and union-busting has gained momentum over the past two weeks.

On October 3, nearly 500 people marched through downtown Minneapolis in support of the Minnesota 15 (MN15), political and union activists indicted by Donald Trump’s Justice Department for their organized opposition to the federal immigration crackdown in Minnesota known as Operation Metro Surge. That same day, solidarity events ranging from fundraising dinners to public meetings took place in 28 cities around the world, from New Haven, Connecticut, to Manchester, England.

The Minneapolis march drew broad support from the Minnesota labor movement, including the Minnesota AFL-CIO, Minnesota Nurses Association (MNA), Minneapolis Federation of Educators (MFE Local 59), Saint Paul Federation of Educators (SPFE Local 28), Minneapolis Regional Labor Federation, and eight other union locals.

This growing labor support reflects an understanding of what is at stake: the indictments of the MN15 are not simply an attack on 15 individuals. They are an attack on the ability of workers to organize collectively against government repression.

Evidence emerging from the MN15 discovery documents reinforces the seriousness of this threat. The documents reveal that federal agents infiltrated the Twin Cities’ resistance and labor movements during Operation Metro Surge, which began in December 2025. Such surveillance may have much deeper historical roots.

On February 15, 2026, four undercover federal agents attended a mass Workers’ Assembly, where workers representing more than 30 union locals participated in democratic debate and decision-making about how to continue the fight against ICE. Other discovery materials suggest an extensive effort to map the organizations, relationships, and networks that sustained resistance to the federal occupation. Taken together, these revelations raise serious questions about the government’s interest in identifying and potentially disrupting centers of working-class organization and power.

Nor is this happening only in Minnesota. At the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, federal authorities subpoenaed three years of meeting minutes and financial records from the 4,000-member Graduate Employees’ Organization (GEO) as part of an investigation involving union members who opposed Israel’s war in Gaza. The implications extend far beyond any single investigation. When the government subjects unions and political organizations to sweeping surveillance and demands for internal records, it threatens the relationships of trust and solidarity upon which collective action depends.

In Minnesota, organized labor played an indispensable role in resisting ICE. Union members provided peacekeepers at marches and rallies, helped train legal observers, organized patrols to protect immigrant students and their families, and helped lead the January 23 mass strike, when an estimated 300,000 workers stayed away from their jobs. That collective action demonstrated something the government would prefer workers to forget: when working people organize across workplaces, unions, and communities, they can exercise enormous social and economic power.

Following January 23, union activists continued organizing through the February 15 and April 5 Workers’ Assemblies. These gatherings brought together a militant layer of the local labor movement to debate how to build on the strike, strengthen workplace organization, and sustain the fight against ICE. It is no accident that eight of the MN15 are union members who were directly involved in planning and producing the workers’ assemblies. By indicting these activists, the federal government has placed some of the Twin Cities’ most experienced and committed class-struggle organizers under the threat of lengthy prison sentences, disrupting their ability to organize at precisely the moment their experience is most needed.

Support for the MN15 has been, in the words of defendants and Defense Committee organizers, “overwhelming” in both breadth and depth. And that support continues to grow. Alongside the October 3 demonstrations, recent weeks have seen benefit concerts, fundraising dinners, public meetings, and screenings of the documentary When ICE Melts, which chronicles the Twin Cities resistance and the January 23 mass strike.

The film drew a sold-out audience of more than 200 in Minneapolis and 130 in Madison, Wisconsin, with smaller screenings from Albuquerque to Berlin. Additional events are planned on both coasts, in Colorado, and across Europe this fall. These events are doing more than raising money for legal defense. They are introducing new audiences to the experience of ordinary Minnesotans who organized to protect their neighbors, resist federal repression, and drive ICE out of their communities. They are also helping people recognize the connections between what happened in Minnesota and the attacks on democratic and labor rights unfolding elsewhere.

The breadth of this support points toward an important strategic opportunity: the MN15 defense campaign can become a catalyst for building a much wider movement against political repression.

The defense of the Minnesota 15 is about more than winning justice for those facing prosecution, essential as that is. It is also about defending the right of working people everywhere to organize collectively against authoritarianism. The MN15 defendants are being prosecuted for activities connected to a movement in which thousands of Minnesotans participated: protecting immigrant neighbors, documenting federal operations, organizing protests, and mobilizing workers against ICE.

As more people learn about the case, they will have opportunities to examine the government’s allegations, challenge its narrative, and understand the broader political stakes of the prosecution. That understanding can help inspire defense campaigns in other communities, including those supporting the Michigan 8 and Prairieland defendants, who also face federal prosecution arising from protest activity.

Such campaigns need not be limited to responding after activists have been indicted. They can also help build the relationships, organizations, and public support necessary to defend communities confronting new ICE detention centers, expanding surveillance technologies such as Flock cameras, attacks on immigrant workers, or other forms of government repression. The point is not simply to replicate the Minnesota experience. It is to take its lessons seriously: build relationships before a crisis, establish democratic organizations rooted in workplaces and communities, and develop the capacity to respond collectively when people come under attack.

As the MN15 defense campaign reaches a wider audience, it can help make political repression more costly for those who carry it out. A movement involving hundreds of thousands, potentially millions, of working people could exert enormous political pressure against the prosecution of activists and the criminalization of dissent. That kind of movement could help keep the MN15 and others facing similar charges out of prison. Just as importantly, it could strengthen the willingness and ability of working people to resist the next attack.

Achieving this will require defense committees across the country that are broadly inclusive, democratically organized, and capable of reaching well beyond existing activist circles. We need the participation of unions, community organizations, immigrant rights groups, students, civil liberties advocates, religious organizations, and ordinary working people who may never have attended a political demonstration.

We also need to reach people and institutions in the mainstream of American political life. One example is the effort that secured Connecticut Senator Richard Blumenthal’s support for the Minnesota 15. Blumenthal is a mainstream Democratic politician, and the Democratic Party remains firmly committed to capitalism. That does not make his support unimportant. On the contrary, winning support from elected officials and other influential figures can help bring the case to people who might otherwise never hear about it. It can broaden public scrutiny of the prosecutions and increase the political costs of repression.

The challenge is to build the broadest possible united front without surrendering the political independence of the working-class movement.

A defense campaign does not require everyone to agree about capitalism, electoral politics, or the ultimate direction of social change. It requires agreement that people must be able to organize, protest, defend their neighbors, and exercise their democratic rights without facing politically motivated prosecution. That is a basis for solidarity far broader than the existing socialist left, and we should take every opportunity to build it.

The prosecutions of the MN15, Michigan 8, and Prairieland defendants should concern every worker, whether or not they have ever participated in an anti-ICE demonstration. If the government can use sweeping investigations, surveillance, and criminal charges against people organizing to defend immigrants or oppose federal policies, what prevents similar tactics from being used against workers organizing against union-busting, environmentally destructive data centers, climate devastation, or other threats to their communities?

These are not abstract concerns. The Trump administration has already made clear its intention to expand federal immigration enforcement operations into other sanctuary jurisdictions. As recently as September 8, border czar Tom Homan described federal operations in New York as an initial phase of a broader effort targeting such jurisdictions. The machinery of repression is being expanded even as communities are organizing to resist it.

And the consequences of failing to defend those already targeted extend beyond the defendants themselves. Every prosecution sends a message to workers considering whether to organize, join a protest, protect an immigrant neighbor, or take collective action: This could happen to you. If people see that those who took risks before them were left isolated, the next person may decide the risks are simply too great.

But when communities and unions mobilize to defend those under attack, they send a different message: You will not have to face repression alone. This is why defense work is not separate from the struggle to build a stronger movement. It is part of that struggle. The ability to organize depends not only on formal legal rights but on the confidence that comes from knowing others will stand with us when those rights are threatened. That confidence is built through solidarity in practice.

The Minnesota resistance showed what can happen when working people move beyond isolated acts of protest and begin exercising their collective power. The January 23 mass strike demonstrated that organized workers, acting together with their communities, can disrupt business as usual and force a political response.

Now the defense of the Minnesota 15 presents another opportunity to build the organizations, relationships, and solidarity that made that action possible. We cannot afford to wait until the next wave of repression reaches our own workplaces and neighborhoods. The old labor slogan has rarely been more relevant: An injury to one is an injury to all.

Support the Minnesota 15. Organize a benefit or public meeting. Book a screening of When ICE Melts for your union, community organization, or local group. And begin building a defense committee in your own city or town.

The immediate task is to keep these activists out of prison. The larger task is to build a workers’ movement strong enough to defend all of us

title: Cagnard prend fin, la lutte continue
content:
En cette rentrée, Cagnard a décidé de clôturer ses activités politiques. Dans ce texte, nous nous retrouvons à quelques-un·e·s pour tirer le bilan de l'existence du collectif et situons sa trajectoire dans la séquence politique que nous traversons. Nous exprimons là notre avis sur la tenue et fermeture de cet espace d'organisation alors que le groupe voit la fin de ses activités comme un constat qui s'impose à lui-même. Diverses lectures découlent de la situation parmi les membres restants.




Il est ainsi à noter que, pour certain·es d'entre nous, ce sont le manque d'effectifs et de motivation qui bloquent aujourd'hui le groupe.


Cette ligne identifie l'impossibilité de l'action future du groupe dans les tensions inter-personnelles qui ont pu apparaître au fil de notre activité et dans un manque de renouvellement de nos effectifs. L'accueil de nouveaux membres aurait alors pu permettre de diluer les divergences politiques, de mettre une distance entre les susceptibilités inter-personnelles ou de voir partir des camarades tout en laissant de nouvelles forces assumer les tâches organisationnelles laissées vacantes.




D'autres camarades voient poindre des problématiques liées à notre fonctionnement, notre ouverture et notre composition. C'est afin de préciser cette lecture que nous écrivons ce texte.




En premier lieu, nous détaillons les enjeux qui ont motivé la création du collectif. Puis, nous revenons sur l'actualité politique du groupe et livrons des éléments d'analyse du contexte. De nouveaux impératifs se dessinent constamment dans la lutte : notre réflexivité doit servir à ajuster nos perspectives politiques à l'aune des obstacles que nous traversons et des tâches qui émergent.




Cagnard, sa création et ses objectifs




Cagnard a été créé en mars 2025 avec pour ambition de former un groupe autonome et ouvert sur Marseille. À rebours des logiques affinitaires et de cooptation, des camarades ont souhaité initier un projet de rupture avec les institutions traditionnelles du mouvement – partis et syndicats – qui assume dans le même temps la nécessité et l'accessibilité de l'organisation politique. Dans un cadre de composition, des personnes de sensibilités politiques diverses se sont organisées sur la base de perspectives communes, à commencer par l'intensification des mouvements sociaux et leur défense face à la répression.




Nous avons œuvré à la diffusion de pratiques de défense, soutenu les inculpé·es face à la Justice et animé des ateliers de formation politique. Il est crucial de battre en brèche les dynamiques de spécialisation lorsqu'elles entravent la participation effective des camarades à l'organisation politique. L'action de rue se doit d'être massive et ne doit pas être l'apanage d'une élite éclairée. Quant à la défense juridique, elle ne doit pas être abandonnée à des spécialistes du droit. Ces deux pendants du renforcement d'un mouvement doivent se trouver aux mains du plus grand nombre de camarades.




Nous entendions défendre ces lignes, ce qui entraînait parfois de porter la rupture au sein du mouvement social, dans la rue et au sein des espaces d'organisation. Plus largement, nous cherchions à soutenir le débordement face à la répression, le dépassement des mots d'ordre défensifs, sectoriels et des cadres de lutte institués, et à exacerber les contradictions en leur sein.




La théorie n'étant qu'un moment de la pratique, la tenue d'ateliers de formation politique et culturelle devait servir à affûter nos perspectives d'intervention dans les mobilisations naissantes et celles à venir. La composition devait nourrir l'intelligence collective : loin de penser que la contradiction affaiblit le mouvement révolutionnaire, nous sommes convaincu·es qu'elle le renforce et qu'elle doit être entretenue. Au-delà du dogmatisme et du sectarisme, l'ouverture de nos espaces visait un objectif clair : défendre et construire l'autonomie politique, dans le prolongement de ce que ce champ a su porter d'anti-capitalisme, d'anti-étatisme et d'indépendance vis-à-vis des partis et organisations syndicales. Il s'agissait aussi d'accroître nos forces de lutte, de propager l'auto-organisation pour gagner en puissance collective.




Tout au long de son existence, le collectif a fait preuve d'une activité politique constante. Toutefois, ces derniers mois, ses membres ont éprouvé des contradictions dans la mise en œuvre de ces objectifs. Notre modèle politique éprouve des limites certaines.




Retour sur l'actualité récente du collectif







Les problématiques de l'ouverture et de la composition




 




Cagnard a constitué une porte d'entrée vers l'organisation politique pour bon nombre de camarades et nous nous en réjouissons. Le collectif a connu des effectifs fluctuants selon les périodes. Le critère du nombre est ambivalent : s'ils permettent une intervention plus consistante et ambitieuse, des effectifs nombreux ne sont pas toujours signe de vitalité et d'efficacité. Alors que la prise de parole est d'autant plus difficile à tenir que les effectifs sont importants, les positions politiques semblent dépendantes des personnes présentes et de leur aisance à prendre la parole pour les défendre. Les structures du collectif paraissent pour certains membres verrouillées. Un double écart se creuse progressivement entre les membres récurrents qui affirment plus facilement leurs opinions et sur-investissent les tâches et d'autres qui deviennent de plus en plus distants, se sentent illégitime à donner leur avis mais envisagent le groupe comme un espace de consommation.




Le risque d'un surmenage des premiers et d'un départ facilité des seconds n'est jamais très loin. Or, le maintien de structures politiques pérennes est d'une importance capitale, en particulier dans la transmission des expériences de lutte et la continuité de l'activité politique d'une mobilisation à l'autre.




À cet aspect limitant de l'ouverture s'ajoute le double tranchant de la composition. Celle-ci permet d'ouvrir le collectif au plus grand nombre : aucun pré-requis théorique ou pratique n'est nécessaire à son entrée. Mais si l'assemblage de différentes sensibilités politiques permet de gagner en puissance d'intervention, il limite par ailleurs les réflexions stratégiques à long terme ainsi que la cohérence politique du projet. Si des divergences émergent, elles sont régulièrement évacuées au profit de la part consensuelle, dans l'objectif d'assurer l'intervention commune en mouvement. Ces divergences se renforcent bien souvent lorsque la nécessité de cohésion paraît moins cruciale, en particulier hors-mouvement. Cette dynamique contribue à focaliser l'activité du collectif sur des tâches essentiellement tactiques, logistiques et court-termistes.







Fin d'année 2025 et soutien aux inculpé·es du mouvement du 10S




 




Le mouvement du 10 septembre 2025 (ou « Bloquons tout ») n'a été qu'un pétard mouillé, sur-investi par les organisations de gauche et les récupérateurs de tout bord et fortement cadenassé par la répression d'État qui n'entendait laisser passer aucun débordement. À Marseille, plusieurs camarades ont été arrêté·es et inculpé·es à la suite des mobilisations. Ces derniers mois, nous avons participé à la défense de plusieurs d'entre elleux. Ces processus collectifs ont donné lieu à des relaxes pour la totalité des prévenu·e·s, actant de précieuses victoires pour le mouvement social. Nous sommes revenu·es plus en détail sur ces affaires dans deux articles disponibles sur notre compte Instagram et sur le site de Marseille Info Autonomes.

 [

1

]

 [

2

]







Questionnements sur le traitement des oppressions et des violences sexistes et sexuelles




 




En mars 2026, de profondes divergences ont éclaté au sein du collectif autour du traitement des violences sexistes et sexuelles ainsi que des oppressions de genre.




Dans une période où le collectif était aux prises avec les prolongements d'affaires de violences survenues dans d'autres villes et avec leur gestion menée en dehors de notre collectif, notre protocole de prise en charge des violences a cristallisé d'importants débats internes. Il apparaissait nécessaire d'y apporter des clarifications, voire d'envisager une refonte générale. Des échanges se sont tenus, sans toujours éviter des tensions plus ou moins tenaces autour de questions qui nous semblent essentielles d'approfondir. Quels sont les objectifs et les impératifs d'une « bonne gestion » ? Quelles sont les catégories sur lesquelles se fonde un protocole ? Quels enjeux se nouent dans la suspension et l'exclusion d'un·e membre du collectif ? Comment doser le degré d'opacité qui doit être maintenu entre le groupe et les personnes mandatées pour traiter une situation ? En creux, la place du désaccord et de la composition qu'il est possible de tenir en la matière, dans un espace politique, a irrigué bon nombre de réflexions.




Malgré la place que ces échanges ont pris au sein du collectif tout au long de ces semaines, nous n'avons pas pu aboutir à l'adoption d'une ligne claire. Le groupe s'est englué et n'a pas su livrer des réponses là où elles étaient attendues tant par ses membres que par les personnes concernées par nos gestions. Parfois, les divergences politiques se sont trouvées exacerbées, révélant l'impossibilité d'établir une décision satisfaisant·e aux yeux de tous·tes. Ni la révision du protocole, ni la définition de lignes politiques précises n'ont été concluantes. Cette séquence s'est étalée durant plusieurs semaines et a mis à l'épreuve les structures du collectif. Elle a vu se poursuivre le délitement des effectifs.




Éléments d'analyse sur le contexte politique




Ces éléments organisationnels et internes ne constituent qu'une part réduite de notre position qui se doit d'être évaluée dans le cadre politique général où nous nous situons. De même que la ligne politique que nous avons adoptée et défendue a pu sembler pertinente dans une séquence politique spécifique, le cours des luttes – pris dans sa composition, ses évolutions, ses contradictions et ses différentes échelles – nous engage à la reconsidérer.




Au niveau mondial, la crise capitaliste s'accentue et la classe bourgeoise n'a qu'une seule solution : renforcer l'exploitation du prolétariat. Offensive économique, ravage écologique, montée de la réaction, intensification de l'autoritarisme, de l'impérialisme et de la militarisation des États : le quotidien se fait toujours plus insupportable. Partout dans le monde, les luttes s'enchaînent vigoureusement sans qu'aucune ne parvienne encore à bouleverser profondément les rapports sociaux existants.




En France, nous avons connu une séquence politique marquée par l'irruption régulière de mouvements depuis 2016 et la Loi Travail. Cette séquence mouvementiste a donné quelques aperçus de rupture avec la direction traditionnelle du mouvement : une hausse de la conflictualité dans la rue, une agitation sociale diffuse et la multiplication des initiatives débordantes. La récente et courageuse démonstration de force des lycéen·nes témoigne d'une même colère trop longtemps contenue. La conflictualité aux abords des lycées a atteint une rare intensité.




L'autonomie, ce champ politique hétéroclite dans lequel nous nous inscrivons, s'est engagée corps et âme dans cette séquence. Elle a trouvé dans ces mobilisations à répétition l'occasion de mettre en pratique une combativité de rue et une auto-organisation indépendante des organes traditionnellement dévoués à la réception – et l'inhibition – des revendications populaires. Ces orientations tactiques, qui furent celles de notre collectif, si elles ont suscité l'adhésion de bon nombre de franges en mouvement, se sont montrées bien insuffisantes pour faire avancer les positions révolutionnaires.




En effet, le constat est sans appel. Malgré quelques étincelles, les défaites se sont enchaînées aussi vite que les mobilisations. La rupture était essentiellement partielle et portée sur les pratiques. Dans son contenu politique, ce cycle de luttes s'est très largement concentré sur la meilleure redistribution des richesses et la défense de l'État-providence. En l'absence d'une opposition suffisamment forte aux propositions reformistes et/ou sectorielles mises en avant en assemblée, l'autonomie s'est cantonnée à jouer un rôle essentiellement tactique. Le défaut d'orientations stratégiques se révèle alors déterminant : des composantes politiques aguerries savent absorber à leur compte la moindre initiative débordante. Le développement de pratiques offensives se transforme en arguments pour les syndicats sur la table de négociation et les assemblées générales des mouvements deviennent des espaces de recrutement et un cahier de rédaction programmatique d'une gauche électoraliste toujours prompte à chercher l'apaisement et à renvoyer la contestation dans les urnes.




Alors que la gauche a toujours travaillé à la récupération des mouvements sociaux, nous avons assisté, ces dernières années, à une recomposition d'une part du mouvement social à la queue de la France Insoumise. Cette jonction, qui n'est pas appelée à durer, s'opère tantôt sur la base d'un antifascisme opportuniste, tantôt sur la perspective d'un anticapitalisme tronqué. Ces gestionnaires entendent profiter de la combativité des luttes, incarner la seule alternative viable face au ravage en cours et se hisser à la tête de l'État. Pourtant, derrière les promesse d'un programme « de rupture », d'un capitalisme débarrassé « de la finance », d'une République et d'une Nation revisitées ou encore d'une démocratie revivifiée, c'est bien la reproduction de l'exploitation capitaliste et de la domination sociale qui se joue. Aucun salut ne se trouve là : les gains sociaux – ô combien salutaires pour les exploité·es – sont toujours le fruit des luttes sociales. Par ailleurs, un simple rééquilibrage des rapports sociaux ne constitue en rien leur dépassement, encore moins leur abolition.




Dans le même temps, l'autonomie paraît se décomposer. Alors que certaines de ses franges se replient sur elles-mêmes ou s'essoufflent dans des querelles intestines, une part importante se projette également à la queue de la social-démocratie. Face à un manque de perspectives stratégiques et de cadres de coordinations, certain·es s'attachent d'autant plus fortement à des éléments de folklore. La mise en place d'une auto-organisation, l'appel incantatoire à l'horizontalité et la pratique du « bloc » sont alors vus comme révolutionnaires en soi. Cet effet s'additionne à une désorientation théorique associée à une confusion dans nos termes censée nous rendre plus rejoignable.




Malgré tout, cette séquence de lutte présente quelques notes réjouissantes : une forte politisation de la jeunesse, une agitation sociale qui couve, une adhésion de plus en plus forte aux pratiques de lutte combatives face à l'impuissance inhérente aux organes de médiation.




Contre le dogmatisme et l'avant-gardisme, nous devons sans cesse prendre acte des évolutions de la situation politique, ajuster nos objectifs et nos modalités d'intervention au cours réel des luttes. Aucune proposition organisationnelle ne constitue une fin en soi. Nous envisageons la poursuite du combat au-delà du modèle politique que nous avons éprouvé jusqu'à présent et qui semble s'essouffler. Malgré cette décision franche, nous insistons sur la nécessité de rendre l'organisation politique aussi rejoignable que possible et de lutter contre le repli et l'isolement qui affaiblissent la combativité des luttes.




Prendre acte, s'organiser, vaincre




Nous saluons les camarades et collectifs avec qui nous avons oeuvré tout au long de notre activité. Nous nous retrouverons très vite dans la lutte.




Nous adressons nos plus sincères pensées aux personnes qui subissent, dans le combat pour l'émancipation collective partout dans le monde, la répression.




Nous avons un monde à gagner : nous voulons tout !

title: Sois jeune et casse tout ! / une émission de Minuit Décousu
content:
Premiers blocages, organisation autonome, répression, soupçon de manipulation et adultisme… 1h de radio pour donner la parole aux lycéen-nes sur leur mouvement, pour écouter leurs stratégies et perspectives de lutte.




Au printemps dernier, on s'était lancé dans un double documentaire sonore sur 

le mouvement contre le CPE

 puis sur 

celui contre la Loi Travail

. Deux mouvements majeurs pour les lycéen·nes et les étudiant·es de leur époque, à dix ans d'écart. Notre plan secret, c'était de faire une émission sur le grand mouvement social de la jeunesse de 2026. C'était écrit, le mouvement devait arriver, rien ne pouvait nous échapper : c'est la prophétie Minuit Décousu.




Cette semaine, on a donc tendu notre micro au 

collectif autonome lycéen Rafal

, pour nous parler de la stratégie du mouvement, de la répression à l'intérieur et à l'extérieur des lycées, dont le but est de marquer les chairs, les esprits et les dossiers scolaires. On a aussi interrogé 

des lycéen·nes qui organisaient leur premier blocage

, sur les effets que ça a sur leur politisation et sur 

la construction d'une AG inter-lycéenne

 qui permet de reprendre du pouvoir quand on est délaissé de tous les espaces politiques qui nous concernent. En filigrane à travers l'émission, les lycéen·nes se positionnent 

contre l'adultisme et la fiction de manipulation du mouvement

, et affirment leur volonté de 

construction d'un autre monde

.




Photographie : blocage devant le lycée Récamier à Lyon par @effugax




 

 

 

 

 

 










Minuit Décousu, c'est un fanzine radiophonique nocturne sur 

Radio Canut

 (Lyon et alentours), 

Radio Vassivière

 (Limousin) et 

Cause Commune

 (Paris/IDF). Semaine après semaine pendant une heure, on en découd avec la nuit et on tire les fils de sons, de textes, d'archives et de voix qui s'entremêlent.

author: Amy Goodman
title: Nobel Peace Prize Awarded to Jurist Who Led UN Inquiry Into Genocide in Gaza
content:
South African human rights lawyer Navanethem “Navi” Pillay began her career defending anti-apartheid activists.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize has been awarded to Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, the South African jurist who led the United Nations commission of inquiry that concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Pillay’s long career in international human rights law includes work as a defense attorney for anti-apartheid activists, president of the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, a former judge at the International Criminal Court and the U.N.’s high commissioner for human rights from 2008 to 2014.

“Everybody in the human rights movement reveres Navi Pillay,” says war crimes prosecutor Reed Brody, who calls the award “a stinging rebuke to Donald Trump.” Brody, a member of the United Nations Group of Human Rights Experts on Nicaragua, also comments on the Trump administration’s decision to deport a Nicaraguan opposition activist, Jeffrey Jarquín, from the United States, where he was in the process of seeking asylum. Upon his return to Nicaragua, Jarquín was immediately imprisoned at the same facility in which he was once tortured.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman, with Juan González.

The Norwegian Nobel Committee has announced the winner of the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. This is the chair of the Nobel Committee speaking in Oslo this morning.

JØRGEN WATNE FRYDNES: The Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 goes to a person who, with exceptional courage and integrity, has led the way towards a more comprehensive global legal order. This year’s laureate has been instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted. The Norwegian Nobel Committee has decided to award the Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 to Navanethem “Navi” Pillay for her efforts to promote peace and international law.

AMY GOODMAN: The South African human rights lawyer and international jurist Navi Pillay has been the United Nations high commissioner for human rights and a judge at both the International Criminal Court and at an international tribunal investigating the 1994 genocide in Rwanda. Most recently, she led the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry that concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza.

Navi Pillay is now 85 years old. She was born into an Indian Tamil family in apartheid South Africa. The first woman to start a law practice in Natal, South Africa, in 1967, she began her legal career defending anti-apartheid activists, including Nelson Mandela, exposing torture and helping establish key rights for prisoners on Robben Island. The Nobel Committee also praised her work in South Africa.

JØRGEN WATNE FRYDNES: A common thread runs from her early work, defending Nelson Mandela and others who stood up against apartheid, to her service as a judge in some of the key international court cases of our time.

AMY GOODMAN: Navi Pillay was in Nuremberg, Germany, at an annual conference of human rights lawyers and judges when she got the news this morning.

NAVI PILLAY: Thank you very much. Thank you very much. If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump. … The last thing I did is the delivery of the report on Gaza naming what’s happening there as genocide.

AMY GOODMAN: Meanwhile, Israel’s Foreign Ministry took to X to denounce the awarding of the Nobel Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, calling it a, quote, “grotesque weaponization of an award to legitimize anti-Israel hatred and prejudice,” unquote.

This is Navi Pillay speaking to Reuters last year about her genocide findings as the chair of the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territories.

NAVI PILLAY: Genocide is occurring in Gaza. We haven’t gone into Palestine yet. We will, because this is a permanent commission. And we named the three individuals that we felt were responsible. And we said — and the one is the prime minister, the other the president, and the third is the former minister of defense. And we said that since they acted as agents of the state, then the state of Israel is responsible. …

Today, we witness in real time how the promise of “never again” is broken and tested in the eyes of the world. The ongoing genocide in Gaza is a moral outrage and a legal emergency.

AMY GOODMAN: For more, we’re joined here in our New York studio by war crimes prosecutor Reed Brody, member of the International Commission of Jurists, served as a member of the United Nations Group of Human Rights Experts on Nicaragua. He’s also the author of To Catch a Dictator: The Pursuit and Trial of Hissène Habré.

First, Reed, your response to Navi Pillay being chosen as the 2026 Nobel Peace laureate?

REED BRODY: This was just wonderful. I mean, I love Navi Pillay. I mean, everybody in the human rights movement reveres Navi Pillay, who actually embodies the last 60 years of work for human rights and the rule of law, from a anti-apartheid lawyer and judge in South Africa to the tribunals on Rwanda and the ICC, as high commissioner for human rights, not just being the first woman in all of these things, but, actually — or the first African, but, actually, you know, breaking new ground on genocide, on LGBT issues, on women’s issues.

And it’s also a stinging rebuke to Donald Trump. You know, Donald Trump is fighting — and the Nobel Committee did not mention Donald Trump, but his name was omnipresent in what they said. I mean, Donald Trump is sanctioning judges, fighting for a world in which, you know, might makes right, in which there is no accountability, and Navi Pillay represents the exact opposite of that: the rule of law, accountability for the worst crimes, you know, the rule of law rather than the law of the jungle.

JUAN GONZÁLEZ: And, Reed, it’s not only a rebuke, obviously, of Donald Trump, but the decision of the Nobel Committee to choose Navi Pillay at this particular time in terms of the impact on Israel and the growing isolation of Israel worldwide. Could you talk about that, as well?

REED BRODY: Well, of course, you know, she, Navi Pillay, was the head of the U.N. independent commission that was looking into abuses in the Occupied Territories. I’m on a similar commission for Nicaragua. And she found, you know, with her — you know, beyond a reasonable doubt — excuse me, reasonable grounds to believe that Israel was committing genocide. And she backed that up, you know, through thousands — with thousands of interviews, through, you know, forensic proof. And I think around the world people can cite the work that Navi Pillay has done on this. When people say that Israel is engaged in genocide, they have this imprimatur from a quasi-judicial body of the United Nations, you know, led by one of the most distinguished judges in the world.

AMY GOODMAN: And if you could comment on the comments of the Nobel Committee around right now the international legal order and what international human rights law is about?

REED BRODY: Well, I think that’s the most important thing here. I mean, we are living in a moment, as you have had on your show several times, in which the entire architecture of international law and accountability is under attack. The United States, which has vowed to dismantle the International Criminal Court, the court that she used to sit on, brick by brick, which is sanctioning the judges, like as she was once a judge of the ICC — we understand new sanctions from the United States are coming down. And here is somebody who represents the exact opposite, who represents exactly that so-called international law, those rogue international judges that the United States is going after. So this is such an important moment.

AMY GOODMAN: And interesting she got the news in Nuremberg, Germany. The significance of Nuremberg and the Nuremberg trials for the establishment of international law?

REED BRODY: Absolutely. I mean, Nuremberg is the genesis of international accountability. It’s the genesis of “never again.” It’s the first international tribunal that held state actors responsible for crimes against humanity, which talked about aggression as the supreme international crime. And in Nuremberg, she’s on the board of the Nuremberg Academy, and there’s a — in fact, one of the last times I saw Navi Pillay was in Nuremberg, where they hold these regular meetings of judges and lawyers to promote the legacy of Nuremberg and the Nuremberg Principles, which stand for this idea that no one is above the law.

And, you know, very importantly, I mean, the United States, Russia, Soviet Union, France and Great Britain were the powers that created the International Military Tribunal. And the U.S. prosecutor, Judge Jackson, said, you know, “It’s the Germans who are in front of us today, but this law has to apply to everyone.”

AMY GOODMAN: I wanted to ask you a question on a separate issue, and that is the issue of Nicaragua. We have the latest news that the United States has sent a Nicaragua torture victim back to, deported him to Nicaragua. A Nicaraguan exile who was imprisoned and tortured after protesting against the country’s government was deported by the U.S. back to Nicaragua, where he was immediately imprisoned, this past week. If you can talk about your role in investigating Nicaragua? And it’s very interesting to speak to you, given that, what, 40 years ago, you were one of the leading critics and investigators of the Contra war crime atrocities against the Sandinistas.

REED BRODY: Well, I mean, so, today, of course, Nicaragua has become a dictatorship, led by Daniel Ortega, in which, you know, there are no human rights, there is no civic space, in which 453 Nicaraguans have been stripped of their nationality, expelled. One-tenth of the Nicaraguan population has fled abroad, and many are in the United States.

AMY GOODMAN: Some of them old Sandinista leaders.

REED BRODY: Some of them old Sandinista leaders, many of them who were expelled by Nicaragua to the United States. And unfortunately, a number of them, seven of — Nicaragua once put 222 dissidents on a plane to the United States. As of today, six of those people have been in ICE detention.

And, you know, Marco Rubio, the United States considers Nicaragua to be a dictatorship. The U.S. government has coordinated international efforts to isolate Nicaragua, including a recent meeting of the Organization of American States that was devoted to Nicaragua.

And yet, what we’re seeing is that Nicaraguan dissidents are being picked up by ICE and, in this case, returned to Nicaragua, where they are rearrested. In other cases, Nicaraguans are being sent around the world. There are Nicaraguans who have been deported to the Central African Republic. A few weeks ago, one of the 222 Nicaraguans who was expelled on a plane, a leading journalist, Luis Galeano, on whose show I’ve been many times, was arrested by ICE, and still — now he’s out on bail, but he still faces deportation hearings.

AMY GOODMAN: And your title on the commission investigating Nicaragua that recently released a report?

REED BRODY: So, I’m a member — I’m a member of the United Nations Group of Human Rights Experts on Nicaragua, similar to the one that Navi Pillay was the chair of for the Occupied Palestinian Territories.

AMY GOODMAN: In which she found genocide.

REED BRODY: In which she found that Israel had been engaged in genocide.

AMY GOODMAN: I want to thank you so much for being with us, Reed Brody, war crimes prosecutor, member of the International Commission of Jurists, has served, as he said, as a member of the United Nations Group of Human Rights Experts on Nicaragua.

Coming up, we look at the ongoing fallout from Cornell University’s handling of an alleged gang rape of a Cornell undergraduate at a college fraternity house. Stay with us.

AMY GOODMAN: “Antipatriarca,” “Anti-Patriarchy,” by Ana Tijoux.
